L.title: Opening session
obj: Explain how the halaqa runs: small group, no drop-ins, four fixed segments each week.
Set the goal as staying on the path of self-purification, not reaching an end point.
Start the daily wird and the 15-day streak before anything is added to it.
Plant the first comprehension question: am I a servant of Allah, and do my days show it?
topics: Why this halaqa is small and interactive
Big halaqas leave no space to share, no follow-up and no way to track attendance. Drop-ins do not work: miss a couple of weeks and you lose the thread.
The goal and the building-block method
Topics are built brick on brick. The goal is tools to deal with life while staying close to Allah, with a lens that explains events so they do not break you.
The Prophet and the Sahaba as the model
They had no PhDs or money but mastered life's difficulties. Islam went from a small part of Arabia to three continents in about 30 years.
The spiritual drought and why people drift
People float in and out of the masjid like tides, because there is no system for keeping the fulfillment. This halaqa is meant to be that system, with what his teachers taught him.
The four segments
Comprehension, connection, rituals/acts of worship, and the weekly exercise with its discussion.
Segment 1: Comprehension
A 10 to 15 minute talk, then reflect through the week without researching. If you have no questions next week, he knows you did not really think about it.
Segment 2: Connection (the wird)

Done twice a day, together once on session day, followed by Al-Fatiha. Build the habit in any weather first. Meanings are explained only after the habit is established. The Prophet and the Sahaba always kept a wird and a portion of Quran.
The 15-day rule
After 15 straight days with no gap, tell him and more is added to the wird, including the Quran portion later.
Segment 3: Rituals, starting with salah

Perfecting salah is the main aim. Most of us only go through the motions. The Prophet found joy in salah and could not be rushed into it. You cannot will yourself to enjoy it, it is a long change of attitude.
Patience and the path

Peel the onion layers. Allah made the cosmos in six days not because He needed them. There is no end goal, only staying on the path until death. Closeness to Allah has no limit, so struggling with sincerity is a sign you are still on it.
How the sessions will flow
About an hour, with most time on how last week's exercise went and what worked. He will not spoon feed. Aside on the women's halaqa and why it runs differently.
Segment 4: The weekly exercise
Not complicated and not daily. Afterwards you discuss why you felt that way and what you realized from doing something you did not want to do.
Recap and what the Sahaba cared about

Contemplate the talk, keep the wird, add the small habit to prayer, do the exercise, note realizations. The Sahaba were preoccupied with things we no longer think about, and bringing that back will change how we think and behave.
Why the wird: discipline and the covenant

Keep it going from tomorrow morning and do not drop it. It takes about 15 minutes, doable while commuting. He ties the daily commitment to the old idea of the ahd, a covenant that unites the group on the Day of Judgment.
Comprehension 1: Tahqiq maani al-ubudiyyah
Continuously check that you are a servant of Allah. Who you are is a real existential question: people with high IQs can believe they descend from aliens.
You are an abd of Allah

Every human is a servant. Ubudiyyah shows in ritual, in serving people and in caring for creation. Ask how many times a day you evaluate it, and whether an outsider watching your day would say you identify as His servant.
Asking the question is 80% of the work
Without it everything else is a waste of time. Identity brings serenity. The nafs resists being called a servant and insists you serve it.
How change happens and closing logistics

Transformation comes from moving service from the self to Allah through the pain of tearing the whims apart one by one. He will ask next week how the reflection went. Room and timing are triple booked, so a new time is coming.
Group wird, salawat and short surahs
The wird is done together, then Fatiha, Ikhlas, Falaq and Nas are recited (Quran sections in the Arabic appendix).
How to count the wird
Have a counter with you and keep the same sequence. Ask him or the brothers if you are unclear on the wird.

L.title: Why deeds are accepted
obj: Introduce qabool al-amal: a deed can be done perfectly and still not be accepted.
Split acceptance into the mechanical side (rules) and the inner side (intention, presence, khushu).
Reframe the halaqa as the way to raise the odds that your deeds are accepted.
Give the first salah exercise: pause before you start praying.
Explain the wird mechanics and the reset rule for the 15-day streak.
topics: Acceptance of deeds (qabool al-amal)
Doing the job is not the same as getting paid. Most people never notice the gap between performing a deed and having it accepted.
Can you know your Jumuah was accepted?

The group answers: follow the rules. He separates two things: the technical side (wudu, not speaking, arriving) and the inner side. You can get every technical part right and still not swear it was accepted.
The inner side of a deed
Intention, why you did it, how close, connected and clear you were. Fiqh can be taught in one session, so the halaqa exists for the inner part, which is a lifelong journey.
The scary thought
You could do a million deeds and none be accepted. A coherent person should be worried by this, and it leads to asking what raises the odds.
What does khushu even mean?
We throw around words like being connected to Allah and khushu, but most of us only have a mental image of someone crying. We have to define it so we know what we are aiming for.
Taqabbal Allah as a reminder
Saying it to each other is a prayer for acceptance and a reminder you are not off the hook yet, so you do more to raise the odds.
Make acceptance a recurring theme
Every action, ask whether it will be accepted. Would I accept this from myself? The answer is not to stop praying, it is to ask how to improve it.
Ideas must stay alive in you
If they die, you drift back to your baseline and lose interest, however many diseases of the heart he teaches later.
Showing off rejects a deed
Riya can cancel a deed as easily as sincerity makes it. No one can judge this but you. It is a disease no doctor can cure, so you read the prescription and fix it yourself.
Q: Is reminding myself why I'm doing it enough?

You can never know a deed was accepted. If you knew, you could stop and go party. Asking the question helps, and next week's topic of niyyah addresses it. The whole journey is about raising the odds by removing diseases of the heart.
Segment 2: the wird

Done together each Friday, then twice a day alone: istighfar and salawat among them, in a set count, about 300 per sitting at the start. Start small so you do not burn out. The biggest jump is going from nothing to this.
Small and consistent beats large

The most beloved acts to Allah are the consistent ones even if small. Each wird takes 12 to 13 minutes, under half an hour a day, doable while commuting. Not up for debate when travelling, sick or in exams.
No meanings yet
He will not explain the meanings until the habit is built. Every Muslim should have a hizb. These three adhkar are the most powerful and every Sufi path starts people on them.
15 days and the plan to grow

Struggles with weekends or a broken routine should be shared. After the majority hit 15 days, small additions begin, reaching about 1500 within a year. Timing is flexible as long as it is once early and once late in the day.
Segment 3: Salah and the weekly small addition
Each week he adds something to your salah. There is no exercise this week, only a warm-up.
Exercise: pause before salah
Stop for about 15 seconds before starting. Cut the train of thought, centralize, breathe, then enter salah.
Why he gives no script
Everyone will find something different, so he will not give an example you would stick to. Whatever puts you in the zone and makes the salah meaningful is correct.
Alone versus in jamaa

Jamaa keeps quality easier. Alone, many of us rush like a 50 second record. A small weekly adjustment adds up to something meaningful over seven or eight weeks. Doing them all at the end does not work.
Salah adjustments versus exercises

Adjustments improve prayer. Exercises are social or nafs experiments. Later on, perhaps a year or two in, he will ask you to buy something you really want and give it away, to see how attached you are.
Why the exercises are artificial

The Sahaba were far less attached to the dunya and did this naturally. Our lives are self-centered. We bring these conditions in on purpose to learn about ourselves, then pull the thread of why we felt something.
The messy house analogy
People look at the inner mess and put the lid back on. It can be cleaned. Tazkiyah is learning what to remove, which is hard because in the nafs you are not sure what is healthy and what is garbage.
You understand yourself least
The only thing you fully control is you. He has no magic wand and no superiority. You walk it together with a network of people making dua.
No finish line
Skills decay without practice, like a procedure a physician stops doing. Stop improving your salah and it goes downhill.
Imam Ahmad and Shaytan
On his deathbed he said not yet, not yet. Shaytan was telling him he had escaped. He refused because feeling you escaped is vanity, which means he caught you.
What the halaqa offers

A basic comprehension of these topics without the decorations or questionable practices. Remove vanity, arrogance, showing off, envy, indifference, lust and laziness. Replace with genuineness, trustworthiness, sincerity, love and humbleness, as the Prophet had. The one who reached the angels still fell.
Rules of the 15-day streak
Miss one, make it up. Miss two in a row, reset. This is how any habit building works. After about two months it should stay for life.
A non-mandatory habit is love
You do the fard anyway. Doing something unrequested daily can only be read as love, like doing something your mother never asked for.
No evidence lecture
A full lesson on the hadith about dhikr would take an hour and a half. He will not defend every instruction with evidence. You can research it yourself.
How future sessions run
Some weeks no new comprehension piece, just discussion of how last week went. Do not sit with a poker face. Participation lets him stop spoon feeding.
Tazkiyah puts the blame back on you
People want to blame others. Tazkiyah says it is all you, and your potential is beyond what you imagine. Some exercises will resonate more than others.
Wird together
Counter reminder, then the group recites the wird and ends with Fatiha and the last short surahs (Arabic appendix).

L.title: Intention
obj: Teach tashih al-niyyah: improve the quality of your intention before you act.
Show that perfecting intention is impossible, but caring about it and honestly acknowledging a flawed one is the work.
Explain how intention changes: repeated reflection until it is second nature, and regenerating it when it fades.
Refine the wird: do it focused, without urgency, with dua after it, and fit it to the shape of your week.
topics: Wird: focus and no urgency
Once every 2 or 3 days do it somewhere you can focus. In session, cut off outside stimuli and drop the feeling of urgency, the I hate this, let's get through it feeling. Let it settle.
Dua after the wird

Make dua for yourself to keep walking the path and have deeds accepted, and for others walking it with you. The wird becomes invocation, Quran and dua together, a daily dose however chaotic the day is.
Streak rules and patience
Miss one, make it up. Miss two, reset. Not everyone gets 15 days quickly and he gives a couple of months.
Why Ikhlas, Falaq and Nas

Ikhlas is the description of Allah, your aqeedah in a surah. The Muawwidhatayn are both Quran and a dua the Prophet recited while wiping his body. Variations in the count are minor. The point is committing to something daily outside salah.
Fit it to your week
Weekends and weekdays differ, so one may work and the other fail. Keep a bird's-eye view of how you run your days instead of being slammed around.
Review of the first two ideas
Always return to ubudiyyah. Acceptance cannot be known, hope alone is not enough, so work on the actions of the heart (amal al-qalb).
Today's topic: tashih al-niyyah
In Islam why you do something matters, including in fiqh: why you bought or hold something changes the ruling on zakat or what you owe.
Be clear on your reason
Have clarity on why. Even a bad intention is better acknowledged to Allah: my intention is bad, I'm not strong enough to fix it, help me. That beats acting fine and hoping.
The story of the janazah

A scholar sat a few seconds while everyone stood for a janazah, then said he was fixing his intention. It takes a moment to know why you are going, or you may only be going so nobody says you skipped it.
Hadith qudsi: the least needy of partners
Allah leaves the deed to the other partner if you did it for Him and someone else.
Perfect intention is impossible
That is the level of prophets. For everyone else the aim is to care, always wonder what your intention is, and work to make it purer.
If you notice showing off
You still pray. Leaving a deed for others is the problem. Acknowledging that your intention was not great is half the work, and then you work harder next time. Innama al-amal bi-niyyat.
Q: group acts like Sunnah prayer

Everyone stood to pray and he followed. You are meant to doubt yourself, but before the deed, not after. Do it even when everyone is doing it. It takes a second to centralize and he does not say to repeat the prayer.
Don't be dependent on the herd
If you only do what the herd does you stop when they stop. A better intention is I stand only for You, I would not put my head down for anyone else.
Be honest: why I'm doing it versus why I should
Acknowledge the real reason and ask Allah to make it pure. He grants the pure intention. You show Him you are serious and He holds it back until you do.
There is no switch
Change comes from frequent reflection and adjustment. He compares it to a doctor staring at the same lung scan every day for years until the patterns become clear.
Internalize the first four topics daily
Am I a servant? Is my deed accepted? Is my intention right? You will find a lot of what you do is not for the right reason. Sensitivity rises: old struggles ease and new ones appear.
Comprehension takes a week of thought
Humans stopped deep thinking. He has no fix and his wand is broken. Slow change is the point, and wanting instant results is something Tazkiyah teaches you to drop.
Q&A: friends all start praying, what do I say?
The group answers. He agrees: take a second, say Ya Rabbi, forgive me, this is for You, alhamdulillah I have good people reminding me. It is just a moment of talking to Allah, not crazy.
Applying niyyah to study and career

Seeking knowledge needs an intention you have worked out: what does for the sake of Allah mean? A doctor who goes in for money tires of patients, one who goes in to help treats people better. Non-Muslims can have good intentions too.
Q: doesn't intention turn into habit and lose substance?
His view: we do not internalize it often enough and it drops, we just recline on the habit. Like a parent working for a sick child, the reason must be clear every day.
Regenerate and keep honest
Intentions can rust, so regenerate them. A general umbrella intention of for Allah does not help the heart. Pause and ask why before everything. Honesty with yourself is what allows change.
Intention is a life plan
Study for the sake of Allah is a whole life story to think through repeatedly until it is who you are.
Q: money as an intention
Yes. You can stack several intentions, such as not begging, caring for family and helping people. The common denominator is submission to Allah.
Q: sports and leisure

Say the body is an amanah and sport keeps you happy and working harder. Leisure is part of obedience when you actually enjoy it, not when it makes you rage. Leisure is therapeutic and Allah commands self-care, mental included.
If your intention was mixed
If you notice showing off while playing, don't stop, acknowledge it, do istighfar and think it through. Sport is more complex than rituals, so start with acts of worship.
Student: this is really hard
He returns to the messy room. You want to close the door and walk away. Open it. It is Allah who fixes it. He wants to see you care and keep at it, even for 60 years.
Repentance later
A few weeks away, with some caveats about it.
Story: delaying marriage over intention
He waited a year to be sure of the right intention for having a child: raising someone to love Allah is worship. Nine months after marriage his son was born. Everyone struggles with different things.
It is a process, not an action
Make mistakes, come back, ask. Understand why the wrong intentions are wrong. There is no fatwa in niyyah. Not all showing off is wrong, such as in sports, but check whether the reason was pure.
You already know the answer
You ask because the nafs wants less work. You do not really need a teacher, you need to face your nafs. The work continues forever and you have to be okay with that.
Wrong reasons backfire
He says it backfires 100% and can bring sin in some cases.
Salah pause follow-up
Keep doing last week's pause. He will not assign something new every week.

L.title: Excellence in relationships
obj: Finish the four core comprehension ideas with the fourth: ihsan, the third part of the religion.
Show where tazkiyah fits: Islam is practice, iman is belief, ihsan is the relationship and attitude.
Frame the relationship with Allah as one you must work on, with expectations to think through.
Turn the four ideas from thoughts into values by daily contemplation, then pause comprehension and move to rituals and exercises.
topics: Schedule and pace
The halaqa moves to after Isha. The early group was overwhelmed because he covered too much, so this group goes slower and may not cover all four segments each week.
Recap of the first three ideas

Ubudiyyah (keep assessing your service), qabul al-amal (acceptance is unknown) and tashih al-niyyah (improve your intention). These four must stay in the background of your mind, however you personally internalize things.
Fiqh gives the rules, not the attitude
Fiqh lists the pillars and conditions of salah. It does not say what attitude to carry. Tazkiyah is about attitude, and that needs a few clear concepts.
Idea 4: Ihsan
Ilm al-tazkiyah is also called ilm al-ihsan. It comes from the hadith of Jibril: Islam, then iman, then ihsan.
Three parts, not two
Islam covers practice and iman covers belief. People assume that is all. Ihsan is the third piece and it is not obvious up front.
Worship as if you see Him

He explains ihsan as a connection so strong that only physical sight is missing, which is not possible in this life. You get there through excellence at the relationship, and salah, fasting and Quran are the tools.
The reward is seeing Him
Looking at the face of Allah is the biggest reward in Jannah. Everything else means little to someone who does not understand what they are here for.
Why he put this last
It is not an add-on to the curriculum. It is one of three sections of the religion, and the quality of your relationship with Allah has to be something you are working to improve.
We do not have to see Him
Seeing Him may not even be possible, and trying to limit Him to what we want risks misunderstanding who He is. There is a distance between our expectations and the reality of this relationship.
The three are worked on together
Islam, iman and ihsan are not sequential. You do not finish salah and fasting first and then learn ihsan.
Why ihsan was left out
It is not systematically taught like prayer, fasting and zakat. You cannot give what you do not have, so parents and communities cannot pass it on if they never received it.
Institutions without tazkiyah
If committees and boards have jealousy and power control, there is no difference from any other company. People with tazkiyah walk in wanting only to serve and ask how they can serve better.
Questioning your intention in every setting
Before you say something, criticize someone or point out a mistake, ask whether the intention is right. People who do this are sensitive and careful with other people's feelings.
Four bricks, and a full third of Islam
These are starting points, not everything. Ihsan is a full third of the faith, working simultaneously with the other two.
Ihsan in everything, even slaughtering
Allah decreed ihsan in everything, so sharpen the blade and spare the animal pain. Even that is done knowing Allah sees you.
Ideas, not lectures
He gives ideas to go and look up, not full lectures.
Three ways to divide the faith

Horizontal: practice, belief, spirituality, which is what he teaches. Vertical: Muslim, mumin, muhsin by degree of commitment, as in the Quran verse where the Bedouin said we believe and were told to say we have submitted. Circular comes later.
Ihsan as an ideal, not a goal
You can never be perfect, but it is a standard you aspire to. Excellence here means building the relationship.
A relationship unlike any other

Relationships decide whether we are happy or miserable and they take work. Name another relationship with something you cannot see, hear, touch or smell. His message to you predates you and is not verbal, so you must learn to read signs.
Your first feeling should be confusion
I have no idea what to do with this. Good, start there. You do not know how to hold a relationship with a human, and now it is with Allah.
Offer your best and He offers His
Act as if you see Him and He is there at all times. Think of duas answered years later and subtle messages through your life. People lose the opportunity because they are not reading them.
What do you expect from Him, and He from you?
Marriages fail from unclear expectations. Have you thought about what you expect from Allah and what He expects from you? Ask your nafs, because you may find you give little and expect a lot.
Is the reward of ihsan anything but ihsan?
Show Him your best and He shows you His. We are not meant to be waiting for something, but we are, so tease that out.
Q: isn't expecting something wrong?
A student pushes back. He agrees it is a good point. Maybe expectation is the wrong word, but unreasonable expectations ruin any relationship, so examine yours.
Pausing the comprehension piece
The next sessions turn to rituals and exercises, then return to build on these four.
How often to ask each question
Ubudiyyah multiple times a day. Qabul at least once a day with one ritual, eventually after every ritual. Niyyah nearly all the time. Ihsan as an ongoing background thought.
The missing third pillar
A house on two pillars does not stand. Establish the third and you know what you are working toward. It does not make you perfect.
Internalize: thoughts into values
We know death is coming, but how real is it to you? A thought you turn into a value becomes second nature and you respond to it automatically.
Examples: working out, and a child
Everyone agrees you should work out but some people internalize it. Reinforcement takes months, like telling a child every day not to hit his sister. If you give up, the harm comes back on you.
Find your values from your life
Look at your habits and routines to see what your values are and where they came from. Notice what you wish was a value but is not yet, and what you wish was not.
If you don't care about intention
Even when you think about niyyah you may get it right only about 10% of the time, so few deeds qualify. This is why you contemplate and turn it into a value.
Don't be overwhelmed
It is not meant to feel impossible. Step by step, slowly, differences come with time.
Q: should you reflect on deeds after?
Yes, good and bad. Good deeds lead you to hamd and bad ones lead you to tawbah. How you view the deed afterward matters.
Everything falls under ihsan
Ilm al-ihsan is the more authentic name, tazkiyah is the Quranic one. The sequence he teaches is not divine, it comes from scholars.

L.title: Ithar and service
obj: Review the ithar exercise (letting others go first and finish speaking) and the pause before salah.
Teach that tazkiyah starts with noticing what the nafs is doing, then controlling it, not destroying it.
Show how to find the root cause: be sensitive first, then reflect deeply in a set time.
Assign a new exercise: repeat an act of service you hate until it stops bothering you.
topics: Group answers on the last exercise
People noticed the urge to take the floor in conversation and to cut ahead while walking. One noticed it only after the fact.
Noticing earlier
The more you work on it, the sooner you catch it, and you become enjoyable to be around and chivalrous. This applies beyond interactions.
Q: how is letting someone finish connected to tazkiyah?

The nafs likes to hear itself talk. His two-year-old pushes his five-year-old out of the way when she tells her day. The urge to interrupt or prepare a reply is the nafs. Notice it, acknowledge it, recognize it, then control it. Over time the nafs learns to wait.
Upbringing helps, but this is holistic
Some people were raised with it. The aim is noticing the inside, then deciding what to change by Islamic values.
Talk to yourself, and why the nafs is there

Ask why you are entertaining a thought. Surat ash-Shams, aflaha man zakkaha: the verb is used with both male and female forms, hinting at two within you. The nafs is needed for survival and confidence, so you control it, you do not destroy it.
From not noticing to no longer having the urge
Not a jump. First you notice late, then earlier, then you mostly avoid it, then it stops being an issue. Same slow growth applies to every part of life.
Luck of upbringing versus working on it
Predisposition and environment are rolling dice. There is a way to find clarity and elevate yourself.
Student: why am I rushing?
Find the root. Driving like a maniac saves 35 seconds on a 20 minute drive. What is my problem? Do the soul searching and dig past the layers of the onion.
Start with sensitivity
You cannot treat a disease you do not acknowledge, like a patient who says the tumor is nothing. Feel the unhealthy feeling up front and do not let it slide.
Q: should I constantly ask why?

No. Constant superficial asking makes you stop caring. In daily life just notice the urge and keep sensitivity high. Then sit for deep reflection, around half an hour, and build a sentence that explains why it is wrong and how to be better. Reinforce it until it burns in.
Follow-up: pause before salah

One person found it helped for the first two times and then he drifted back to bad habits. He says that is fine, you are starting to notice, and noticing is how healing starts. He is not trying to make you feel bad.
Al-Ghazali's start
He noticed he was thinking about fiqh and aqeedah in salah and asked whether he should be. That question started his path and led to the Ihya. Naming a feeling helps you work on it.
Q: one thought in salah?
Fine to start with one. Salah has stations with different things to say and do, so you must move between thoughts. He will walk through what each posture is for another time.
Why the pause matters
It breaks the chain of thoughts so they do not enter salah. Some scholars imagined it was their last prayer with Jannah and Jahannam around, and their color changed from fear and reverence.
Salah as a daily break

As a physician in clinic he gets problem after problem. He clears loose ends before salah and writes the rest on a sticky note. Salah becomes something you look forward to, a mandatory break. Carrying calm into dua is better, but do not drift into planning.
Recap of the four ideas
Assess your service, think about acceptance, work on intention, and treat ihsan as the third pillar. Admit honestly that your intention is bad before each act, and start there.
New exercise: an act of service you hate
Think of an action you hate that contains some service. Keep doing it until you stop hating it. It was a big headache with the women's group.
Examples and rules

Dishes in the evening, teaching a sibling math, taking out the garbage. It must be repetitive, for someone else, and honest. Running or showering are not service. The point is that the hate is a perception of the nafs, not real. He is not asking you to love it.
His own example

At 16 he was told to walk his sister to school though he hated it. He stopped hating it and built a close relationship with her. He realized it was selfishness. Perks appear when you stop focusing on the hate.
Q: hate is too strong
Fine, replace it with I do not want to. The shift from not wanting it to being unbothered is real. The nafs dislikes the word service because it is a servant.
Student's example that backfired

He picks up a brother for the masjid and argued with himself that it is good for me, and he disliked it more. Repeating the argument is not working. Flip it so it is your responsibility, and ask why you actually hate it, then find a solution. Do not dig the root cause yet.
More examples
Visiting someone who does not like you or treats you badly.
The mother-in-law story

A woman buys poison to kill her mother-in-law, rubs it on her back daily. After 25 days she loves her and begs for an antidote. It was olive oil. Doing a nice act changes the relationship and your nafs.
A brother's phone call
He called a relative daily that he disliked. In the first days it was tiring and then he said he loved the person and they get along.
What the goal is
Reaching I am content with offering this, no more. Not to love it, and not to make you great at dishes.
Q and answers
Some examples are time management or self-discipline, which come later. A silly example works, like always getting the group's drinks. Gym and practice are not service.
If you hate serving you are in trouble
You are a servant. If you do not enjoy serving, the whole plan fails. This is why ubudiyyah comes first.
Keep it simple and reach out
Small, silly ones are best. They give you reference points for later.

L.title: Consistency under stress
obj: Explain what the wird is for: learning to commit to something optional and be consistent, before focus or meaning.
Teach centralizing: being present in this moment instead of living in the future.
Train the wird as practice for salah, including slowing the heart rate and finding your attention span.
Review the ithar and hated-service exercises and introduce expectations of yourself and of others.
topics: Consistency has a precedent
The Prophet taught the Sahaba a portion of Quran daily, made up the next day if missed, plus invocation. The goal here is learning to commit to something you do not have to do.
The amount and the value
The most beloved acts are consistent ones, even small. 300 and 300 is about 12 to 15 minutes. The value is the commitment and holding yourself to a standard, with dua at the end.
Difficulties with consistency
Weekends are harder because weekday routines give flow. You must plan, like for a day of travel. For the first year he will not ask for focus or understanding of the words.
Fatima and Ali's tasbih
When they asked for a servant the Prophet gave them tasbih instead. Ali said he never missed it, not even the night of Siffin.
Discipline first, focus later
Zero to 600 is the biggest jump in the halaqa. After that you add 100 here and there. If you break the streak, come back again.
Do not rush it
Doing it all at once at the end of the day is not wrong, but it is not the point. The nafs wants to jump to the next thing. Together you slow down, and that is valuable in itself.
Giving up control of the timing
Someone leads and you follow, like the imam. If you only got 80, it does not matter. You do not need to finish your count when he moves on. This makes it less to worry about.
Centralize: living in the present
People live in the future, 10 minutes or a year ahead, a mirage. No one stresses about the past, only what will come from it. This moment is all you have.
Being in the moment
It is not about focusing on the words but being present without the anxiety of wanting to move on. Most people cannot do it, and your tics show where you are uncomfortable.
Build slowly over years

Within two or three years you have a reasonable amount of awrad that does not hurt. Anyone who starts with 2000 tasbih a day fails within a week, a universal law. Like a plane, there is a moment the wheels leave the ground.
How to do it in session
Turn toward the table, sit comfortably, silence your phone unless on call, do not lean on a wall unless you have a medical reason. Use a counter or beads. Eyes closed is fine.
Why 10 to 15 minutes of focus
If you can centralize in a group, you can do it at Hajj among two million people. Do not itch to leave. The nafs will eventually give in.
Counting at home versus here
Here, follow him. At home, count, since it gives a sense of achievement. Later you may move to invocation without counting.
Group wird
Recited together with salawat and the short surahs (Arabic appendix).
Debrief: when did you get fidgety?
That point is your attention span for something you do not define as fun, play or joy. Anything you find joyful is easy to focus on.
Turning it into joy

Start with maybe three minutes, then slowly extend. At some point it becomes joy, like playing a game when you are not fidgety. He cannot train you inside salah, but he can here. If you fail the wird it is no big deal.
Transfer to salah
The ability moves to salah slowly. Breathe and say Allah slowly two or three times to lower your heart rate, because your tongue and mind match it. Scholars discussed this around 1100 years ago.
Anxiety shows up in the body

An anxious person moves. He had a tic at 17 and his father held his hand. Living in four futures at once leaves stress in the body. There is overlap with anxiety in the DSM-5, though this is not psychiatry.
Practice alone every 2 or 3 days
Do it somewhere quiet, with wudu, toward the qibla, no deadline. It calms the heart rate and helps on the spot more than anything else he teaches.
Managing stress is life
How you manage stress matters. He gained about 18 kilos after leaving Syria. The wird forces calm, but it is not a hocus pocus fix. When it is hard you ask why.
What is in the wird
Istighfar, with the intention not to return to the sin. Salawat, with the hadith of Ubayy where Allah takes care of your worries. Tawhid, Fatiha, Ikhlas three times, and the Muawwidhatayn.
Dua shows you what you want

What you ask for reveals what bothers or excites you, your priority list. If you ask and do not work toward it, you are lying to yourself. Example: someone asked to memorize Quran but never opened it, and it was really about honoring his parents.
Q: dua against qadr
If it is going to happen you ease it for yourself and others and support people.
Review of two exercises
Ithar (let someone take what your nafs fights for) trains sensitivity to nafs urges. The hated service exercise shows the nafs can stop hating something with some mental massaging.
Expectations as a trick

One person found that deciding the day before that he would drive her the whole week made him not mind. Pin the word expectation: marriages, work and friendships need proper expectations, and Allah also has expectations of you.
A week is not enough
Years may be needed to change a likes or dislikes pattern, especially one you indulged. Enjoying it takes longer. Content is the target.
More examples
Sleeping early until he loved it was a great example of changing a feeling, though not service. Cleaning a bathroom. Picking up others' slack.
First rule of the halaqa
I do not care what other people do or learn from you. This is the one time to be selfish and focus on your improvement. Exceptions for raising a child.
Expectations and your role
If staff get used to coming late, a 9am start upsets them. If you tell yourself I do not do this it is an uphill fight. Set your own role.
A trick that is fine
Doing something you dislike while watching something relaxing is a good adjustment. Most people never observe how they make things easier.
Free happiness
When you expect more of yourself you are pleasantly surprised and do more. People who expect very little of themselves are hardest to fix.
Raise your expectations slowly

Raise them gradually or you crash within weeks. The wird twice a day is an expectation you set for yourself, and feeling guilty when you miss it is a good thing. His clinic example: expect to see all three patients and you are happy when someone takes one.
No new exercise until both are done
Adding without doing the previous one wastes everyone's time. His shaykh asked each student one by one. The observations are golden. Know your strategies so you can protect them.

L.title: Time and value
obj: Explain why the wird is easier on the run (dead time) and harder when sat down: the action is not valued.
Teach that you assign a value to everything, and your real priority list is what you actually do.
Set the exercise: build your priority list and place the wird in it.
Show how people lie to themselves, and that opening the inner cellar and being honest is 80% of the work.
topics: Sitting versus on the run
Some found the wird easier when sitting and thinking about the words. Others found it easier while walking or driving.
Dead time versus valued time

On a walk or train you have nothing else to do, so you fill dead time. At home it is not dead time and you want to get on with the next thing. This is a psychology finding: people avoiding an essay will write it on a six hour train.
The reason: you do not see the action as valuable
The action does not deserve your time, so you only do it when nothing else competes. Music listeners hit the same issue. Either change the time or change the action.
Student: easier at Fajr
Doing it before your brain starts demanding the day is easier. The quietest time of the day.
Car is the only quiet time
Salah is like a checkpoint: stop, calm down, come back slowly. Carve out time once or twice a week outside driving, planned so you are not preoccupied, tired or rushed.
Know your own pattern
We are creatures of habit and someone watching you for a week could predict your days. Observe yourself and you will see when you sin and when you are at your best.
Where to put it
Anywhere quiet, even next to a wall at a loud place, 10 to 15 minutes. He prefers one early and one after Isha. Not mandated.
Q: I feel I'm wasting time
Keep the tongue moving even if the heart is not there. Do not kill the part that works. Notice what works where and ask why.
Two ways to fix it
Change your view of the action (make it valuable) or your view of the time (see it as dead). The first is easier. The second requires scheduling the whole day.
Goal: sit once or twice a week
The rest of the week on the run is fine. Eventually you do the main one in a focused session and do other things on the run. He does muraja'a and Quran on the run.
Why dead time feels serene
Because you hate that time anyway, anything done in it is a plus. Salah is hard because it cannot be done on the run, so treat the wird as a mini salah experience.
Your expectation of the time decides the feeling
Same time, same action, different mood depending on what you thought you would do.
Breakfast versus the wird
Breakfast takes the same ten minutes and the nafs enjoys it. Many people find more joy in fasting because the soul is nourished too. The blockades are what we are tearing down.
We avoid asking why
Answering means we have to change something we like and hold ourselves to a standard. We say later, but there is no later. Failing many times is fine. Taking out the white flag is when you lose.
Student: giving up sleep
Waking earlier became easier over time once he accepted giving up what he liked.
Priority list
To make something valuable ask what your priorities are. Where does this action sit on the list? Sequence it after one, two and three. Reflect on what the value is to you.
You value everything
You are assigning every thing a number and deciding on a scale. With optional acts, obligating yourself needs paperwork inside.
You are never too busy
He removed the value of sports a decade ago and does not lie about it. You are never too busy for what matters, only for what does not. Too busy means you did not make the cut.
Honesty gives hope
Not going to the gym is a conscious decision. Being honest lets you move it up the list. Class over the wird is a correct priority.
Q: why do I like the wird in the car but not prioritize it?
The car is dead time. Would you take a three second teleport? Anything of value in zero-value time is a plus, even priority 20. He agrees you may be fooling yourself that you like the action.
Find a reasonable place
Not number one, just a place where after one, two and three you can sit and do it in not-dead time.
We lie masterfully
And we swear our lies to Allah. Self-accounting is the goal. Honesty is like a warm shower and it makes you free.
Q: what if it has compounded for 15 years?
The nafs fortifies it with layers like a castle wall. It was simple at 10. You have to live with yourself and you evolve from ignoring to lying.
Example: lowering the gaze

Why do so many people look at women on the street? For many the real reason is they do not believe it is haram. The problem is the belief, so solutions elsewhere miss. Same with alcohol and many behaviors.
The cellar of real beliefs
The nafs projects one belief while another sits underneath. Nobody thinks they are evil. Open the cellar and look.
The wird has no number yet
It sits on the shelf without a number. Say it is important, but you have not gone to that secret place and given it a proper spot.
Student: I've read this in psychology books

Why do we know it but not follow it? He tells them to think about it. A student says we need a Western source. He answers that trusting what Allah says is a different standard and takes time to build.
First step: what am I lying about?
Do not hurry to change. Recognize first. It is easier for others to see than for you to see yourself.
Back to the wird
Open the cellar door. What do I actually feel toward this? What should I feel? Are my feelings justified? Build the sentence and a priority number will form.
Things to do first
Pages, patients, an obligatory prayer time, those come first and that is correct.
This week's exercise
Assign a value to the wird. A student asks him to explain the benefits. He refuses to spoon feed, saying you should know why: tasbih, Quran and dua twice a day builds a habit.
What you give an infinite number
Someone gave money an infinite value. Allah will test what matters most to you. Either you realize and let go or you make a devastating mistake.
Q: should I write the list?
A draft is a good start, or just contemplate. Your real list is what you do. Make three lists: the ideal, the reality, and the one you claim.
Seeing, believing, internalizing
They are three different processes. Allah says it is the most important thing and we shelve it.
Student method
He writes down the excuses his inner self makes that do not match his goal.
80% is recognizing
Step back, recognize it, acknowledge it and hold on to that new honesty. It gets harder the older you are because you want to believe you figured it out.
How old halaqas worked
Miss once and you are out. You sat, listened and did what they said, and trusted it works. He was kicked out once and had to beg into another.
Why not argue back
Defending your position is the opposite of tazkiyah. Put yourself in cross-examination, a lawyer with all your records, and rip yourself apart privately.
Tazkiyah is a path
Not an accomplishment or a moment of figuring things out. Everyone is at a different point.

L.title: Love for the sake of Allah
obj: Recap the four basics (knowing your state, perfecting your deed, fixing intention, wondering about acceptance) as a firewall you keep in the back of your mind.
Lay out the roadmap: comprehension (hub/love, tawadu'/humility, rahma/mercy), then connection (the wird stays as is), then small salah improvements.
Teach that love is the ultimate long-term motive, and that loving what you cannot see is hard, so you start by loving the Prophet, the Quran and the people who love Allah.
Teach how to reflect (run scenarios, ask questions) and the difference from overthinking.
Set the exercise: make dua for someone you envy or dislike.
topics: The four basics as a firewall
Keep them like a bulletin board in your mind. Thinking about your intention stops you walking into something wrong. Wondering if it is accepted keeps you humble and pushing.
There is always a spiritual side
Children just act and move on. You should remember that servitude to Allah is the point of life.
The second layer: hub, tawadu', rahma
Love, humility, mercy. Like building a castle, the lower four must be stable first or the upper layer cannot be carried.
Plan and pacing
Each of the three takes weeks. Humility takes longest because you need many other ideas cleared before it means anything. Mercy is simpler but equally important.
The wird stays as is for now
He will add things outside the wird before asking you to add to it. Report back after 15 days, then a month. Doing it at home was to learn how you value your time.
Salah in small increments
Baby steps before and during salah. Either all at once or one a week, depending on how people respond. Each practice is to discover something about yourself.
The whole path is rooted in love
Love is the only motive that lasts. Greed, anger, envy and competition work short term. Even fear alone or hope of reward alone does not last.
Hate is love aimed the other way
The same energy targeted at something not good. Hope is the crystal in the laser: without it nothing functions.
Loving what you cannot sense is hard
You have only ever loved what your senses could reach. Nodding means you did not understand the request. Even loving a grandparent you never met is difficult.
Easier to love the Prophet than Allah
Said so you know you are not alone. You can picture him, his stories, his walk. That love opens the door to Allah.
Start with the Quran and people of Allah
Love the Quran and people who love Allah, and they open the door. It is fine to admit you do not know what loving Allah means yet.
Knowing Allah, accepting life as given
Loving Allah includes knowing Him, seeing the world through that lens and accepting what you were given and what was taken. It is all in the Quran.
How to reflect (tafakkur)
Most students have no idea what to do when told to reflect. Set weekly times for deep reflection on what matters or bothers you.
Before electricity and radio
Humans once had only the sky and their thoughts. Today distraction means we avoid depth because it surfaces what we do not want to know.
Technique: run scenarios

Take a topic and run long examples to the end, like when you fight someone and rehearse responses. Do the same with values: what if I do not do this, what if I do it well, what holds me back? Ten to fifteen minutes a day.
Why the early generation talked less
The Prophet made sure fundamentals were internalized, so they lived them. Aim for them to be like oxygen.
Ask real questions
If I am to love Allah is that a feeling? How do I feel for what I cannot reach? Is it possible? How did others do it?
Overthinking versus deep thought
Overthinking adds irrational thoughts or repeats the same thought with no tweak. Repeating means something is missing, a loophole or anxiety. Real thought ends in a conclusion.
Define what hub means to you
It is a huge word and what you picture at your age is not what is offered. Is it purely a feeling or more?
Verse in Surah at-Tawbah (9:24)

If fathers, sons, brothers, spouses, tribe, wealth, trade and homes are more beloved than Allah, His Messenger and striving, then wait. These loves are normal, but trouble starts when they outrank Him.
Love is not one simple thing
Love for mother, child, spouse, friend differ. Find the common denominator and what it leads to.
What does for the sake of Allah mean?
Students offer: because He rewards, a reflection of His creation. He keeps pressing: what do those words mean to you? Love for different people is unequal, so how is it all for Allah?
Benefits of understanding love
Helps tazkiyah and also your family life. You can at least admit when you are emotionally absent or dry.
Reading versus reflecting
Reading is needed but leave time for your processor to work. Reflection plateaus, and that is where ilm and teachers come in.
A conclusion that has not gone down
If a conclusion does not change you, it is still floating on the surface of the ocean. The nafs bureaucracy is heavy and sends things down slowly.
Claiming love of people for Allah without loving Allah
If you do not understand loving Allah, what have you built on it?
A student: no other reason than loving Allah
Good for staying humble, but he asks you to think there may be other reasons. Mixed intentions risk not being accepted. Reward-seeking, reputation, feeling good all fade, then you stop.
Fear and hope of reward are not wrong
Valid intentions, but love is the infinite fuel for the long run.
Hope is the elixir
All the diseases of the heart get washed out by love. People in love talk about the beloved, do things for them and know why they are here.
Does love go up and down like iman?
Iman changes because iman is internalizing, and the nafs fights back. Hope lets it keep growing. Your sensitivity rises so what you called sin gets noticed.
Acknowledgement keeps you safe
You will never perfect it, but the moment you stop caring is the danger. Tazkiyah is a path, not an accomplishment.
How do you know you reached love?
Love is hard to miss. True love of Allah brings humility, compassion, self-accountability, not vanity.
Different ways people show love
Define love of Allah. Part is emotion, but the proof is following the Prophet (3:31), not inventing what He never asked.
Love for people as His creation
Even when you dislike them you love the One who made them. That buffer lets rahma and tawadu' exist.
Love of Allah and oppressors
It does not lead you to love oppressors but to act differently.
Top down and bottom up
If you love Him, right actions flow. If not, learn the right actions from the bottom up. Both are being done here.
Reflection returns each cycle
Hope for four or five weeks, then tawadu' or rahma, then return as your capacity grows. Reflection is not wrapped up in one or two sessions.
No limit to closeness
Having a checkpoint that questions your motives is healthy. Is the feeling there? If not why, how to jumpstart it, do you need it?
The exercise: dua for someone you envy or dislike
Not oppressors. Someone who shrugged you off, mistreated you or left a bad taste. Last time was a disaster as no one did it. Struggle with it and report back.
What if I cannot think of anyone?
There is always someone who misjudged or mistreated you. The extreme person is not the target. He will not say what to ask for in the dua, that is the point.

L.title: Love and how we judge people
obj: Debrief the dua-for-someone-you-dislike exercise: what people felt, where it got hard and why.
Teach humanizing the person: bad assumptions, dehumanizing, and seeing that neither 'pure evil' nor 'worst day of their life' is probably true.
Teach that when you cannot make dua for someone, the problem is in you, not them (envy, value derived from a trait, the nafs as protector).
Cover hasad (envy) practically: what it does, how to protect yourself, and why you should not put your blessings on display.
Set the next exercise: write the priority lists (ideal versus real) and keep the wird sitting once or twice a week.
Explain why we do the wird (love talks about the beloved) and teach the hadith of drawing near through nawafil (the wali hadith).
topics: Housekeeping: where the exercises are
He confuses which exercise was assigned when. Priority list is to be done today, dua for others was last.
Priority lists recap
There are different lists: the one projected to the world, the one you tell yourself and the real one. He asked for the wird at a specific time to show you do not value it yet.
Debrief: dua for the disliked person
A general dua feels okay. Extending it into detail becomes hard. People notice they want it for themselves first.
The urge to limit the dua
Typical thought: I will give him but not more than me. In dua you do not limit what Allah gives. Ask good for them and for yourself too.
A student: it got easier with repetition
Over time he moved to details like a good spouse and family.
I said it but did not mean it
One student made detailed dua without meaning a word. That is a mechanism for distancing from what you say. How do you get from not meaning it to opening the heart?
Piling on reasons does not solve it
Telling yourself it benefits you or Allah rewards you works but does not address the problem. You need to humanize the person.
Ask why you dislike them
What happened? Identify their mistake. Then ask what the mistake has to do with you being unable to wish them good. Ask why the two are connected.
Do not accept maxims
If you do not like them you do not pray for them. Why are these linked? Answers: they do not deserve it, I do not want them to have good because they hurt me.
What did we just do? Assumptions
The group made assumptions and judgments. A single act summarizes them as evil. You would not accept that being done to you.
Dehumanizing
You take away their humanity: they are all bad, raised badly. They probably did not even notice you or had a bad day.
Assumptions are central to humility
Tawadu' requires understanding assumptions. We judge fast when we dislike and fall in love fast when we like, and marriages fail on painted pictures.
Example: the club debate
Someone said something uncalled for. Try imagining the opposite: it was the worst day of their life. Neither picture is probably true, but the second brings rahma and forgiveness.
When bad assumptions are allowed
When you are responsible for protecting others, like a father screening a suitor or someone running a kindergarten.
Why the nafs assumes the worst
It sees everything through survival and is your champion. One harm and the person is the devil. Teach it: I am not in danger.
The envy version
Same idea but different. A student assumed the envied person has no problems. That is another assumption. The truth is in the middle: good days and bad days.
Why does it bother you that someone is better?
Because you derive value from a trait or action. When someone beats you at it you feel threatened. Value derivation will return in later lessons.
Hasad turns into action
Not radio waves. It goes from thoughts to words to suspicions to harming them in front of someone who matters.
Hasad versus the evil eye (ayn)
Ayn is different, metaphysical. You cannot prove it, correlation is not evidence. If suspected, protect yourself.
Practical protection from envy
Do not display what you have to those who lack it. Be careful what you show at home. Ease the heart of a person you suspect envies you, for example by complimenting them.
Zina and public display
Do not put your lifestyle on public display unless it is gratitude to Allah or service. Ask honestly why you need people to know.
Two takeaways
One: humanize the person and notice bad assumptions. Two: when you cannot make dua for someone, the problem is with you.
Story: the ACL injury

A teammate in a second division match went for his leg, not the ball. Three surgeries, never played again. He carried it for years, finally made dua, and now they are close friends. The man never knew.
Why we judge others by intent but ourselves by accident
When you hurt someone you say I did not mean it. Others must be malicious.
The grudge burns only you
It does not hurt them. Why carry it? Get rid of it. Do your own digging into why it occurs.
A student: what if it repeats?
He prompts them to look for a non-evil explanation. If you find one you will not hold it.
Rule of tazkiyah: it is about you
Do not project on others. People will walk their path. The more you focus on yours the less you hold on to others.
Oppression is separate
Do not mix personal feelings with a real wrong. A judge must separate. The one who insulted you does not get a worse sentence.
Apologize even if you were wronged
If someone may have taken it the wrong way say sorry. They may accept or not. You do it for your ethics.
Try the exercise again
Aim to make a full dua without limits and see if the discomfort drops. It is hard and painful, you are climbing your own hill. They do not even know.
Wird update
If you did 15 days in a row, tell him. After about six months everyone should do it twice a day. The weekly sitting is only to show you its value.
Next exercise: priority lists
Write the ideal list and the real list by watching your own day for three or four days. Give the wird a number, not high, just high enough to do it.
Three lists
The public list, the one you tell yourself, the real one. Open the cellar door to see the real one.
Claiming versus internalizing
Iman goes up and down by how much you internalize. You are okay with dead time but not real time, showing your priority.
Why we do the wird: love
People in love talk about the beloved. Saying His name and the Prophet's name should bring joy. If you do not feel it yet, that is why we practice.
Allah loved first
He started the story of love before you knew. Define love or you fall out of it when life gets hard.
Hadith: nearness through faraid and nawafil
My servant draws near to Me with nothing more beloved than what I made obligatory. Then keeps drawing near with extra deeds until I love him (hadith qudsi, Bukhari).
The wird is a miniature salah
It contains the invocations, Quran and dua found in salah. You cannot be corrected inside salah, so you learn through the wird.
When I love him, I am his hearing and sight
He hears, sees, strikes and walks through Me. If he asks I give, if he seeks refuge I protect.
Hadith: drawing near by a span, an arm, running
Whoever draws a hand span, I draw an arm. Whoever comes walking, I come running. Figurative language, not measurements.
Reassurance
He does love you and has already shown you.

L.title: Culture
obj: Explain that tazkiyah has no stages or levels, and why earlier attempts to turn it into a ranked system failed.
Explain why this halaqa is run open, with questions, instead of the old silent-listening method.
Teach that culture drives behavior and that this group is a pioneer generation building one.
Show the difference between a culture embedded in Islamic values and borrowed social habits.
Explain why comprehension must come before practicing humility, love or service.
topics: No stages in tazkiyah
You may start new practices but there is no stage A or level 2. It is a journey, not an accomplishment.
History of failed attempts
Like fiqh and hadith, we see only the end product. Many attempts failed. Those who made tazkiyah accomplishment driven became vain, lazy, status seekers and built hierarchies.
Do not judge where others are
Your job is to walk your path and help others on theirs. No comparison on the Day of Judgement.
Competition as service
Be more beneficial to others than they are to you. You want them ahead so you can benefit from them. Someone always one step behind you is no use to you.
Why he allows questions
A student asks why this halaqa takes questions when his own teacher allowed none. Different audience, mentality and culture.
The Western context
There is no embedded culture of respect for knowledge here. If people are not treated as they expect they will not return and he would be left with a handful.
The goal decides the method
The aim is the same as his teachers: bring people closer to Allah. The method has to be adapted. He admits it is harder than how he was taught.
Tweak the method, not the goal
He was unsure how to convert what he was taught into an open model. It does not take anything away.
What culture is
Mentality, attitude, practices, morals: a culture of humility, love, service, respect. Once present, newcomers pick it up.
People leave over interactions, not cultures
Most stop coming because of a bad interaction.
His son and the older cohort
A son will not follow an old grey guy. He follows people seven to ten years older. That becomes his norm.
The Prophet established a culture
Different places in the Muslim world have one. We are new and do not have it yet.
How long does a culture shift take?
He asked scholars and none had done it. His guess is half a decade to a decade.
You are the dictators of the next generation
They will not do what I say, they will do what we do. The sum of the group's humility and hate is what the next generation walks into.
The Prophet changed the culture
He opened hearts. People looked past race, color and geography and saw a person.
Hospitality as culture

Knock on a Muslim door and the guest is treated like a king. Here people talk to you at the door for hours and never invite you in. Islamic values that are tightly embedded survive, loosely embedded ones were lost.
Younger generation goal
They study, attend halaqas and learn Quran without being coached, because it is the norm.
Story: the empty masjid in 2013

He came to a new city, the masjid was empty seven days a week. They started programs. For months there were complaints about loud children and candy wrappers. He did not respond. After a week off people asked where the kids were.
Change starts with you
Everything around us sucks and we are amazing. You cannot control others. Start with what you control.
Build positive cultures and make them contagious
Something weird and unwanted becomes the norm. Letting young people lead prayers drew complaints at first.
If we were transported to the Prophet's time
You would feel foreign. They lined up, prayed and listened differently.
Masajid reputation
The grumpy man yelling about shoes. It should be anyone who greets and helps newcomers. Conceptually easy, very hard to do.
Two options
Do it how the people before did and expect people to fall in line, risking repelling many, or adapt.
Two faces and strong culture
A strong group culture means you are the same person inside and outside. Children follow whichever culture is stronger.
Why kids misbehave in the masjid
The outside culture is stronger than the inside one.
The sum of cultures
Until one or two generations hold core values, places have no culture. Then people just do it automatically.
Social norms and arrogance
Walking into a space and refusing the norm shows arrogance. Norms are only a problem when not embedded in Islamic values.
Norms not from Islam
Many adab came from parents or a time in our lives and are not Islamic. How do we change them?
If I ran it as I was taught
Would you last? You would stop coming. That does not achieve the goal.
Cultures last while the connection lasts
They fade after a couple hundred years when people forget why. At Hajj you pick up tawaf by looking around.
Be a pioneer
A rare chance in life: no Islamic culture yet exists here. You help set footsteps.
Story: starting a Quran program in Syria
No one sent their kids at first. He built it with his two brothers, then a few hundred students in two years. Children thought it was part of the school curriculum.
Superficial versus meaningful change
He can force behavior but without meaning it does not last. Do not be humble before you understand humility.
Why comprehension comes first
Talk it out, struggle, see if it works, then it is real and you can carry it elsewhere.
Good cultures are stronger
The Prophet had no law or politics, only a strong culture. He gave principles to govern relationships and the self.
The culture he wants
Respect for seeking knowledge, self-accounting, service, humility, compassion and commitment to the deen. It saves generations from reinventing the wheel.
Closing dua
Salawat on the Prophet. Some Arabic is a closing invocation, not verses.

L.title: Seeing through a lens of love
obj: Finish the hadith of the sweetness of iman: love Allah and His Messenger most, love people only for Allah, hate returning to disbelief like being thrown in fire.
Teach that you can only love people truly for Allah's sake, because other reasons come and go with mood.
Teach that every act of worship (abudiyyah) contains love, and why starting from the Prophet is easiest.
Show that all that Allah gives and withholds is love, and fear of punishment is not the same as no love.
Debrief the priority list exercise (ideal versus real).
Give the next salah practices: a pause before salah and one theme from al-Fatiha, plus the meaning of ruku'.
topics: Sweetness of iman: three conditions
Love Allah and His Messenger above all, love a person only for Allah, and hate to return to disbelief as one hates being thrown in fire. Hate is just love of the opposite.
Four loves for the sweetness
Allah, His Prophet, Muslims and Islam. If all four are among your greatest loves, practice becomes joyful.
Why do you love someone?
A student says he loves pets or parents because they did good for him. The teacher asks what happens when they stop providing, or someone abuses you. You are redefining love.
Love for Allah's sake survives mood
Otherwise love comes and goes with how someone behaved today. You love them even when they are at their worst.
Magnet analogy
Turning each molecule manually takes a lifetime. A big magnet turns everything. Once Allah is your biggest love you see people through that lens.
Keep the good ethics, change the lens
The early Muslims kept their good traits but saw them through reward and doing it for Allah.
Love as care
You love someone when you worry about them and cannot say I do not care. Lust mixes into romantic love and fades in months.
Love requires knowing yourself
He will return to it every couple of months because your self-understanding grows.
You are enslaved to what you love
You pursue it to obtain or keep it. Abudiyyah is love-based service, not ownership or coercion.
Allah did more than my parents
Even if my life is not great, I was given existence. Understanding that changes how you see everything.
Why the dua for someone you dislike
One way to break hate is to say: he is Your servant, I bring him back to You out of love for You.
Loving what you never sensed
The only experience we have is of physical things. Our relation with Allah is unique. He also made everything we are.
The easiest door: love the Prophet
You can love a person you never met by learning his story, like loving a character in a movie. It is impossible to know him fully and not love him.
He is the middleman
Revelation was not given individually. He was chosen because he was most beloved to Allah. Through his love you learn the love of Allah.
A boring technical Islamic life
Without love it is mechanical. The early Muslims enjoyed saying His name.
Presence of the beloved is comforting
Opposite of isolation among people who treat you badly.
All of it is love, including hardship
If He gives He gives, if He withholds He gives. Looking back at 60 you see the difficulties differently. Tough love exists in parenting.
Fear of punishment and checking in
Salaf asked: are You upset or is there love? Difficulties are part of the deal, do not waste time on why.
Joy makes it sustainable
Fighting the nafs only works while you have energy in reserve. Joy in worship helps you rather than burdens.
Debrief: priority list

One student found his real priorities are dopamine things like YouTube and food. Another tells himself obligations are priorities but the time counts say otherwise. Another says priorities are seasonal and cyclical.
How to do the lists
Watch two to three days of what you do. That is the real list. Compare with the ideal and ask what is missing.
Why the real list differs
From the real list to the ideal list you question your understanding of the thing. If you can only do the wird in dead time you have not established belief in it. Needs self-coaching.
Do not alter your behavior while tracking
A student noticed he stopped himself from doing things so he would not have to write them. He asks for observation, not judgment.
Most people notice too late
Consequences later inform you: my family was my priority but they did not spend time with me. Giving money is not prioritizing relationships.
No new exercise, three salah practices
The most difficult and most important change is pausing before salah.
Practice 1: pause before salah
Stop the thought process, put a pin in it, centralize for a moment, then begin.
Practice 2: one theme from al-Fatiha
Choose one theme: praise, universal mercy, service (iyyaka na'budu), guidance, and think of it while reciting. Do not try all or you burn out. Same topic every time is fine.
Movements mirror attitudes
Each posture mimics a mental and spiritual transition. Standing is reciting the lesson back like a student.
Do not recite Quran in ruku or sujud
The Prophet forbade it. Recitation belongs to standing.
Ruku' is submission
Bowing says I am not equal to you. As for ruku': exalt your Lord.
Subhan means exalted
Muslims exalt Allah from time, space, flesh, emotions of envy and any similarity to creation. This differs from most faiths.
Blame yourself, not Allah
In hardship you ask what you could do better. It is one of the most important differences.
Ruku' coaches your opinion of Allah
Subhana rabbiyal azim. Your opinion: He is exalted, not questionable. You will need it in life when hit with curveballs.
Talking about God with people of loose language
People speak about God in a loose way. A Muslim, even a lay one, would not.
There is no equality in this love
He loved us first. If you love your child as an equal it is not pure, but with Allah it is exaltation.
Think of exaltation in ruku'
Take as long as you like in ruku' to exalt Him. This also deepens praise.
Love precedes us
His love is before us. We are given a chance to reciprocate, but you need these pieces.
Recap of the week
Pause before salah. Contemplate one theme at al-Fatiha. Reflect on exaltation in ruku'. Keep daily.

L.title: Maturity, play and aspiration
obj: Debrief the priority list exercise and explain the real question: why is there a gap between what I know is right and what I do?
Teach cognitive dissonance: the struggle cannot be a losing battle forever, so you either change your behavior or your opinion of the behavior.
Teach the qalb as the place of real beliefs, and that tazkiyah moves ideas from the superficial mind into the heart (the difference between islam and iman).
Teach that as long as you still struggle you are safe (the hadith of the man who killed a hundred).
Teach joy as the engine: the nafs seeks joy, maturity is widening what you find joyful toward what is useful.
Remind that the work is on the student, not the teacher, with daily self-questioning.
topics: Priority list check-in
Before moving to the next exercise he needs to know people tried it.
A student's checklist version
Made it a checklist. The first days were eye-opening, and checking items off became a habit. Time management and accountability help.
The real question: why the gap?
Why is there a difference between my ideal list and what I do? That is the question tazkiyah exists to answer.
The alien test
Explain to an alien that you believe an action helps you, you can physically do it, no one stops you, yet you do not. Laziness has no real definition.
Another creature inside
Something inside is steering and you are unaware. Until you recognize and acknowledge it you keep saying I know I am better than this.
Stakes rise with age
At 15 failing a semester is forgivable. At 35 not spending time with children or marriage problems stay with you.
Cognitive dissonance
Two ideas fight and you end with idea A, idea B or a mushy C. It is tiring, so something gives: change your behavior or change your opinion of the behavior.
Staying safe while struggling
The danger is changing your opinion of the bad behavior. As long as you struggle you are safe, but it cannot be a losing fight forever.
Acknowledging hurts
Most people never fully acknowledge the internal struggle. Naming it is painful on a basic psychological level, so we avoid opening that.
Why you really do it
Outside addiction, you do it because at some level you do not believe it is a problem. Coming to that conclusion matters.
Two layers: the mind and the qalb
The true priority list lives in the qalb. The Quran speaks of hardened hearts (qasawat al-qulub) where nothing gets in or out.
Superficial belief versus heart
Zina is haram, salah is wajib, be compassionate: ideas floating in the mind. Moving them into the heart is the work. He points to his Empty Space series as a baseline.
Islam versus iman
Iman is internalizing the theology so it becomes part of you. Quran: the Bedouin said we believe, say rather we submit, as iman has not entered your hearts (49:14).
Do not claim too early
If you do not feel it you are not there yet.
Ripping off the bandage
Most painful, a 20 year adhesive bandage. We prefer blaming the world, friends, parents, society, economy.
Iyyaka na'budu: the claim versus proof
What does Allah say back? Let's see. Saying I love you and not acting on it is worse than not saying it. Children of abusive parents are hurt more deeply.
A soft heart can be cleaned
The qalb always accumulates negativity and needs constant cleaning. A fortified heart takes nothing in and cannot be cleaned.
There is no safe point
You never reach a stage where you are done. The danger is a heart that projects darkness instead of taking in light.
As long as you fight, you are safe
The moment of giving up is the danger. Even in the mud, saying I know this is wrong, may Allah forgive me, is valuable.
Hadith: the man who killed a hundred
He had no moral compass but asked if there was repentance, and still had hope.
Student: is there a point where it gets easier?
He cautions about up and down language. Sensitivity to our relationship with Allah will be an upcoming exercise.
Free time and leisure
The nafs wants joy. When there is joy you focus easily and do not want to leave. When bored you want out. The problem lies there.
The sweet nectar again
Iman can become joyful if you get the right ingredients, and then it is less of a fight.
The scientist example
A scientist pouring over data is happier than you may be. Joy in productive activity is a big deal and tazkiyah moves fastest for such people.
Play and children
His two-year-old plays all day. Animals play. That is the human soul. Identify what is joyful and you see your patterns.
Joy in harmful things is the worst
Joy in useless or harmful activity is a problem.
Maturity is finding joy in the useful
He draws a line from childhood to adulthood. Leisure is still needed: laugh and drink tea with friends.
Taste of iman
Content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muhammad as Messenger. Hadith (Muslim): he has tasted the sweetness of iman.
Joy that pulls you from bed
The early night prayer: sides forsake beds to pray (32:16). The Prophet would stay if his wife wanted, then go. He found more joy elsewhere.
Maturity is widening your joy
Joyless rigid regimens fail because you cannot live without joy. Consistency depends on joy.
My job is to challenge, not to fix
He gives ideas, concepts, exercises and be a sounding board. You are the surgeon.
Student: I cannot find the answer why
Be patient. It is buried under rubble. Pull the thread even if slow. A therapist can help but can make you lazy.
Humans are lazy
Define laziness. You have to learn to figure yourself out, accountability, when to be lenient or strict.
Mujahadah
Push for answers you may not want. Conclusions will be uncomfortable. This is a form of jihad.
The nafs behind high walls
Your subconscious controls and holds the keys. If you can take care of your nafs you can overtake the world.
No promises
If you do not think about it, practice, do the exercises and come back to discuss, years later you will say I have not changed.
Daily four questions
Am I a good servant? Is my intention right? Are my actions accepted? Is it done with ihsan? Your nafs quickly forgets who it is.
Where the wird fits
He will talk about the wird over about six months. No effort, no change.
Outcome of the work
People enjoy you more, you become kinder, considerate, hold yourself to a standard without arrogance.
Chipping at the wall
Every chip hurts. At some point you find joy. Hadith: none of you believes until his desires follow what I came with.
Desires can shift
The righteous still feel accountable, with higher sensitivity, and find joy in learning, teaching, worship and khayr.
What is useful?
Helpful to others or to yourself physically, mentally, financially or socially. Maturity is doing something useful, ideally for others.
Joy in work
If you find no joy in job, volunteering or relationships you are a miserable human being. Change definitions and priorities. If you enjoy your job it stops being work.

L.title: Purposefulness
obj: Debrief the joy and fun reflection: what makes something fun and what it means to focus through joy instead of discipline.
Teach three factors behind joy: knowing how to do it, conditioning and labels, and accomplishment tied to purpose.
Show that learning itself is joyful and that school conditioning taught us it is boring (Adam and the names).
Teach purpose as a hierarchy where small tasks feed a bigger aim, which is why the daily four reminders matter.
Argue you need some portion of joy in hard things (inna ma'al usri yusra) and that love is the only lasting motive.
Set the exercise: pick a meaningful task you dislike and find a way to make it joyful.
topics: Topic is timeless
Some tazkiyah topics fit anywhere. He leaves them before breaks for reflection.
Two ways to focus
Discipline yourself to concentrate, or be naturally focused on what you find fun. Can a behavior be made fun?
Why do animals play?
Psychology still does not fully understand play. Ask why fun is fun.
Factor 1: you enjoy what you know
If you do not understand the terminology in a course you hate it. It is not the math. Reverse the advice: you become good at what you learn, then enjoy it.
A child who stands at his chair
A story about a child who will not move from standing in front of him, showing how focus drifts.
Students' answers on fun
Easy to access like video games, things from childhood, accomplishment, pleasure, benefit, stimulation, competitiveness, feedback like points.
Going to work with dad
One student said something he hated for six or seven years became enjoyable once he saw it as time with his dad.
Do good marks feel good?
Positive feedback such as points or praise adds to the fun.
Myth: do what you are good at
Nobody is born good at anything except one in a million. His clinic example: he enjoys the cancers he knows how to treat and dreads a clinic where he does not know the drugs.
Teachers decide the subject
You dislike a topic because of who taught it. The subject is blameless.
Factor 2: conditioning
Are we told what is fun? Alcohol and tobacco taste horrible the first times and make you vomit, but peers condition you to like it.
Studying is not boring, we were conditioned
