Neuroscientists find solving a problem releases the same reward as the most pleasurable things. Aha moments.
Story: taking Quran away from his son
He forbade his son from picking up the Quran. After shock, the son came back three days later asking for it. A privilege, not a duty.
Homeschool examples
Children raised to see learning as fun did far better. A psychologist family raised a world chess champion.
Adam and the names
Learning is the first thing Allah did for Adam. Angels could not do what Adam did: process, add something of himself. Your brain is a processor, not storage.
Learning is the most fulfilling thing
Arrahman, taught the Quran. The aim is infinite so you never stop. Sad that most want never to open a book again.
Interest in different things
You can be more drawn to one subject than another. Knowledge is knowledge. Do not accept the label learning is boring.
Factor 3: accomplishment tied to purpose
Purposefulness: serving the nation, pleasing Allah, in his case educating and mentoring. Every small act feeds a bigger one.
Story: reciting a half-juz to the sheikh
The happiest moment of his life was after passing his recitation: not just an accomplishment but a step in his chain toward ijazah.
The three questions
Is there labeling and conditioning? Does knowing how increase joy? Does purposeful accomplishment add joy? And how to balance benefit with needed fun.
Accomplishment is a stepping stone
A stepping stone to purpose. People who live for Allah find joy in every little thing because all channels toward the aim.
Living for the weekend
Good physicians can be miserable. Life is not designed to be lived that way. Things that do not serve the purpose naturally fall away.
Why video games are fun, asked later
He avoids why for now so as not to confuse. First: can meaningful things be fun?
Student story: joy after validation
Finishing a section with the sheikh felt like a step closer to the certificate and the chain of narration.
The four daily reminders give purpose
Reminding yourself what your purpose is makes simple acts like eating or intimacy become sadaqah with the right intention.
Habit loop book reference
A student mentions cue, craving, response, reward. He says it is more complex but a good baseline.
Getting out of weekend living
Find purposefulness and joy in daily activities and you stop living for the weekend.
Even a clear purpose does not make studying all joyful
A med student will not enjoy 100% of study but 25 to 30% joy carries you.
The Ramadan statistic
Perhaps 5% of salah in Ramadan is joyful, yet we call it the best time. Imagine 25% or 40%.
Not everything can be fun
Of course there is struggle but some portion of joy is needed. Inna ma'al usri yusra (94:6): difficulty with ease.
Rewards versus love
A student asks about reward charts with his son. Not everyone responds to the same reinforcement. Reward-based motives do not last, only love does.
The exercise
Take a meaningful, beneficial task you dislike (not necessarily service) and find a way to make it joyful. Run it by him by text or he will pick it apart.
Example: waking up early
Do not pick something trivial. Ask whether waking early can be made enjoyable. There is no one switch, many tweaks.
Attach something enjoyable
Make a pleasant breakfast, meet someone. It is training wheels. Flash cards were rejected as not clearly purposeful.
The double decker bus to the beach
If you were told at 5 am you were going to the beach you would not dread waking. Attached joy makes it easy. Over time the meaning itself becomes the joy.
Camp idea
Students suggest a group camp. He lived without electronics for years, slept after isha and woke before fajr with the birds.

L.title: Choosing the activity
obj: Explain why exercises exist: to learn something about yourself, not to tick a box.
Give the rules for the 'make a disliked, purposeful task joyful' exercise and the classic qualifying choices.
Teach the aha conclusion: what you dislike is mostly about you, not the task. Want is the real issue.
Show how to adjust a task (company, expectations, environment, education) so it becomes enjoyable, using fasting and waking early as models.
Teach that honesty with yourself (about 90% of this) and honesty with Allah is the base, and that artificial motives are fine as training wheels.
topics: Recap
Last time was joy and fun. Now commit to an exercise.
Exercises teach you about yourself
If you run from it, pick something easy or fool yourself you cheat yourself. Baby steps now versus huge painful changes later.
Deadline: next week
By next week you choose. He shares classic choices but leaves the choice to you.
Classic choices
Waking up for Fajr and staying awake, fasting (people who dislike it often ask to fast daily afterward), a daily learning topic or online lecture, time with relatives you do not enjoy.
What does not qualify
Getting groceries for your sister does not. It must be something you can actually enjoy, and more than once a week.
Not too simple, not too complex
Too simple and it is just commitment. Too complex and it takes layers. It needs adjustments and associations.
Differs from the earlier act of service exercise
Earlier: do a hated service until you stop hating it. Now we want to enjoy it, and it need not be service or for someone else.
Daily exercise and walking to the masjid
Daily physical exercise also applies. Walking to the masjid may lack complexity.
Student: I do not hate it, I just do not do it
He needs something you genuinely dislike to see how you can go from not liking to liking.
The aha conclusion
When you move from not liking to liking, you see it was never about the task, it was about you. You just do not want to.
Honesty is 90% of it
Not bullshitting yourself. Therapeutic once admitted.
Want is the big word
Where does it come from, what is it based on. Later topic.
Value in the cellar
You assigned it a good value somewhere deep. To remove the dislike you have to change your attitude to the activity.
Addiction is different
Cocaine involves physical dependence plus value. Not blame.
Come to Allah transparently
As long as you admit you do not like yourself in that, you are safe. Lying breaks trust. Self-awareness is the majority of the first years.
Can fasting go from dread to enjoyment?
You do not want to, that is all. Another student's answer sheet: fasting twice a week.
Ramadan versus twice a week
The first two days of Ramadan are hard, he misses the lunchtime tea. After two or three days it is fine.
Fasting with water as a start
He allows easing in with partial steps, not legally fasting but as exercise.
How to make fasting enjoyable
Fast with someone, plan something nice, pace your day, sleep early for suhoor. Fasting also makes you more functional.
Adjustments differ by activity
For a family member you do not enjoy, find common ground, avoid arguments, talk about topics that are safe.
Student story: fasting gave migraines
Because of a rushed approach, poor suhoor and too packed a day. That is what he means by adjustments.
Waking up early
Do something beneficial after Fajr. Adjust sleep time, put the alarm across the room, get out immediately, ask someone to wake you.
Remove demotivators, add motivators
Make lunch the night before and have things ready.
Expectations
If your expectation is waking at 7 then 7:05 is fine. Fasting twice a week in Ramadan would feel amazing.
Why not snooze
Snoozing trains indecisiveness. Set a real time and decide.
Tips later from the Sunnah
He wants them to try first and research, then he will share the Prophet's habits like the nap (qaylula).
Nap tradition
A colleague naps 20 minutes in his office after clinic and is more functional. A lifestyle adjustment.
Bed-making is not complex enough
Needs adjustments to your life. Waking up and staying functional needs many.
The five qualifying categories
Waking up early, praying on time or fasting, daily exercise, daily learning, time with people you do not enjoy. Others can be shared.
School homework does not qualify
Too complex.
Education changes the attitude
Read about benefits such as dunya and akhirah benefits of fasting to be convinced. Spending 10 to 15 hours making it enjoyable is worth it as a lifelong investment.
The later trap
Waiting for after medical school, marriage, a steady job. The nafs says later so you never change.
Training wheels fall away
Company, food and tricks stop mattering. Hunger gets easier after two days.
Using artificial motives
A student says he is doing it for the teacher. That is fine if you know you need extra help and it is not the only motive forever.
Why the student put it last on his list
The nafs saves the least wanted item for last.

L.title: Making it feasible
obj: Check in on the 'make a disliked task joyful' exercise: early wakers and fasters report what changed.
Teach that evidence (hadith, science) only helps once you have decided to act, and that research is part of the adjustment.
Teach honesty with yourself: affirmations and 'fake it till you make it' can lie, so use true sentences from contemplation.
Warn about getting status or reward you did not work for (entitlement).
Introduce tawadu' (humbleness) as the master of ethics and draw the pendulum of self-view and view of others.
topics: Who tried the exercise?
Students share early attempts.
Waking up: adjustments need to be more than an alarm
A student woke fine on weekends but not for school because he dislikes what comes next. He is told to try sleeping earlier.
Fasting two days: forgot why I hated it
A student fasted two days and forgot why he was against it.
Joy needs a change of perspective
Looking forward to something requires a change of mindset and adjustments. It takes time.
Waking early and sleeping earlier worked
He gets more done in the morning, feels better and has nicer evenings.
Research why it is good
Part of the adjustment is learning the science and religious evidence. This is only helpful once you decided to change.
Silat ar-rahim as an example
The ahadith on kinship become meaningful when you actually have to spend time with a relative you do not enjoy.
Dealing with people you dislike
Stop reading everything they say negatively. A student with an unfiltered relative finds humor now.
Story: great aunt and the donkey
After Eid they visited the cemetery for the elders. A confused elderly aunt called him 'Abu Himar' (father of the donkey). Take it in a way that does not harm you.
Question: visualizing the goal
Self-help books say imagine the end result. Imagining is fine, but telling yourself you already did it takes drive away. Do not tell others your goals.
Affirmations: I am merciful
A student says it made him narcissistic. The teacher says it is better to remind yourself I will be merciful today, not I am.
Never lie to yourself
He will never encourage lying to yourself in tazkiyah. Be honest: I am tired but I have enough sleep to function. Encouraging yourself is not lying.
Man up when it is cold
A student says telling yourself it is not cold is fine. Teacher: you are encouraging yourself, not lying about the facts.
Contemplation ends in a real sentence
When you contemplate you end with a true sentence to repeat.
Fruit you did not work for
Affirming that you already achieved takes the fruit without work. An MD title without medical school.
Entitlement and youth
Young stars and athletes lose their way because they get what others work 40 years for. Many legends vanished in their early twenties.
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
He worked hard and was chosen as heir with no favor to the family, restoring things. Hard work teaches you to handle power.
Entitlement and comfort
We do not realize how entitled we are. Serve in uncomfortable places to humble yourself.
Born and buried in a refugee camp
A young man died in a refugee camp in Palestine, born and buried there. Something to reflect on.
Starting tawadu'
The second layer: hub, tawadu', rahma. He mentions his Aqidah series and that the humility course normally takes eight months.
Humility is the master of ethics
Sayyid al-akhlaq. Without it we are wasting time and he would be harming them.
Is love an ethic?
Love is hard to define, not an ethic, not just an emotion. Motive is an effect, not a definition.
The pendulum
Inside you is a pendulum that swings with life. The goal is to hold it in the middle.
Two levels: self-view and view of others
The first layer is how you view yourself (confidence and low self-esteem). The second is you in comparison to others.
Both extremes are toxic
Vanity when things go well, inferiority when you fail. Arab men can be confident about nothing. The nafs wants survival.
Swinging freely
Arrogant people are often depressed because the pendulum swings freely. Staying fixed at one end is a psychiatric problem.
Goal: confidence plus humility
Confidence in how you see yourself, humility in how you deal with people. Humbleness is both.
Can one exist without the other?
True confidence has humility. Without both, one is a mask.
The nafs and the middle
It will lie to make you think you are there while pushing you to an extreme.
Swing is natural
You still feel happy and sad. The ethic keeps your behavior the same.
Humble definition
Proper understanding of your self-vision plus proper vision of yourself relative to others.

L.title: Value and mood swings
obj: Explain the low side of the pendulum (low self-esteem), why it is more common today and why it usually needs outside help.
Explain why the nafs naturally pushes you to the high side and why the same person swings both ways.
Introduce self-value as what fuels the pendulum and ask where you derive it.
Teach that your value as a human is constant, given by Allah (karramna bani adam), so nothing raises or lowers it.
Separate 'value to a team' (productivity, usefulness) from your value as a human being.
topics: Plan: look from different angles
Humbleness is simple, but he will go through it from several angles until fully comprehended.
The low side is shorter to cover
The nafs usually finds a way out of a low quickly. Long stuck is a clinical issue needing therapy or medication.
The high side is organic
The nafs is grandiose and wants to tell you that you are better than you are. A survival mechanism.
Low is more common today
Past societies had larger communities and constant contact. Now people can be isolated at home, with fewer interactions that pull them out.
Modern pace and stress
More demands, quicker pace, less leisure, more anxiety.
The Quran talks less about the low side
It is more abnormal and usually needs external help.
Those who swing high swing low too
Arrogant and vain people often have severe depression. The pendulum swings freely or you hold it narrow.
The nafs is a child
His two-year-old cries as if his arm was cut over a chocolate. The nafs cannot regulate emotions.
Disorders keep people at one end
Psychopaths can sit at one end, chronic mental health conditions at the other. This is not a psychiatry class.
The norm and learned regulation
Good makes you happy, bad makes you sad, and you learn to lessen the bad. No one fixes what feels good.
Drugs swing the pendulum aggressively
He declines to become a substance abuse specialist in class.
Sadness is normal
Life ends and has pain. Nothing to fix when you are sad occasionally. Allow it, then move on. It is an issue when stuck.
The two layers again
Layer one: how you see yourself in the mirror. Layer two: how you compare to others.
Are we born pure and balanced?
Babies swing wildly with no regulation. Regulation starts around age two.
The nafs learns to find reasons to feel high
Delusional people with nothing to be happy about believe everyone should want them.
What fuels the swing: self-value
Good days send it one way, bad days the other. The nafs keeps trying to send it up.
Where do you derive value?
Students: purpose, grades, satisfying others. If your purpose is to satisfy others, one busy day means zero value.
Value must be constant
A student says it must be something that does not change.
Identity as a Muslim
A student suggests identity. The teacher says that is more basic.
Your value is given by Allah
It never grows with success or shrinks with failure. No one can touch it. It is equal to everyone's.
Cut the tubes
The tubes fill and vacuum it. Say: Allah created me, He must see something in me. I try again the thousand and first time.
Open the cellar for self-value
Go down and see where you derive value. You may be surprised.
Closer to Allah means more valuable?
How do we measure? You cannot judge others. Each measures themselves against themselves.
Motivation based on value
Do you act to become more valuable? Who told you you had less? What if you fail?
Why the word value?
If something is worthless it has no value. Is anyone worthless? We should not see ourselves or others that way.
Hold accountability without value
Compare yourself to yourself and ask whether you are making progress. Nothing changes your intrinsic value.
Is value binary?
If it grows or shrinks it swings. The fuel must be steady.
Society assigns value to brands and wealth
You absorb what others assign. A student argues society must regulate behavior and feel shame.
No one should feel worthless
Feeling worthless requires mental health work. Change behavior without attacking value.
Purpose, not amount
Allah gave everyone a purpose, abudiyyah, and made the earth serve us. The amount is not what matters, constancy is.
The Oscar winner example
A billionaire most handsome person can still struggle because there is nothing to compare to and it never feels enough.
Karramna: Allah dignified you
Dignity given by Allah (17:70). Why prove you are more valuable?
Proving your value is fine in a team
Value to a team means usefulness and productivity, not human value.
Repercussions of mixing them
If I am not valuable to the NBA team, I am not worthless as a person.
Basketball example
A student sucks at basketball but does not feel less human. Skill is separate from value.

L.title: Small adjustments
obj: Open with the group wird: salawat on the Prophet, istighfar, al-Fatiha, al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas.
Teach that making a disliked task enjoyable needs small adjustments that chain together, not one big change.
Teach that failure must be analyzed (why did I fall off?) and never blamed on 'some reason'.
Show that you can attach something enjoyable to the task as a stepping stone, but invest in the task itself so it survives when the attachment is removed.
Note that joy plus function is rare (sports), and that either you discipline yourself or you make it enjoyable.
topics: Group wird begins
Long recitation in Arabic: istighfar and salawat on the Prophet (about 1:19), then later the opening surah and the three short surahs. Audio is mostly static between.
Al-Fatiha
Recited at about 9:09.
Al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas
Recited at about 9:26 to 10:14.
Check in on the exercise
Most people have chosen a task. He offered advice to some from each group.
Small versus large adjustments
The exercise was meant to need small adjustments, since large ones are hard to maintain. Small ones chain like dominoes.
Example: waking for Fajr
Needs sleeping around 9, no pending work, less leisure in the day, and ordering the day backward from the sleep time.
Add something to look forward to
A particular breakfast, meeting someone, a ritual. He will not spoon-feed every factor.
Large adjustments come later
If you learn small ones you can handle big ones. A student asks how to remove a 10 to 15 year habit.
Make the habit feasible instead of counting days
Reduce obstacles to good habits and add checkpoints between you and a bad habit.
Write down your adjustments
Keep a list of what small changes you made.
Punishment or doubling for missed days
A student asks about penalties. It is a classic method from the scholars. If you miss, you do it twice. Requires discipline. He does not mandate it.
This exercise is not discipline
The earlier exercise used discipline. This one asks you to find comfort and joy. You live by the routine you built so you have to move things around.
Can it still be hard?
Yes. Enjoyable means you look forward to it. 25% joy can be enough. There is always some jihad.
Fasting adjustments
Sleep earlier, fast with someone, be focused since you are hungry anyway, and have a meal to look forward to.
Changes are required for any improvement
You cannot consult the deen and keep your routine safe. Most people stick to the routine they have.
Alarm far away
Small, simple changes work when you know yourself.
Student: fasting from Fajr was too hard
Wake earlier and fast from Fajr while the day stayed as busy, so the last hours were dreadful.
Building habits takes longer than 30 days
Months may pass before you find the sweet spot. Familiarity lets you appreciate the goodness.
How to restart after falling off
Reset, but ask why you fell off. People do not do the analysis.
No 'for some reason'
Someone said he missed the prayer for some reason. That deflects blame to something abstract. Find the exact cause.
The wird had the same history
On and off at first. He had to make small adjustments to make it continuous: sit after Fajr until done.
Discipline or joy
Either discipline yourself fully or it becomes enjoyable. He thinks you can afford not to do everything by discipline alone.
Work example
He hates the paperwork and certain clerks but likes patients, so he keeps going. Without a bit of joy only discipline remains.
Reading the section on prayer
A student found reading Ghazali on prayer improved focus, but it faded. Reinforce the why continuously.
Adding a habit needs room
Otherwise it is a foreign body and gets thrown out.
The bus to Vegas
It is not the waking that is the problem, it is motivation and the context.
Attach a ritual
Breakfast, friends, a workout. Artificial joy is fine.
Hate the workout, love Fajr
If you wake for a workout you must be up for Fajr. Fajr becomes easy.
How to keep it fresh
Change details, renew the intention. Boredom comes from losing the intention and turning it into habit.
Habits are good but risky
Islamically habits can lose the essence, so aim for joy not just habit.
The cheat code
The means do not matter. If you do it long enough you become the person who does it. Like training wheels.
Joy threshold
A student asks if the target is 100% joy. It is enough to keep you going.
Functional and enjoyable is rare
Sports is the main example. Professional athletes lose the fun.
Daily four things
Check your intention daily.
Attaching soccer to Fajr
A student wanted soccer after Fajr and his mother objected. The teacher says it is okay if you know you are too weak otherwise, and tell Allah that.
Negotiating with the nafs
Like negotiating with a monster at the wheel. Methods: harsh (raise the wird in steps), negotiate (soccer for Fajr), or change life so it is natural.
Intention stays good if it started right
If you started for Fajr, the attachment improves it. Losing focus can happen at any time.
Invest in the activity itself
If the attachment drops and you have not invested, you lose Fajr. Study it, listen to Quran and find how to focus.
When religion is low
Safety adjustments (team, companionship) carry you.
Big adjustments come later
Not yet. If you do not do small ones you will not do big ones.
Halal attachments only
Video games during the first hour of the fast is a free ride, a grace period, then invest in Fajr.
Ramadan is a gift
Everything comes for free for 30 days. If you build adjustments before Ramadan it will help.
Failed to sleep early
Did you finish work, stop eating, stop the phone? A student started sleeping hungry so he wakes hungry and eats suhoor.
Salaf kids waking starving
In the old days kids ate at 5pm and woke at 6:30 starving, so Fajr was followed by a great breakfast.
Closing: judge your own niyyah
Next topic is value, but time ran out.

L.title: Adjustments for Ramadan
obj: Close the 'make a disliked task joyful' exercise by stating what you were meant to learn.
Teach small adjustments (a ripple through your schedule) and associations (the carrot behind the deed) as the method for building good habits.
Teach the grace period: the nafs gets bored, so use the truce to build a real relationship with the deed.
Teach that bad habits need large adjustments (cold turkey), which is what Ramadan is for, and good habits need small ones, as two parallel tracks.
Assign the Ramadan plan and a detailed list of your bad habits.
topics: Opening banter
The teacher says he lived his whole life in his village and never in Damascus.
Group wird recitation
Arabic dhikr, salawat, then al-Fatiha (about 9:31), al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, an-Nas. Mostly Arabic with static.
Exercise check-in
A student sleeps early and wakes early but needs a great day to end on a high, so he stays up till 1 am.
What is a great day?
Who defines a great day? You may have defined it subconsciously. Redefine it as a day you fulfill obligations and do khayr.
Wrap-up of the exercise
He will make sure the lesson is clear. Waking early is just the example.
Your day is segments
Pulling the wake time earlier means pulling sleep earlier and removing something else. A ripple effect through the schedule.
Small versus large adjustment
A large adjustment rips the routine out, like a catastrophe or being thrown into jail. Cutting scrolling for an hour is small.
Have a schedule
If you do not have a schedule this will be hard.
Associations: the carrot behind the deed
Use the strength of your nafs. Put what it likes right behind the deed you want: soccer after Fajr, a nice breakfast, a workout.
Discipline versus diplomacy
Discipline is fine, but this is a diplomatic approach: what do you need to leave me alone so I can get up for Fajr?
The grace period
The nafs gets bored quickly. His son loses interest in the thing and is left with waking up. The truce lets you build a real relationship with the deed.
Use the grace period
Study Fajr and the wird, increase khushu', cement it into your schedule. If not, you keep swapping rewards. Cemented deeds do not fall off when the schedule shifts.
Bad habits are cemented too
They also resist the ripple. That is why bad habits need large adjustments.
Large adjustments remove bad habits
Ramadan rips your schedule out and gives a 30-day window with no room for bad habits. Good habits need small adjustments.
Cold turkey for addictions
Alcohol, drugs, porn: you rip it out completely. Gradual does not work.
Why we attach things
People survive jobs or school by finding enjoyable parts. 25 to 30% joy is enough.
Student: the gym example
His brother in the military must go to the gym daily. Attach it after Fajr.
Ramadan: cleaning bad habits
Gossip, video games, internet, movies. Then make small adjustments so they do not return.
Assignment: write your Ramadan plan
Be detailed with tangible goals, not 'be closer to Allah'. Think about your schedule.
He books the last ten nights a year ahead
Every fiscal year he blocks the last ten days off, unreachable.
Be realistic
If you did not fast regularly, do not plan to fast forever after.
Student: social media at Ramadan
Videos pull you in for 15 minutes. Check iPhone screen time. Be specific about what you scroll.
Apps that make you write your intention
A student shares an app that asks you for an intention before opening social apps.
Moderation
One student deleted social media during fourth year and found it harder to talk with family.
Assignment: list your bad habits
Be specific: which app, how long, what content. You can only remove a habit you describe well.
Two parallel universes
Bad habits are removed with large adjustments, good habits inserted with small ones. Replacing one with the other does not work.
Replace with Quran?
He is not sure replacing works. Music: art has a role, but overlistening and certain content is a problem.
Rip out then reintroduce
If it is a bad habit, remove it completely, then bring it back with a plan if it is halal.
Ramadan changes preferences
You usually do not feel like music in Ramadan.
Ramadan is your hero
A safe haven for self-accountability. Write a plan every year. The Salaf wrote plans.
Why people could not stop eating the soup
Last time someone struggled with fasting. He wanted them to ask why.
Bad habits versus serious ethical flaws
Lying is more serious than a bad habit.
Be ambitious
Set your sights high so that when you fail you still land high.
Ramadan is one big tazkiyah halaqa
Over the break he will give them something to contemplate. He thinks of expectations and assumptions.
Question: how to sleep in Ramadan
Depends on your day. He sleeps less all month and makes it up after Fajr and in the last week.

L.title: Defining habits
obj: Teach how to define a bad habit precisely (what, when, where, how long, why) because vague habits never go.
Choose three bad habits for Ramadan, one of them a heart-based tazkiyah habit such as bad assumptions or showing off (riya').
Build the Ramadan schedule: Quran (memorize, recite, comprehend), qiyam, congregational prayer, knowledge, service, and a planning (future) session.
Teach what to carry after Ramadan: start small habits during Ramadan and decide three things to continue.
Teach life planning with milestones across categories, and getting advice on whether a goal is realistic.
topics: Three elements of the Ramadan plan
Remove three bad habits, build the schedule, choose what to hold on to afterward.
Ramadan is a large adjustment
It ruins your routine so you cannot do bad habits if you do it well. Awareness is 90% of removing them.
Be specific
A student says he scrolls before sleep. He is pushed: how long, what app, doing what? Instagram for 30 to 45 minutes.
Pick only three
More than three and you fail or get bored.
Define profanity
He says there are no bad words, only bad intentions. Is it when angry, with which friends? Break it into specifics.
Sleeping in
Give hours and days and what you should be doing. He pushes a student to go deeper.
Gaming
He is not against all gaming. Define the hours, the games, the times. Keep what is moderate and halal.
A student: watch a YouTube video before study
The teacher says it is up to him. A bad habit is subjective apart from open sin.
Lowering the gaze example
Define exactly when and where: at the gym, at a specific spot. The more you define the sin, the more you catch it.
One must be a tazkiyah habit
One of the three should be inside the heart. Suggested starters: bad assumptions and showing off.
Bad assumptions
Easy to define. When do you assume bad of someone or feel upset at their success? While driving you assume every driver is out to get you.
Riya', showing off
Wanting recognition. Imams and reciters have a big internal struggle: are you doing it for Allah or for their praise?
Mixed intentions
Do not stop the deed because your intention may be mixed. Keep doing and keep watching.
Reflection is how you remove it
Why should I care what they think? It requires constant reinforcement.
Start with sins
If there is a sin, start with the sin. Make one in the qalb.
Arrogance as an example
Think where you feel it and be aware each time.
Intention like a vessel
A drop of the other in the love of Allah is what we fear. It is a problem only if it is fully for people.
Bad assumptions ruin humbleness
Start with that one, especially for young people.
Why three
Five or six leads to dropping them all.
Schedule your Ramadan
Write down each day. His routine has not changed for 20 years: wake, work, steal an hour of sleep, kids, food, halaqa, repeat.
Cut out time wasters
Remove gatherings that do not help. He skips his weekly family card game for the month and tells them he will see them after.
Quran in Ramadan
Memorization, recitation (how many khatmas) and comprehension (listening to tafsir).
Prayers
Add nawafil. Congregational Fajr and Isha at least. Tarawih with nothing less than a full khatm if possible.
Stand with the Quran
If you do not do it now you never will. Do it in the masjid.
Seek knowledge
Plan which halaqa or course. Any knowledge counts.
Do not read from the phone in prayer
He says to leave it, listen to the Imam.
The worship of planning
Schedule time to sit and contemplate your future. Have a ten year picture.
Your plan will fail, but have it
It gives you direction and a value-based approach. In 2010 he would not have believed he would be where he is.
Journal
Write it out. He brought his journals when he left Syria.
Milestones
Goals without milestones are useless. They help you adjust when a curveball hits.
Story: starting in 2013
He arrived in July 2013, wrote his first lessons in English, and started this halaqa in September 2013. It has run 11 years.
Categories of life
Academic, social, financial, contribution, physical, and prioritize.
Give it time
Three days of 30 minutes each will clarify who you are and drop unrealistic goals.
When do I give up on a goal?
Ask wiser people who care for you. Medical school applicants who retry need plan B and C. Be realistic about NBA dreams.
Ramadan schedule also includes service
Volunteering, sadaqah. Stronger schedule, better result.
What to hold on to after Ramadan
You cannot keep everything. Choose categories: Quran, prayers, knowledge, relationships.
Start it during Ramadan
Whatever weekly or daily habit you want to continue, start it now. Do two rakahs of qiyam after Ramadan if you did 20.
Large for bad, small for good
Remove big bad habits with large adjustments, add good habits with small ones.
Baby steps afterward
You cannot hold the same frequency afterward. Define something doable.
Deliverables for next time
Three defined bad habits (one inner), a schedule and what to hold on to.
How not to go back
If you really removed the time slot for 30 days, going back is less likely.
Overeating at iftar
Eat a few dates, water, soup, then tarawih, then more. A full stomach means no khushu'. The first three days are the hardest.

L.title: Relative value and assumptions
obj: Start the revision cycle: two of the four categories per sitting, finishing in roughly 10 weeks.
Re-teach the four daily points of reflection: servanthood, acceptance of deeds, improving the intention, and the spiritual side of everything.
Teach self-value (comprehension) with the pendulum: why it swings and why it should not.
Separate relative value (to a team, job, community) from innate value (given by Allah, fixed).
Show that comparison and bad assumptions come from taking value from variable things, and that real humbleness is accepting reality.
Plant the question for next week: should you hope others do better than you?
topics: Revision plan
Goal is to cover everything again in about 10 weeks. Each sitting covers two of the four categories. Today is comprehension.
Four daily points
Think about them every day until they become second nature.
Servanthood
Ask: is this behavior the best expression of service to Allah? Would a true servant think or act like this? At least once a day.
Do not set a time for it
If you schedule it, it only happens then. It should arise at any moment, through experience.
Acceptance of deeds
Always wonder whether your deeds might be accepted. That pushes you to do a little better.
Improving your intention
Always ask if your intention is good. Caring about it is the safety. When it stops mattering to you, you are in trouble.
The spiritual aspect of everything
Even playing sports has an inner dimension. Do not ignore it.
Today: self-value
The clearest category but the most complex. Taught through the pendulum.
The pendulum
Life is a bumpy road and swings you both ways. People with arrogance and vanity are also the ones who later fall to low self-esteem.
Should it swing at all?
Probably not, it is unhealthy. What fuels the swing? How you value yourself.
Relative value vs whole value
His value to an NBA team is minus a million, to a medical team it is reasonable. That is relative. Your value as a person is different.
What feeds your value
Class brainstorm: wealth, utility, social status, health, accomplishments, reputation, friends. Should they affect you? They do, but should they?
Variable value means endless swinging
The only way for the swing to stop is for the source to be constant.
Your value is divine
Praise does not raise it and humiliation does not lower it. Being paraded on a donkey takes away relative value, not innate value.
Athletes and depression
People who see themselves only through relative value fight to be valuable all their life. It is a sad existence.
Check where you take value from
When you feel bad about losing money, you were taking self-value from wealth. Watch yourself for the rest of your life.
Better reason to act
Doing things to prove you are worth something is a sad motive. You already have worth, so find a better reason.
How we were raised
Some friends were told they are valuable from birth, which is better, but they lack motivation. Many of us were told 'doctor or lawyer or you are dead'.
Status is not value
Your reach and status do not equal your value. We are equal, and he will never be more than a hafid.
Taking feedback
If you cannot take criticism, you tied self-value to relative value. A medical student told he takes poor histories should hear it as room to grow.
Equal is not arrogant
I am not better than you and you are not better than me. I may be a worse physician or athlete and still equal.
Humbleness needs this
Humbleness is not an act. Acting humble while thinking you are higher is disguised arrogance. It is accepting reality.
The reality
We are from earth and return to it. Only Allah judges ranks. His satisfaction motivates you.
Value motivation is short-lived
Once you feel full of yourself you stop trying, then lie, steal and harm to protect it. Even a billionaire compares himself to someone else.
Recording noise and recitation
From about 20:00 to 38:00 the audio is mostly noise, music and a recitation of Al-Fatiha (around 26:49 to 29:48). No teaching here.
Where do you derive your value?
Usually over weeks they find every source is variable and so dangerous. Only the Divine is constant, directly between you and Allah.
Evaluate with ideals, not value
Hold yourself to principles and ethics, not 'high value today, low value today'. Bosses, parents and friends who do the latter are toxic.
Comparison is the biggest source
Within five seconds you size up a stranger and tell a story to feel a little better. You would not want to be sized up yourself.
The river and the streams
Comparison is the big river feeding self-value. Comparing relative skills is fine, comparing who is 'better' as a person is not.
Gamers and rage quits
Rage comes from deriving value from a game. Utility, wealth, health and beauty are fine to build, just not as self-value.
When it is pathological
Stuck pendulums are psychiatric problems and need treatment. This halaqa is not for that.
Assumptions come from comparison
You cannot know anyone's story, not even if they tell you. Judging is insane, yet it makes us feel better.
If you assume, assume good
Someone cuts you off, maybe he had a bad day. Not naive, not a doormat, but bad assumptions afflict you, not them.
When bad assumptions are allowed
Marriage, leadership, teaching, business and money, advice, and protection. A father should assume the worst to catch problems.
Better still: do not assume
You know nothing about them. If the nafs wants an assumption, give it a good one so it loses its purpose.
Story of his shaykh

A friend who was a mesmerizing speaker visited. The shaykh realized he took value from public speaking, so he had the friend give the khutbah every night for a week while he introduced him and served water.
Father and child
Questioned why a father assumes the worst. The point stays: with responsibility you must, otherwise do not.
Why we assume
You are still taking self-value from comparison. Stop that and good assumptions become easy.
Redirect curiosity
Curiosity about people's private lives is misplaced. Be comfortable not knowing many things and pursue one thing.
Half of knowledge
'I don't know' is half of knowledge. Be comfortable with lack of knowledge and with dying not knowing much.
Access to knowledge
His shaykh said the most beautiful thing is access to all knowledge in the next life.
Competition is allowed
Competing in good, drawing near to Allah, is fine because the intention is to improve, as long as you do not derive value.
Danger: value from closeness to Allah
The scariest source. Knowing this protects you from tazkiyah turning into arrogance.
The hill story
A sinner going up and a pious person coming down. One was drawn closer, the other lost love of himself as Allah removed it.
Look at others with humility
I am not better. I was given more, so I have more responsibility. Make dua for others.
Question for next week
If you feel equal, should you hope people do better than you? Do the opposite test: if the opposite sounds bad, the question is good.
The third option
Stop concerning yourself with their path. Assume good, wish good, focus on your own problems.
Homework
What would help you hope good for them? Think about it.

L.title: The pause
obj: Set the revision rhythm: each topic returns every two weeks, and abstract values need time to seep in through reflection and practice.
Re-teach the pause before salah and add one Fatiha theme to contemplate while reciting.
Re-teach ithar-style awareness: notice the nafs leaping for dunya in small moments so you can recognize it in complex ones.
Re-teach the act of service you dislike: do it until you stop disliking it, not until you like it.
Show how to handle disappointment and difficulty: do not carry people in your mind, learn the lesson, take the test as a sign Allah still cares.
Set expectations: think, try and fail before asking, because this teaches skills and methods, not answers.
topics: Two weeks per topic
He gives two weeks between returns to the same topic so you can really contemplate it.
Values seep in slowly
Abstract concepts need reflection and practice before they become real values. Values are like gold that people grow up with, you can acquire them but it takes time.
Why salah is the focus
Mistakes in salah are held against you, so small increments of improvement matter. Two practices at a time.
The pause before salah
A moment before takbir because most people carry the same thought straight in.
Why it is hard
Pausing means ending the thought. The nafs wants to continue it, and waiting for the thought to finish is not feasible in jama'ah.
Intention and not-intending
Intending prayer also means intending not to be distracted by other things.
Take a note
He sometimes writes notes down to release a thought before prayer.
Centralize
Put everything on pause, take a deep breath or two. Over time it becomes second nature.
Salah as time out
The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to find it a relief from worries. 'Give us rest with it, Bilal'.
Do it for the five fard prayers
Even if you cannot for sunnah, give three to ten seconds before takbir, and before wudu.
Do not enter distracted
Enter at least with focus. Start on the right foot.
Anxiety and heart rate
Pausing a stressful thought calms adrenaline and heart rate. Your future will not be lost in five minutes.
Running scenarios in bed
Replaying anger at night harms the body. Contemplation is brain-led, emotions running scenarios cannot be stopped.
Add a Fatiha theme
Pick one of the seven themes of Al-Fatiha, like hamd or guidance, and think about it. The dua in the Fatiha is the easiest.
Repeat the surah if needed
If you read and thought nothing, read it again and find at least one point.
Speed bumps
The goal is to slow down so you can find joy in salah.
Question: contemplating behind the imam
Contemplation is not recitation, you can stay on one thought while the imam moves on, and rejoin.
Next steps
Habitualize pause and contemplation. In two weeks two more points are added.
Practices as controlled experiments
Isolate one feeling at a time to learn about yourself and fix it.
Practice 1: the leaping nafs
When you race for a door, a parking spot or free food, feel the leap and recognize selfishness.
Story of the bus door
A brother stood to enter the bus first and let everyone on. The teacher says not to do that, just recognize the leap.
Bookmark the feeling
The same feeling shows up in complex moments where you can spin the story as right.
Awareness, acknowledgement, accountability
Those three words are the method.
Take it, but slow down
If you want the parking spot, take it, but notice how un-calm you were before.
Not yet joy
Enjoying giving way comes later. Now only recognition and calming.
Every fight club rule: it is about you
Never project tazkiyah onto others. Focus on self-awareness, not other people.
Spinning the story
You can argue your point so well that everyone believes you demand it for the right reason, while inside it was just the nafs.
Redo with this insight
If you stopped, restart, scaling back the small fights.
Practice 2: service you dislike
Choose a small service to others you dislike and do it until you stop disliking it. Not liking, just stop disliking.
Doing the dishes
The most common example. It requires skills you must find yourself.
Return and tell me
If you come back saying you did it, he assumes you stopped disliking it. If you still hate it you have not learned.
Make it less annoying
He used to hate school drop-offs and now Mondays are among his favorite. You must go out of your way to find methods.
How often
At least once every two or three days. Weekly is too infrequent to feel change.
Goal: indifferent
If you end up enjoying it that defeats the purpose of this small exercise.
Recording noise
From about 37:00 to 53:00 the audio is mostly noise, an Arabic recitation of Surat ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh (around 42:55 to 45:16) and unrelated speech.
Think, try, fail, then ask
He wants mature questions. No answers, only skills and methods. He leaves things out on purpose to see what you can figure out.
Do not stop asking
You may reach out. If it shows no effort, he will say so.
Personal story: disappointment
Medical oncologist, rejected more times than hairs on his head. Rejection by outcomes does not bother him. What bothers him is being naive and not having a plan B.
Do not carry people
Preoccupation continues the harm. Deal with it, learn, make a plan, hold yourself accountable and move on.
Joy in difficulty
A scholar's saying: I am happier with a difficulty than a blessing, because a blessing may be istidraj but a difficulty shows He still cares.
A test is a sign of worth
Say alhamdulillah, bring your A game, be self-accountable, grateful and patient.
Perspective
On the pediatric oncology ward you know what a test is. He walks out happy since everything else is small.
Pray for ease
You ask Allah for ease but when difficulty comes, keep that in mind.
Assignment for two weeks
1. Recognize the nafs leaping. 2. An act of service you dislike. 3. Pause before salah and contemplate one Fatiha point. The third exercise is postponed.

L.title: Vanity and envy
obj: Recap the pendulum and self-value: why vanity and arrogance sit on one swing with low self-esteem.
Answer the two homework questions: why does the nafs compare, and should we hope others do better than us.
Define vanity (ujb) as seeing yourself, and arrogance (kibr) as seeing yourself above others.
Teach hamd (praise of Allah) as the cure for vanity and give the right way to celebrate success.
Show how vanity stops you trying your best and makes feedback devastating, and why mediocrity is fine.
Introduce Iblis as the model of arrogance and set up concentration practice for salah.
topics: Confidence and the pendulum
He uses the diagram again. The ends of the pendulum are vanity and arrogance on one side and low self-esteem on the other.
Why it matters
Both extremes can ruin you. Self-value is what feeds it, and the only true source is that Allah created you with an innate, divine value.
The nafs wants something more exciting
It inflates self-value from external, variable sources that can just as easily deflate it.
Swing leads to breakdown
Mental breakdowns, severe depression and anxiety come from letting it swing.
Cut the sources and reattach
Keep detaching from external sources until the idea of constant, divine value sinks in.
Two layers of belief
What you tell people you believe versus what you really believe. Your life shows the second.
Iman needs time to sink
It takes contemplation, practice and changed behavior. Nodding is not enough.
Filling in the gaps
We do it because we feel threatened and take value from comparison. We make excuses for those more successful than us.
Double standard
You give yourself excuses for their success but not excuses for others when you want to feel more.
Stop sizing people up
If you stop, you stop needing excuses. Assume good, or better, do not assume, and spend the time on your own inside.
Tazkiyah turns the telescope inward
What you need to clean up is inside. Everything else you cannot control.
Q1: Why does the nafs compare?
A student: it feels secure when it is better. Answer: it gets self-value from comparison.
Stop comparing and feel lighter
Compare yourself to yourself, your own standards and principles.
Be genuinely happy for others
You can only do that once you stop comparing. Otherwise you fake a smile and burn inside.
Happy for them yet wanting better for yourself
Possible. The difference is wanting to achieve without wanting them to fail.
Question: how is this different from hasad
Hasad is showing happiness but not being happy. It comes from not accepting that others should be ahead.
Role models
Aim to be like someone, and do not want them to fail.
Q2: Should others do better than us?
Team player vs selfish player analogy from the class.
Ego exercise
A student wishes the best for others to put the ego down. Teacher: better if the ego is not fighting you at all.
Everyone has their own story
Wish them the best and serve them. Live your own story.
Hoping to be the worst in the group
A well-known teaching: if you are the best in the room, find a better room. Hope for companionship with better people so you get lifted on the Day of Judgment.
Wanting people behind you
That is an insecure, bruised ego and comes from deriving value from comparisons.
Compare to your past self
A student suggests it. Teacher: that is purposeful self-assessment, comparing to others is a psychological struggle.
Competition done right
Work on yourself to be the best but do not mind if someone else achieves it. An ego-inflating competition makes you a bitter loser.
Vanity and arrogance as the top two
The deadliest diseases of the heart in the Quran and Sunnah.
Vanity vs arrogance
Vanity is seeing yourself in the mirror. Arrogance is seeing yourself above others, so it needs other people.
Qarun as vanity
The Quran tells him not to be vain: 'La tafrah'. He said, I got it because of knowledge I have.
Entitlement
I worked hard, I deserve it. Feeling you deserve every good thing but nothing hard.
Confidence vs vanity
Confidence: Allah put potential in me and I trust His khayr. Vanity: the spotlight is on me.
How he sees others and himself
When others succeed he says mashaAllah, enjoy your moment. For himself he sees Allah's facilitation: intelligence, opportunity, time, ability.
The cure is hamd
Where is the spotlight? Allah is worthy of praise.
Question: is it wrong to celebrate?
No. Celebrate the blessing of Allah, not 'I did it'.
Credit is tiny
Your body and soul are owned by Allah. Take a very small amount of credit, it could have gone wrong infinitely many ways.
Alhamdulillah
The tool to hold vanity down. Say it as you achieve.
Entitlement again
Entitlement is the beginning of a long fall. He gives the example of Iblis starting with a little vanity: I deserve this.
It is rude to claim credit
Everything I use and am comes from Him.
Are vanity and arrogance linked?
A student: vanity leads to needing to validate by putting others down. Teacher: they become one mush, and the swing is hard to separate.
Confidence vs vanity is a slither
A small piece of perspective that is not fully right.
Vanity stops effort
You protect a self-image so you do not try your best. You would find out you are mediocre.
Your best is probably mediocre
We are all mediocre. Practice makes it better. Rare freaks of talent aside, everyone fails a million times.
Feedback hurts the vain
Medical students are ripped to shreds and if value comes from being a good student it breaks you.
Accountability vs self-worth
Feel bad that you did not try hard enough. Do not question your worth.
Imposter syndrome
Most people live with it because they derive value from their work.
Public speaking
You will suck at first. Take the points, try again, fail again, hone your skills.
Being okay with mediocre
You may not be number one. I am mediocre at best and okay with that.
When you look in the mirror
Vanity vs the opposite swing, 'I am such a loser'. Confidence looks to Allah.
Arrogance
How I view myself in comparison. My core is just better, I just have not had the time.
Iblis story
Iblis refused: I am fire, he is mud, I earned a spot among the angels. Who of you earned a spot?
Would you defy a direct command of Allah?
Class says no. He replies that Iblis thought the same. The point is to learn from the story.
Wudu and distraction
Lessen distraction during wudu, sit, close your eyes and focus.
Concentration
Attention spans are short and we live in the past or future. The prayer is for being in the moment.
Being centered
The Prophet (peace be upon him) was always centered. Salah brings you back to the present, which makes reflection healthier.

L.title: Pause before prayer
obj: Explain why this halaqa exists: every Muslim needs a method of creed, a method of fiqh and a method of suluk (tazkiyah), and the third is the neglected one.
Debrief the pause and the Fatiha contemplation: closing eyes, priming with a verse, doing the pause before takbir not after.
Teach why we pause with the idea of ihram: you are entering a different realm for a few minutes.
Teach how to deal with the day's problems: set aside time to sort them instead of carrying them into prayer.
Teach ruku' as a physical transition and add the new practice of thinking of Allah as the Exalted when saying subhana rabbiyal 'azim.
Debrief the service-you-dislike exercise: satisfaction, appreciation, self-imposed expectations, and the joy of giving.
Assign du'a for someone you envy or dislike.
topics: Revision plan
Four categories, two at a time, two weeks between each. Today's categories are rituals and the second one.
Why we do all this
Every Muslim needs three methods: aqidah, fiqh and suluk.
Method of creed (aqidah)
You need a way to make sense of attributes, free will and qadr. It shapes how you understand events in your life and the world.
Method of fiqh
How to pray, fast, pay zakah and hajj, where you get rulings. Study at least one school to have a reference.
Method of suluk is the neglected one
This is tazkiyah: purifying the heart, connecting to Allah, understanding value and ethics.
There are different ways
He is not saying his is the only one. It is the way that makes sense to him and he offers it.
Here you are stuck with me
You can choose a madhhab or creed, but almost no one has studied every suluk path. A lifetime to learn one.
The destination is one
In Syria the Rifa'i and Shadhili ways were prominent. He took pieces of both. The core here is love.
Laymen follow their imam
That is fine, but you are here to learn to teach and lead with clarity.
Why he runs this halaqa
Suluk is taught sporadically in his other halaqat and can go unnoticed. Here the goal is to remove distraction and focus on you.
You need a teacher
Studying suluk or fiqh alone you get lost.
Needed most in the West
Wealth and leisure create heart problems. It is available elsewhere if you look.
Debrief: pause and Fatiha
A student found the pause hard to keep up. Another loses focus in the second raka'ah.
Closing the eyes
Scholars differ but it is not worth an argument. If it helps your focus, do it for now.
Prime with a verse
A student runs a verse in his head before the pause to remember it.
Seven themes of Fatiha
The teacher offers to share them again.
The niyyah and the pause
The pause is before takbir, not after. Niyyah is a pillar of salah for most schools.
Ihram analogy
Ihram is a place and a time. You cross a line, change clothes and give up usual things. Salah is a similar zone.
Die in salah
Dying in Fajr, ruku' or sujud is the best state to be taken in.
The meeting analogy
Imagine sitting with someone for half an hour on your phone. That is how we enter salah without knowing who we speak to.
Qiblah as a reminder
You face the first house of worship, the Lord of all humanity.
Training wheels
These increments are not a permanent solution. Over time other things get fixed.
Q: dealing with the day's problems
Set aside time to sort work, family and relationship problems. Closing a problem feels satisfying.
If it is always fires
Something is wrong with how you run things. The occasional emergency is normal.
Third practice: ruku'
Physical transitions facilitate mental ones.
Standing, bowing, prostration
Standing is a student reciting to the teacher with head held high. Bowing historically established the king and the peasant. Do not recite Quran in ruku'.
Subhana rabbiyal 'azim
You are coaching your nafs: I am not equal to Allah and I do not blame Him.
When the nafs says why me
If you trained yourself in salah, the tasbih kicks in when hardship hits.
Surah story of Isa
'Subhanaka' in the Quran is used when something is outrageous. Jesus is asked whether he told people to take him and his mother as gods.
Thinking of Allah as exalted
He is not questioned about what He does. I am the one questioned. Do it for ten seconds.
Assignment: ruku'
For two weeks think of Allah being exalted before and during ruku'.
Recording noise
From about 30:47 to 33:22 there is chatter, music and rainbow talk. No teaching.
Debrief: service you dislike
A student: seeing the clean place gives satisfaction. You look forward to the feeling.
Appreciation changes relationships
When people appreciate your small act it takes away negativity and you stop disliking it.
Being bothered by expectations
Another student is bothered when his mother reminds him. Teacher: you obligated yourself, so a reminder should not bother you.
Why it bothers you
Maybe your intention drifted to the person, or you assume how they should see what you do.
Reminder of salah
Someone reminding you of prayer should not bother you since you held yourself to it.
Why you care how they see you
Your problem is with an assumption of how they should see you.
Do not stop
Unless the schedule changes, do not stop a service that costs you nothing.
Am I better than them?
A student found a feeling of being better. After reflection he said we are the same.
The joy of giving is addictive
Philosophers agree on this. Learn the joy of serving with no strings attached.
Transactions are fine
Just tell the other person it is a transaction. Do not claim it is for Allah and then cash in.
Arrogance will creep in
After serving selflessly the nafs will say I am better than the others in the house. Cut off value again, that is why humbleness comes first.
Fatherhood and expectations
Children expect you to provide. Learn now that you obligated yourself and you do it for Allah.
Humans should see it as their right
Hold yourself accountable. Whether people have the right to expect from you is not your business.
Assignment: du'a
For two weeks make du'a for someone you envy or dislike, a regular person, not the extremes. Really mean it.
Heart opener
It is eye-opening the first time. He will tell his story next time.

L.title: Mistakes and arrogance
obj: Finish the Iblis case study: the lesson is not that he was stupid but that arrogance can grow into a monster that defies Allah and refuses a way out.
Show that saying 'I would never do that' is itself arrogance, since you do not know your circumstances, your breaking point or Allah's knowledge of you.
Replace it with gratitude for what Allah kept you from, and a plea that He keep you safe.
Link arrogance to comparison, racism as collective arrogance, and the sneakiest forms (intelligence, religiosity).
Give the remedy: serve everyone and go out of your way to show humility, which also tests whether the nafs is attached.
Add a small practice for group dhikr: do not count, just say it and enjoy it.
topics: Recap: Iblis and the trick question
Last time he asked 'would you ever defy a direct command of Allah?' as a trick.
Grateful that Allah prevented you
A student says he is grateful Allah kept him from mistakes. Teacher: hold on to that.
Companions' story
A group wished they had been with the Prophet. You cannot say you would have stayed.
Thinking you are better is arrogance
Even if you see a person's flaws and say you would never do that.
Generational arrogance
'My generation would never do this' is the same pattern.
Why was the question arrogant?
Do you have the ability to say with confidence that you would absolutely not have done it?
Leave the credit to Allah
Whatever small contribution you made, let Allah judge if it is praiseworthy.
You assume you understand
You do not know what it was like to be him.
Not a public topic
It can sound like excusing Iblis. He is not excusing him, he is teaching you not to repeat it.
The right answer is inshaAllah
If I am put in that position, I ask Allah to help me not to defy.
Iblis had a reason
He was still wrong, but he was not 'just an idiot'. He could choose, like you.
Part two of the mistake
After the first mistake he was offered a way out and refused. A student says the second part is much harder to imagine.
The monster inside
The lesson of Iblis is you can build a monster inside you so powerful it will defy Allah.
Dismissing it repeats his mistake
Saying 'no, I'm better than that' puts you in the same trap, closer than before.
Rahma for everyone
We hold people accountable but keep basic mercy.
Doubling down
Arrogance makes you take it to Jahannam rather than admit you were wrong. People today destroy things to avoid admitting mistakes.
Two ways to look
1. Be grateful you have not done this. 2. Say inshaAllah, and ask Allah for strength.
You will be tested
Your ego will be tested with someone you despise when you must be fair or admit fault.
We sugarcoat
Iblis had no way to sugarcoat since God spoke to him directly. We rationalize.
A little fear
When you see someone fall, ask Allah to protect you from what your nafs could do.
Is it harder with age and status?
He is not sure, but the bigger you make it the harder it is to get rid of. Life pokes holes in the balloon.
Keep the pendulum in the middle
Confident in the potential Allah gave you, humble in how you see others.
The hypothetical in the Quran
Allah says what would have happened if the Confederates entered Medina. Only Allah knows hypotheticals.
Only Allah knows what you would have done
That is the scary part.
Movie analogy
Trading Places: swapping a CEO and a homeless man shows how much is circumstances.
A small amount is me
Who judges whether your effort is praiseworthy? Allah.
I am not justifying anyone
If someone's mistake harms others you still stand against it.
Two parts of a crime
Act and intent. Umar suspended the hadd for theft in the year of famine.
Even Adam and Iblis
Ask the same: would you have eaten from the tree?
Positives only go up
You do not want to be seen as less than you are, so you say 'I wouldn't'.
Semantics matter
'I would never' is arrogant. 'I pray I never make this mistake' is humble.
Hudhayfa and the Trench
The Prophet asked who would bring intel and nobody volunteered. A tabi'i said they would have carried the Prophet on their shoulders. Hudhayfa said you did not live what we lived.
What they should have said
InshaAllah we would have stood with the Prophet. Try to live a life that proves it.
Humbleness
Imagine that in another circumstance your response is not as confident as you think.
Everyone has a breaking point
Only Allah knows yours. Use free time to strengthen yourself so it is far away.
Allah is holding tests back
He gives you time to strengthen your iman. Iblis failed the test and is accountable.
Focus on yourself
You have no time to assume things about others.
Personal difficulty
It was hard to say 'I do not know' about someone he knew whose act was horrific.
What swings the pendulum here?
Comparison again, plus racism as collective arrogance.
Why racism is so evil
You think a whole race is innately lesser and can never be you.
Iblis went all in
He was offered a way out, instead he doubled down like a poker all-in.
Scared into focus
The story is meant to scare you. Not one bit of arrogance is allowed.
Good deeds can be poisoned
Vanity and arrogance can make deeds worthless, so he must teach this first.
Comparing is dumb
Starting points and tools differ. The only fair comparison is effort, which only Allah can judge.
Five million steps behind
Maybe you are five million steps behind me but above me because of the effort it took you.
Prayer here: do not be distracted
A companion kept praying when a wall fell. He did not count, so he is not responsible for the number.
Dhikr: do not count
Just say it and enjoy it. The leader carries the counting.
Subhanallah wa bihamdihi
The practice stays at the basic words for now.
Brick vs pendulum
Adding things to the brick (your value) makes it swing. Each swing goes farther until you reach Firawn.
Firawn's swing
Frequency and distance of swings makes a narcissist. Firawn said I am your highest lord.
The sneaky ones
The nafs says I do not derive value from wealth or status but I am smarter.
Intelligence story
At 21 he met a friend, now a doctor in Detroit, much smarter than him.
Religiosity
Deriving value from being a better Muslim than others destroys baraka. It also causes envy of those closer to Allah.
How it shows up
You feel threatened by someone more guided instead of learning from them.
The remedy: service
Walk around thinking they may be closer to Allah than me. Serve everyone and give salams.
Do it deliberately
Smile, greet, get to know, say something nice, ask what you can do to help.
Test your nafs
If the nafs gets standoffish when you greet someone, fix it.
Service as the test
The Prophet served everyone. You cannot know if you are attached without testing.

L.title: Resentment and gratitude
obj: Explain tasbih as the core of aqidah: exalting Allah, never blaming Him or attributing flaws to Him, and why only a Muslim understanding of tasbih is complete.
Show how the nafs refuses blame and how the lens of tasbih lets you accept hardship with gratitude.
Add the fourth salah practice: when you rise from ruku' say sami'a Allahu liman hamidah, and think of a blessing each time.
Teach hamd as unconditional praise, the antidote to 'ujb (vanity), distinct from gratitude.
Debrief du'a for someone you dislike: why it is hard, what the nafs fears, and how to humanize.
Assign the next practice: a list of 50 sins to mention in istighfar, one for every two repetitions.
topics: Why this is unique to Islam
Every prophet taught it, but other faiths today do not have the same understanding of Allah's perfection.
Aqidah course
Attend it within the next year or two. It gives a method of creed that lets you function with other Muslims.
What the quarrels are about
Every theological school accuses the others of not exalting Allah properly. It is the same goal.
Personal tasbih
Do not blame Allah, question His wisdom or accuse Him of imperfection when things go badly.
The nafs refuses blame
Look at children. Almost no one says 'it is my fault'. The nafs is committed to you not being at fault.
When nobody is to blame
If life turns south, the trained subhana rabbiyal 'azim kicks in: I am in His debt.
A thought versus a blow
A rude thought is not sinful. He fears the blow strong enough to move past a thought. A scholar thanked Allah each hardship that his religion was not taken.
Tasbih becomes your lens
You become fine with whatever Allah gives, even if difficult.
The mindset of being tested
You expect hardship. He quotes Surat al-'Ankabut: do people think they will be left to say we believe and not be tested?
Teachers' optimism
They were more optimistic with hardship because it showed that Allah still cared.
Tasbih is a process
It starts with understanding and takes time.
How other texts speak of God
Old Testament depictions are offensive to a Muslim, like God sulking and fighting Jacob.
The white student story
A 50 year old student attending for a world religions class described God as frustrated with his face in his hands. He was shocked. That is not how we speak of Allah.
Synonyms
Taqdis, ta'zim and tanzih all mean exalting Allah.
Do the exercises
He is considering turning it into a workshop. Knowledge without action is scary.
Your own difficulties
Some are generic, others specific to your nafs. He can only help if you try and fail.
Practices recap
Pause before salah. A Fatiha theme. In ruku' something about tasbih that is meaningful or that you struggle to understand, like death or wars.
Tasbih becomes joy
After a while you say it with joy since everything points to Allah's perfection.
Aqidah course timing
It runs May to August every year.
Fourth practice: qawmah
Standing after ruku': sami'a Allahu liman hamidah, rabbana wa lakal hamd.
Praise is not the same as gratitude
Gratitude is conditional on a blessing, praise is deserved regardless. Allah is Al-Hamid.
There is always something to be grateful for
If you cannot see it, there is a disease inside. You exist, which you can never repay.
Think of a simple blessing each time
Not the big ones. Your eyes, ears, health, being Muslim. Try not to repeat the same one every prayer.
Dawud's alhamdulillah
Dawud asked how to thank Allah for the ability to thank. Allah said now you understand. It goes on forever.
Why you stand for hamd
You do not praise your provider dressed like trash. Standing tall shows His care over you.
Hamd is the antidote to 'ujb
Where is the spotlight? On Allah.
Salah fixes the diseases of the heart
Ruku' tasbih, hamd and others each treat one. Hamd removes 'ujb.
'Ujb vs riya'
'Ujb is vain self-praise. Riya' is wanting attention for what you do. They are intertwined.
Pull one thread at a time
Diseases of the heart are tangled so you remove them one at a time.
Salah assignment recap
Pause, takbir with focus, one Fatiha theme, ruku' thought, and a blessing at hamd.
Debrief: du'a for someone you dislike
One student found he did not hate them that much once he broke down what they did.
Humanizing
Seeing them as human as you are.
Why can't you make du'a for them?
A student: it is against my interests and I do not care. Teacher: why not? Do you care that Allah guides people?
Not about oppressors
This is a regular person who mistreated you.
Is it destiny?
A student says harm was predestined. Teacher: it is a useful view but the person is still accountable.
He does not ask you to forgive
Only to make du'a and mean it.
Why it is hard
The fear that the du'a works and the person rises. The nafs says they should stay garbage.
This person does not know you
Your struggle is with yourself.
Connection between harm and du'a
What does being harmed have to do with your ability to ask Allah's generosity for them?
His football story
A malicious tackle ended his career in Syria with three knee surgeries. It took him a month to make du'a.
How he humanized him
He imagined his childhood, struggles and dreams. Later the player became a friend, stays at his parents' house, and did not remember the tackle.
Do not let them add to your burden
The hurt already happened. Excuses, the bigger picture or qadar can relieve it like popping a balloon.
It has to make sense first
If it seems illogical, say so. It is not illogical, since it aligns with your values.
Du'a for someone in absentia
An angel says ameen and the same for you.
Nafs does not want them to be better
That is deriving value from comparison and being stingy with guidance you do not own.
A student's wider du'a struggle
He has trouble making du'a at all because he is unsure it will be accepted. One of four outcomes: now, later, better, or the Hereafter.
Next practice: istighfar
When you say astaghfirullah, think of fifty sins and write them down. Every two repetitions for one sin.

L.title: Boundaries
obj: Ground humbleness in real examples: where in your own life do you need to humble yourself.
Show that praise and fame are the other pull on the pendulum and how to resist them: do not let others' assumptions change what you know about yourself.
Teach how to respond when someone is arrogant, rude or racist toward you: it should not move your self-value, and you respond from equality, not weakness or arrogance.
Define anger as the response to a threatened self-value, with fear on the other side, and note that children can tell discipline from venting.
Introduce boundaries as self-preservation: know your breaking point, walk away, calm down and respond rationally.
Assign: identify your boundaries and breaking points.
topics: Ask for personal examples
Where do you personally feel you need to humble yourself. Give something real, not idealistic.
A new job
You will be put in your place, so you must be humble to learn.
Two people do not learn
An Arabic proverb: the arrogant and the shy. One will not ask and the other cannot accept being told.
Teaching children
Seeing kids misbehave, you may say 'I would never'. His being a bad kid helps him judge less. Humbleness mellows you.
Learning from a colleague
A student's first reaction is 'you don't know what you are talking about'. Being taught does not make anyone superior.
What does praise multiplied by a million become?
Fame and popularity, where the pendulum wants to swing.
Famous footballer
Take the praise and hand it back to Allah. The blessing is from Him.
Do not let someone's assumption change your facts
Praise or insult, you know yourself better.
Firawn
He knew he was human but people kept saying he was godly. Musa told him to wake up.
Know your credit
You know how much of your achievement is due to you and how much to Allah.
Barbecue example
People tell you how to cook for a meal you planned for a week. Humbleness lets you not take it personally.
Avoid being triggered
People who get triggered are hard to work with and escalate. Humble people absorb it and keep things moving.
Correcting younger relatives
It is hard when correcting a cousin without feeling above them.
Critique from someone who loves you
Humbleness helps you take it, they want the best for you.
When someone is arrogant toward you
How do you respond? A student says he would not fight back but wishes he had stood up honorably.
Is standing up about self-value?
If I stand up because my self-value is threatened, I have a problem. The why determines what honorable means.
Honorable means calm and confident
Not weak, not arrogant, not threatened.
Self-respect vs self-value
He says self-respect is vague. Self-value and boundaries are clear.
What decreases self-value
He adds aggressiveness: being called names or treated rudely. It makes the pendulum swing.
How people treat us
The missing source of self-value. If it stays on you for a week it feeds into your sense of self.
When it should matter
Parent, sibling, mentor or friend criticizing you, you care because you love them.
His childhood
Called the Arab boy in Canada, the Syrian in Saudi, the Canadian in Syria. Bullied from grade one to twelve.
Respond from equality
Not from weakness, not from arrogance. 'He started it' is a lame excuse.
Agree with the rude person
If you are self-critical, nothing they say is new.
They want to swing your pendulum
If you lose control and win the fight, they still won because they controlled your behavior.
Strength is self-control
The hadith: the strong one is the one who controls himself in anger.
The Prophet's boundary
Hind bin Abi Hala: he never got angry for himself but when someone transgressed against another, he intervened.
What is wrong with them?
See their rudeness as a disease. No one with a sound heart does this.
Boundaries vs the pendulum
Responding when the pendulum is in the middle is rational. Responding when it has swung is emotional.
Anger is a threatened self-value
As a father: am I angry for his sake or because he disrespected me? Children sense the difference.
Fear on the other side
Fear makes you regret not speaking. A pendulum in the middle gives a response you will not regret.
What if someone obliterates a boundary?
A student's hotel room story. Boundaries exist for self-preservation.
A boundary is a line before your breaking point
Boundaries get closer to zero with time.
Prophet and the debtor
A man demanded repayment rudely. The Prophet's companions wanted to punish him but he was patient and told them to pay and give more.
Insecure people
Their self-value is fragile, so they need to put you in your place immediately.
Physical aggression
A man grabbed the Prophet's cloak and pulled so it left a mark. The Prophet told them to give him what he wanted.
Bring the pendulum back
Calm down, respond when not angry. Do not respond to arrogance with arrogance.
Saudi school years
He used to prepare comebacks with poetry. It made him think badly of a whole population.
Be strong enough to be gentle
A voice actor's brother's advice quoted by a student.
Village story
Two villages with no real line between them, both claiming the other are idiots. Superiority never ends.
If you are confident and humble
You will regret very few things. Regret comes from responding when the pendulum swung.
Elevator story
An old man made racial remarks. He later gave him a ride at night and he never said anything bad again. Not everyone will change.
They provoke because of an emptiness
He will explain why people provoke, and you should know why you do it too.
Action item: boundaries
Think about your boundaries and breaking points. Put a boundary right before the breaking point.
Walk away, calm down, respond
Do not ignore, just wait until you are rational.
Boundaries are not permanent
Work to make them less broad so it is harder to get to you.
Sticks and stones
The idea is valuable: do not let it take away anything from you.
Recording after the lesson
Mostly casual conversation, Quran recitation (Al-Fatiha appears around 56:57) and noise. No teaching.

L.title: Counting sins
obj: Teach self-solving: when an exercise fails, find the root cause and try something new before asking for help.
Explain that the small salah adjustments are only training wheels, the full fix comes from tazkiyah and cleansing the heart.
Add the fifth salah practice: make at least one du'a in sujud, understanding du'a as a conversation and documentation, not a genie lamp.
Teach why du'a is therapeutic and how a mature person asks for less dunya and for what is best.
Explain the 50 sins exercise: the number you can list depends on your sensitivity to Allah, and istighfar is for all the ways you fall short.
Teach raising standards gradually, not in one jump, and assign tawbah from one modest sin with its four conditions.
topics: Alternating schedule
Sisters and brothers are on an alternating system. He wants to fix it so both groups cover the same material.
Review of last sessions
Humbleness and praise, then boundaries and breaking points.
One more practice for salah
Pause, Fatiha contemplation, ruku', hamd. Who is struggling?
Student struggles
One says he cannot pray if not locked in beforehand. Another freezes on a verse and loses the rest.
Solve it yourself
