If you wait until someone tells you the fix, it will not work. This is lifelong self-awareness, self-accountability and self-correction.
Medicine analogy
A student presents the history and labs, a resident also gives a plan. Come in with what you tried.
Find the root cause
Put on the oxygen mask, dive deep, try something new. Otherwise I will die and you will be stuck.
Training wheels
The full fix for salah comes from tazkiyah, cleansing the heart, and finding tranquility in hamd, istighfar and Quran. It takes time.
Summary of practices so far
Pause, one Fatiha point, tasbih in ruku', gratitude at hamd.
Fifth practice: sujud
A hadith: when prostrating, make a lot of du'a, it is worthy of being answered.
Why sujud for du'a
Putting the most dignified part, your face, on the ground. You are defenseless.
The Aladdin's lamp complex
Du'a is not a genie that grants a new car or job. It is a phone call, keeping the line alive.
The Prophet at Ta'if
Bleeding from his feet he made a du'a: I complain of my weakness. As long as You are not angry with me, I do not mind.
Maryam's mother
'My Lord I have given birth to a girl.' She is speaking to Allah. Du'a is verbalizing.
Du'a as documentation
Like a medical note. Thoughts do not count until said or done. You put on record why you want things.
Waraqa ibn Nawfal
He told the Prophet he would be his supporter if he lived and died soon after. It was recorded.
Du'a is not only requests
Ya'qub said I complain of my sorrow to Allah. It is different from complaining about Him.
Take off your masks
Be honest and self-aware. You are not in a job interview. Face on the ground you are begging.
Prophet's quick descent
He went quickly to sujud because the rest was done well and now he opens his heart.
Assignment: one du'a in each sujud
At least one, anything you want.
Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b
He waited at the Prophet's door to help with wudu and slept. The Prophet said ask. He thought and asked for companionship in Jannah.
As you mature, ask for less dunya
You do not know what is best, so ask for good and acceptance.
No one makes du'a for haram
If you want something wrong, you may say 'I want this but I do not want to want it'.
Du'a is therapeutic
Do not go down, touch your forehead and say nothing.
Do not only ask in hardship
Do not treat Allah like a psychotherapist you see in need.
Repeating the same 10 du'as
That is fine and shows who you are. His own du'as: parents, teachers, children, repentance, a good ending, halal, ability to keep teaching, benefit for those he helps.
Ask for the diseases of the heart to go
If you have arrogance, vanity or ostentation, ask Allah to remove them.
Ritual structure
Dhikr, Quran and du'a, so you make du'a at least twice a day. Not only the last ten nights of Ramadan.
Debrief: list of 50 sins
He asks how many came up with 50. Nobody. Try now, on your phone.
Write what is worthy of istighfar
The Prophet said it a hundred times a day. Our lives are full of things worthy of it.
Sin judged by sensitivity
The less sensitive you are to the One you are accountable to, the fewer sins you see. The more sensitive, the more you see.
Fajr in jama'ah
For some it is a good day if they prayed Fajr. For others it is not if they lacked khushu'.
Every prayer is worthy of istighfar
Quality and intention are lacking. That is why you say astaghfirullah after salah.
Counting becomes easy
Raise your standard and 100 comes easy. When you first try you can only write 10 or 15.
Self-accountability
Accepting a low standard from yourself and a high one from others is a bad equation.
Raise standards gradually
People who go full speed hold it two or three weeks then collapse. Go from 0 to 1 to 2.
Habits take time
A rehab facility removes you from your environment, which is not always possible.
Greatest sin: satisfaction with yourself
A saying quoted in Arabic: the mother of sins is being pleased with yourself.
There is a standard
The Prophet is the standard, so not infinite.
Fasting and sunnah
Are you sensitive to the sunnah and blessings? Expect more from yourself since you expect so much from Allah.
Do your best
Your limits are way beyond what you think. The cap is artificial and social.
Fasting 30 days
You can fast 30 days in summer and still function, which shows your capacity.
Too critical?
He is not worried about you being too critical. If it happens, hold yourself to the Prophet's standard.
The point of 50 sins
A small change of perspective takes you from counting 10 to counting a million. It keeps you improving.
The person who does tazkiyah
Whenever you meet them they are a few steps ahead.
Assignment: tawbah
Choose one modest sin, not flimsy and not a long entrenched one. Perform tawbah.
Elements of tawbah
1. Regret, with no nostalgia. 2. Stop. 3. Intention not to return. 4. If you took a right, return it.
Backbiting
Do an act of kindness and retract it in the same kind of gathering. Preferably do not tell the person, as it harms the relationship.
Why harm leaves accountability
Harming people leaves you to find ways to make up for it. Make du'a for them and do good.

L.title: Boundaries and control
obj: Collect more examples of where humbleness matters: creative work, compliments, religiosity, seeking knowledge, receiving feedback.
Teach that you learn more from people who dislike you, and how to take harsh feedback without defensiveness.
Explain why boundaries are needed alongside humbleness, with early scholars as extreme examples of selflessness.
Define a boundary as a place where your self-value is still fed by something, so the pendulum swings and anger shows up.
Name control as the big hidden theme: you control only yourself, and being bothered by lack of control reveals arrogance.
Assign: examples of loss of control that provoke anger.
topics: Recap
Humbleness examples, then boundaries, then anger.
Examples of humbleness
Most people said when you are mistreated.
Creative circles
You compare with others. You find your creativity is not as magical as you thought and only learn if you take criticism.
His first poetry
His shaykh ripped it apart and told him to throw it out. Without humbleness this can crush you.
Compliments
Be bulletproof so praise does not enter your self-value bucket. Do not use compliments to dismiss correction.
Listen to yourself
Not to praise or criticism. You know the truth.
Be careful with religiosity
It is the worst source of arrogance, especially around people less practicing or knowledgeable.
Seeking knowledge
Without humbleness you cannot learn. You only learn from packaging you are willing to accept.
Learn from your enemies
A person who dislikes you gives information no one else will. There is always something for you in every comment.
The famous
Not talking about people with hundreds of thousands of comments.
Friends soften the fall
Those who like you will not tell you the truth.
Do not get defensive
The first times you will not know how to respond. Get comfortable if you want to excel.
His public speaking
He started at 17 and has spoken 24 years. He got vicious feedback until the last two or three years. One shaykh told him he should only write.
Take every criticism as insight
Do not be defensive. He never became perfect but became bearable to listen to.
People stop telling you
Once you are known, only people who like you attend, so you lose feedback.
Invite feedback
It is the only chance to improve at scale. Otherwise you fail on a stage that matters.
May Allah have mercy on one who gifted me my flaws
A saying of Umar. A humble person wants correction.
Boundaries and humbleness
Without clear boundaries, humbleness can lead you wrong.
Early scholars with no boundaries
Stories of imams so selfless that nothing bothered them. The Prophet only intervened when others or Islam were offended.
Ibrahim ibn Adham story
A soldier hit his head. He offered it again: this head that disobeys Allah deserves it.
Aim for genuine humility
Not artificial reminders. Your self-value must become stable.
What a boundary means
You know where your weaknesses are, like temper. Make it smaller over time.
Eggshell people
People with huge boundaries are stressful to be around. Humble people are easygoing and forgiving.
Identify when you fail to stay humble
Stay out of those situations while you work to defuse it.
Anger (ghadab)
Part of it is your emotional reaction when someone pushes a boundary and the pendulum swings.
Write your boundaries
Where you feel anger mixed with arrogance and say vicious, malicious things. Gaming is common.
What boundaries are
Self-value sources still feeding. Someone touches it, it swings, you get angry.
Move boundaries inward
Until they sit right on the source and disappear.
Huge boundaries give others leverage
Anything can swing you. They control your response.
Propaganda uses it
If I can predict your reaction I can set you up and reap the benefit even if you beat me. Collective version: a cartoon provoking violence.
Batman and the Joker
A student: Batman refusing to let the Joker control him.
Find why it bothers you
One answer is control.
Control
We like control but control very little. Tazkiyah teaches what you can control.
Student examples
Being interrupted, a father criticizing, lack of respect, unprovoked negative comments.
Repeatedly poked
If someone keeps hitting a boundary, decide whether to get bothered.
Is it really a boundary?
A boundary is where you lose control of yourself. Some bothers are not boundaries.
Why am I bothered?
Learn to pick out what bothers you and why.
Only Allah controls
He is the King. We are servants. We control our thoughts, feelings and behavior.
What's the problem with not controlling?
A student: guilt. Another: not knowing your place as a servant. A third: arrogance.
Humbleness is reality
You cannot control anything except your choices. You are under the bar, nothing else is.
Not even your children
Parents of teenagers come to this quickly. You can encourage and guide, not control.
His anger at his child
He was trying to control his destiny. Be okay with whatever path he chooses.
Control vs affect
You can affect them by guidance, rules while they are under you. You cannot control what they want or think.
Words to use
Guide, persuade, lead, inspire, mentor.
Being bothered by control
A student asks if being unhappy they do not listen is reasonable. Teacher: know why you are bothered.
Boundary vs pet peeve
Boundaries are where you feel you lack control of yourself and the pendulum swings.
Fix underneath
Nothing should be within your boundary but you are human.
Anger shows the swing
You may feel threatened, then arrogant, then condescending.
Control as a common hidden source
If humbleness is not clear you may think you control things you do not.
Assignment
Examples of loss of control that provoke anger. A student works in a field where that is the biggest problem.

L.title: Repentance
obj: Finish the salah increments with the sitting between prostrations (jalsa): why we sit for forgiveness and think of one sin each time.
Debrief tawbah and teach its pillars: regret, stopping now, and a real plan for the future, plus returning rights.
Teach a root-cause analysis plan: when, where, with whom, what trigger, what time, then remove factors and retry.
Explain that repeating tawbah with a new factor removed each time is how you improve, and that addictions need outside help.
Introduce the 'black box': what you really believe versus what you tell others and yourself, and why planning fails if the belief is wrong.
Teach honest self-confrontation and contemplation time as the way to change beliefs.
topics: Alternating week
This week is the practical session: another addition to salah and a tawbah follow-up.
Training wheels
Waiting until all concepts are covered would take too long. Small increments help now, but the full fix comes from tazkiyah.
Practices so far
Pause, Fatiha point, tasbih in ruku', gratitude at hamd, du'a in sujud.
The last movement: jalsa
The sitting is for seeking forgiveness, rabbi ighfir li.
Why separate from sujud
Sujud is for the present and future. The past goes to istighfar.
Why sitting is the posture of apology
Someone ashamed sits low and lets the other see the remorse on their face. Apologizing with your back turned is missing something.
Think of something
Do not end the sitting with nothing. A general 'forgive me for everything' avoids the practice.
What comes to mind
Whatever comes to mind is what bothers you most. Those are the sins that matter.
How often to change it
He does not care. You can keep the same one.
17 times at least
At least 17 sittings a day, so you can keep working on the sin.
Prioritize and consult
Sometimes people regret things that are not a problem, like watching movies. Binge-watching or filth is a problem. Ask if unsure.
Add them gradually
If you add everything at once it is a big change and you risk relapse. Add one every couple of days.
Praying alone
Especially when praying alone, add these to find something in it.
Debrief: tawbah
Did anyone try performing tawbah?
Make it practical
If you do not try, it becomes another lecture.
The elements of tawbah
Regret in the heart, which can be expressed with astaghfirullah or atubu ilayh.
Past, present and future
Regret is the past, stopping is the present, a plan is the future. A fourth, returning rights.
Returning rights
Easier than it seems for backbiting. For murder you may have to turn yourself in.
Stopping is easy
No one repents while sinning.
Regret and planning
People say 'I do not want to do it again' without changing anything. Same habits, same environment, same person, they will do it again.
Root cause analysis
Why, when, what time of day, day of the week, frequency, who is around, what triggers it, what emotions or thoughts.
Tawbah from one sin fixes many
Scholars say real tawbah from one sin is tawbah from most, as you uncover other problems.
Example: lifestyle
Sins happen when you are up all night. You change your lifestyle.
Surah at-Tawbah
It is the surah about repenting from lagging behind the Prophet. He compares it to staying in Medina while he is at Tabuk.
Remove toxic people
Circles of acquaintances, friends and best friends. Assign cards and move people. Distance from toxic people without declaring war.
Plan and fail
You make a plan, fail, do tawbah again with another factor removed. After four or five tries the frequency drops.
Motivation to try again
A student says fear of Allah. Teacher: you cannot say you will not stop and just ask forgiveness.
Pillars
You need all of them. The scholars mostly talk about regret and a plan because they are hardest.
How to plan
Write the factors: why, when, who, how. Remove them. Perform tawbah repeatedly, each time removing one more.
Addiction needs outside help
Drugs, alcohol or porn addiction may need a rehab facility for six to eight weeks.
Willpower
Willpower is the ability to overcome what the nafs wants. Understand why the nafs wants it.
The plan is circumstances
When, where, why, how. Remove them one by one.
Planning skill
Planning is technical. Poor planning ruins tawbah even with perfect regret.
Three layers of belief
What you tell others, what you tell yourself, and what you actually believe.
Example: looking at women
You say it is haram, but is that what you really believe?
The black box
Most people never open it. Tazkiyah is ripping the lid off to see what is inside.
What is inside can be devastating
You risk losing respect for yourself. That is the only way to improve.
Why a sin will not go away
You do not really think it is a problem, so you cannot regret it, so you cannot stop.
Zina example
Men who say it is wrong still cheat when no one is watching. Yusuf's story shows the opposite.
Rationalizations
'Allah will forgive me, I only need a few times.' That is what you believe.
First be honest
Confront that you have not told yourself the truth.
Thoughts, actions and feelings
Use the cycle so they feed the same direction. It moves from Islam to iman.
How you got there
You lied to yourself for years. Reverse it by learning the contrary: read Quran, scholars, take it to heart.
Maintain it
If you relapse, find why. Change takes time.
Prayer example
Deep down some think why five times a day, why not two. That belief is why your prayer is poor.
Rip the lid off
It is painful. If it does not bother you, you did not do it.
Contemplation time
Schedule time in your day or week to sit and think with a notepad.
Cognitive dissonance
Either your real belief or your stated belief wins. Some stop trying altogether.
Your job
Move the religion's beliefs from the superficial layer into the black box where they dictate behavior.
Why you failed the increments
If the root belief is unchanged, no plan works.
Say it to yourself
Put out what you actually think, even if rude, and then break it down.
Hypothetical: murder with no consequences
Would you? Quran's 'law' hypotheticals show Allah knows.
Breaking points
Allah's grace is that He does not test you to the breaking point.
We are Muslim because we were not put in the position
A humbling thought. Make beliefs more negative about sin.
Yusuf
Everything made it easy and refusing lost him everything, yet he refused.
Abdullah ibn Hudhafa
A king sent a woman to his cell. She said I do not know if I entered on a man or a woman, he never opened his eyes.
How to get there
Change company and environment, seek knowledge. The more you know of Jannah and Jahannam the more you adhere.
Student question: verbalizing a belief you know is wrong
Teacher: say it to yourself in the context that you want your belief aligned.
Why he teaches this through tawbah
It is the practical route to work on beliefs and factors.
Why people do not change
Their belief system is not aligned with what salah is. That is okay, start there.

L.title: Boundary swings
obj: Set the rules of the small group: do the tasks, fail, and come back with something to discuss. Tazkiyah is a workout, not a lecture.
Re-explain 'boundaries' as triggers: what makes the self-value pendulum swing and pulls you out of rational behavior.
Show that the pendulum swings in both directions: down (insult, anger) and up (praise, winning, vanity), and the upward swing goes unnoticed.
Give tools to bring it back without anger: realism, remembering Allah, gratitude, seeing praise as encouragement from Allah.
Teach that real happiness is a state, not something that must swing the pendulum, and that motives other than proving self-value are healthier.
Assign two to three weeks of reflection: your triggers in both directions and your own tools to return to the middle.
topics: Why the group is interactive
Questions and sharing let him follow up with people doing the tasks.
You must do the exercises
If you only drop in to listen, it is not helpful. He prefers you listen to recordings instead.
Try, fail, come back
Practice instead of theory. Making it work requires failing and discussing.
Tazkiyah is a riyadah
Scholars call it a workout like the gym. Muscle responds only after repeated tries.
Why not another lecture
Past general talks were interesting but no one benefited because there was no follow-up.
Open to disagreement
Tell him what you do not understand or agree with. You learn about yourself by doing so.
Back to comprehension and connection
Leftover from two weeks ago: the word 'boundaries'.
Boundary versus trigger
The ladies preferred 'trigger'. He cares about the Arabic concept, not the English word.
Recap: where humbleness matters
Examples were all about being mistreated, when the pendulum swings down.
Why the pendulum moves
The self-value box is not clean. Something is attached to it that should not be.
Aim for the middle
Confident and humble. That is what tawadu' means.
Anger is the way back
Anger drags the pendulum back up. The cause is something attached to your self-value.
Remove variables one by one
You cannot know them all. Life shows you, then you say 'I should not have let that bother me'.
Not life boundaries
A teacher or therapist needs boundaries with others. That is a different skill.
Prevent: step away
When you feel it move, do not engage. Reset your head, then come back and respond appropriately.
No one gave the opposite example
Everyone gave examples of the downward swing. That concerns him.
The upward swing goes unnoticed
The nafs does not mind it. You can live a lifetime pushed up and get accustomed to it.
Treated normally feels wrong
Some people live unrealistically high, so normal respect feels like a drop.
Not every praise does it
You know which praise or recognition sends you up. Prevent it the same way: do not engage.
His public-speaking example
At around 15, praise swung him. Shaykhs told him not to feel it, so he walked away. Later it stopped mattering.
Realism
If you know the truth about yourself you are not fooled by others' uninformed or momentary opinion.
Question: family insulted
Teacher: defend what must be defended. The issue is irrational emotional response, not life boundaries.
Two responses
Lash back and say what is not you, or address it calmly and clearly without feeling threatened.
Boundary differs by person
Wife, mother, enemy. That is another skill. Here: what triggers you.
Upward swing is as toxic
You bring the downward swing back fast. The upward one you leave for a long time.
Student example: winning at chess
Trash talk after winning. Teacher: it differs by person.
Happiness has two kinds
Why Allah says do not rejoice (fariha) in the Quran: the bad kind of happiness.
How to tell
If you are happy because the pendulum swung, that is the problem.
Hadith of the Prophet (praise)
A man asked about someone praised for good deeds. The Prophet said it is the immediate good news of the believer.
Tool: see praise as encouragement
Do not read it as 'I'm awesome'. See Allah sending encouragement to continue.
Calm response has grace
If someone provokes you and you stay calm, it says something about them, not you.
How to send it back
What is the feeling and thought process to bring it back? Think about it for 2 to 3 weeks.
Nafs gets angry or depressed
Down swings give anger or depression. Remove yourself, identify the trigger, return without anger.
Tools, not one tool
Not a quiz. Several tools exist to hold it in the middle.
The nafs thinks vanity is safe
The nafs loves you and ignorantly thinks vanity and arrogance keep you safe and strong.
Negotiating with your nafs
I do not want it to swing at all. We will be happy without swinging it upward.
Nafs's dictionary
The nafs defines happiness as swinging up. Teach it otherwise.
Life teaches true happiness
At the end of life people name moments with family as the happiest.
Winning without swinging
Possible. Those are the people you admire: they win and stay humble.
Tool: realism, again
Know yourself accurately.
Can you be happy when you lose?
Not required. You may be sad. The question is whether it swings.
Student tool: remember it is from Allah
Reminding yourself the good is a gift that can be taken away.
Differentiate
Sit down and separate the happiness that swings from the real, and anger that is right from anger that is ego.
Right anger
Watching people oppressed, anger is correct. The reason matters.
Real emotion
Feel sad when sad, cry when crying, without attaching it to self-value. Happiness becomes a state.
His own story
He lost the roles he built (physician, nurse) and was not happy for years until he let go of needing something to swing it.
Happiness is a state of mind
Unless you are very ill or poor, you can be happy now.
Student: does it hurt motivation?
Dissatisfaction drives goals. Teacher: is lack of self-value the best motive?
Healthier motives
Gratitude, a calling, service. You do not need to prove you are valuable.
No retirement
Muslims never talked about retirement. A mission continues until death.
Assignment
Reflect on what swings the pendulum both ways and how to return it. Tools are personal.
Upbringing
We grow up in a world that makes us question our value: racism, beauty standards, money, attention.
Humbleness as service
Serve: make someone tea, say something nice. It does not bother you because your self-value is stable.
Humble from love, not hidden vanity
Not hoping someone discovers your greatness. You serve out of love of Allah and His creation.
Self-analysis loop
After a swing ask why this one. Rip the lid off the black box and see what you believe.
Schedule
Off for 2 to 3 weeks, with reminders in the group chat. Humbleness will be concluded after.
Humbleness is strength
Not weakness. Inner strength more than muscle. Linked to love.

L.title: The tashahhud and the black box
obj: Reset the group after the break: two years in, build a foundation so newcomers do not stall the topics, and limit new joiners to a new batch.
Re-set the weekly rhythm: four elements (comprehension, connection, ritual, exercises), two per week, each revisited after two weeks.
Teach that tazkiyah is self-analysis: think deeply, write, run scenarios, and only then ask mature questions.
Finish the salah increments with the tashahhud as the conclusion of a unit, with salam to the Prophet, to yourself and to the righteous, and to the people (and angels) around you.
Introduce the sunnah rak'ahs plan: 12 a day, two added every two weeks.
Revisit tawbah: the regret needs a true belief behind it. Teach the three levels of belief and the difference between iman (fact) and emotions that fluctuate.
Show that knowledge (ilm) is how a rationalized belief is rewritten, and that you must be a seeker of truth, not convenience.
topics: Why structure matters
The group has run two years. By next year members should be comfortable enough with the main topics to teach younger people.
Building bricks
A foundation lets him move to complex topics. People who jump in new slow it down.
New people go to a new batch
Give friends' names to Abdurrahman. A new batch will run on another day.
Keep your twice-a-day work
Add small elements around your baseline until remembrance of Allah is a habit.
Weekly rhythm
Four elements: comprehension, connection, ritual, exercises. Two per week, revisited every two weeks.
Reflect before asking
If you do not reflect, you cheat yourself. Think alone, write, run the scenario to its end.
Do not ask every question
Ask mature questions that come after thinking. It helps the teacher and builds the habit.
Tazkiyah is self-analysis
Self-awareness, self-reflection, self-accountability. He teaches concepts, you learn to analyze.
Methodology, not answers
No two life problems are the same. Like an exam: learn the tools, not the exact question.
Today: ritual
Small increments in salah. One left: the sitting (tashahhud).
Recap of the five fundamentals
Pause, Fatiha contemplation, tasbih in ruku', gratitude, du'a in sujud, and today the sitting.
Tashahhud is the lock on every unit
Every two rak'ahs there is a sitting. It is a wrap-up of a meeting.
Step one: praise Allah
At-tahiyyat is wishes of life, greetings, salawat and good words for Allah.
Step two: salam to the Prophet
'As-salamu alayka ayyuhan-nabi', as if he is present. Not worship of him.
He is aware of our deeds
He witnesses the Ummah's good deeds, blesses them, and makes du'a for us.
No relationship with Allah without the Prophet
He is the medium who told you about Allah.
Adab: do not remove the medium
You never remove those who supported you. This is why we give salam to him.
Step three: salam to yourself and the righteous
Then the two shahadahs.
Concluding a unit
Even if the unit was poor, conclude it well, like ending any meeting.
Conclusion of the whole salah
Praise, tasbih, gratitude, du'a, istighfar, Quran, all done. Conclude with salawat.
Jalsa versus tashahhud
The jalsa is for istighfar. The tashahhud concludes the unit.
Final salam: greet the people
Look to the people (and angels), not at your shoulder. As an imam you look at those behind you.
Praying alone
You never pray alone: angels roam seeking gatherings and join you.
Next time: sunnah and salawat
Which sunnah to hold, how many, best ones, intentions.
Plan: 12 rak'ahs of sunnah a day
Two before Maghrib and around the fard prayers. Keep qiyam for extra, even two or four.
Two weeks per increment
Commit two weeks, then add two more. Hard at home, easy in the masjid.
Tawbah debrief
Regret and planning are both harder than people think.
Tawbah nasuh
Nasuh means advice and sincerity. It fixes other problems too. The verse appears once in the Quran.
Scope: rights excluded
Returning stolen items or fixing riba is separate. Focus on the two basics: regret and resolve.
The black box
Do you truly regret it? What do you actually believe about it?
Reflection uncovers other problems
Once you rip the lid off you find other issues feeding the sin.
Three levels of belief
What you tell people, what you tell yourself, what you genuinely believe.
Example: resurrection
Do you really believe you will be resurrected and held accountable for every detail?
Root problem of many people
They say they believe but have only learned to act as if. He gave an extreme example.
Belief versus emotion
Feelings of hope, fear and reverence fluctuate. Belief should be fact.
Quote on certainty
If I saw Paradise and touched Hellfire it would not add to my certainty, only to my reverence and fear.
Emotions are a range
Love, khashya, khawf go up and down like a hot spring.
Iman encompasses both
One part fixed fact, one part that fluctuates.
Example: the zina slip
It is not that he stopped believing. The fear plummeted.
Belief not yet a fact
If the belief is not a fact, fluctuation is wild and stability is absent.
Diagnose
Is my problem a missing stable belief or a normal human fluctuation?
How can you regret what you do not think is wrong?
Looking at women in the street: to regret you must believe it is a serious wrong with no excuse.
The scroll, not a word
Your belief is a long scripted rationalization, not just the word haram.
Example script
'Everyone does it, I cannot marry for years, I did nothing major, I will stop later.'
Result: no real regret
Maybe not great, not really wrong. That is the problem.
Human fluctuation
A believer with full belief still slips. Without right belief, tawbah is impossible.
The nafs gets in under stress
His story: slapping his three-year-old, then true regret that changed his life.
True regret
Goes against every fabric of who you are. It drives decisions.
Check your belief about the Hereafter
Spend time and see if you are truly certain and live as such.
Student: true belief governs action
Contemplate, intellectual piece, remove rationalizations.
Reality check
Study what the Quran, the Prophet, the scholars say. Knowledge crystallizes.
Ilm is a weapon and immune system
It pushes the nafs's narrative down. Who wrote the rationalization? Your nafs did.
Take back the pen
Write what you believe you stand for, grounded in knowledge.
Example: lowering the gaze
Listen to scholars, the Quran, science, others' experience. Belief strengthens, regret improves.
Addictions need external help
General sins can be dealt with by this method.
Triangle and the heart diagram
Thoughts, feelings and behaviors are all affected by what you insert.
Student: ilm is a rabbit hole
The scroll gets longer. Discussed in the next point.
Oncologist who smokes
Why would a lung cancer oncologist smoke? Seeking convenience, not truth.
Seeker of truth or of convenience
You can seek convenience no matter what you are told.
His music story
As a youth in Saudi Arabia he loved music and was told it was haram. He did not believe it so he could not leave it.
Research took over a year
The more he read, the less he believed. He feared rationalizing convenience.
Seeker of knowledge
The scholars are 50/50. He had never been told of the half that allowed it.
Hit the brakes
When an opinion suits you, ask: convenience or truth?
Not every truth is inconvenient
Accept all truth. He is not arguing music is allowed.
No tawbah without regret
Then planning is the second piece, next.
Logistics
He goes to the other group. Stay and chat until Maghrib or leave.

L.title: Emotions and the pendulum
obj: Re-present the pendulum: every swing generates emotions, and swing-generated emotions are unhealthy by default.
Teach that the only way you know the pendulum swung is by your emotions, so you must question them: why am I feeling this today?
Distinguish healthy from toxic versions of happiness, anger and sadness (farah/ghadab/huzn mahmud versus madhmum).
Show the danger of living only in swing-based emotion: you lose the ability to feel genuine emotion, such as khushu' in prayer.
Define khushu' as an emotional response to something you intellectually agree with, not a swing, and show it needs real knowledge.
Teach that self-value never moves with sin or worship, and how to reframe: gratitude for Allah's gift, sadness at losing closeness.
Set the practice: contemplation and journaling of daily emotions, starting with simple ones.
Teach that tazkiyah is slow and boring, with no 'aha moments', apart from rare people (majadhib).
topics: Return to comprehension
First comprehension session after the break. Self-value wraps into humbleness and service.
What swings your pendulum
The remaining job: find what still makes you unable to think straight.
New angle: emotions
When it swings it generates strong emotions, and they are toxic emotions.
Healthy and unhealthy versions
Each emotion has a healthy and an unhealthy form.
Anger as the way back
When triggered you bring it back with anger. Not all emotions are healthy.
Ghadab lillah
Anger for the sake of Allah is part of the deen, but there is also blameworthy anger.
Blameworthy happiness
The Quran says Allah does not love the exultant. The wrong kind of happiness comes from deriving value from achievements.
Healthy huzn
Some sadness is required when you think of the Hereafter, but not the kind that makes you feel worthless.
Your job in tazkiyah
Identify what swings the pendulum and generates the emotions.
The self-value box
Nothing should feed it. It is constant and from Allah, but you are not fully disconnected yet.
Boundaries are triggers
Identify them, then work to remove them. In the meantime recognize when they swing.
Emotions are the only signal
You know the pendulum swung only by feeling more or less valuable.
Student: happy versus sad framework
Student mentions farah mahmud and madhmum, ghadab and huzn. Teacher: very good.
Question your emotions
When you feel extremely sad, angry, or very happy, ask why am I feeling this today.
Any emotion from the swing is unhealthy
If healthy, the pendulum has not moved.
How to tell them apart
Question where the emotion came from. With time you distinguish quickly.
Healthy happiness
It motivates you and comes from Allah's bounty and mercy.
Contemplation, not me
He cannot tell you which of your emotions are healthy. You must sit with them.
Nafs does not bring you down from a high
You stay up there. It uses toxic emotion only to bring you up from the low.
Regulation means awareness
Be aware of the origin of the emotion, not necessarily control it.
Losing the ability to feel
People who cannot cry at a loved one's death. If you only feel toxic emotion you cannot feel the good ones.
Raw emotion
True joy and true sadness are healthy and not tied to the pendulum.
Why people cry at good news
Healthy emotions all come together in the end.
Stop attaching worth to achievement
When you achieve you are not more valuable. When you fail you are not less.
People differ
Some are more capable of raw emotion, shaped by upbringing, trauma, friction.
No quick fix
Daily contemplation. 'No magic potion.'
Is this sadness healthy?
Ask whether it is sadness that something bad happened or sadness that you felt lesser.
Racial slur example
Do not repair self-value by mistreating the other. Acknowledge it swung, put a pin to revisit, restore in a healthy way.
Student: circular test
How do I test whether it was swing or gratitude? Teacher: coach yourself, 50/50 maybe, the intensity drops and what remains is genuine.
We are sensitive to others' feelings
We pick up vibes from others. Turn that sensitivity inward.
Never pure
Most moments of happiness or sadness have a little swing. Remove the toxic part.
Anger that motivates
Seeing oppression and wanting change is healthy.
Fake enthusiasm
People with swagger in their step feel off because it is not genuine.
Genuine emotion
Seeing something beautiful or sad that is real. It motivates and does not break you.
How to judge your happiness
Does it lead to gratitude and closeness to Allah or to forgetting obligations?
Segue: khushu' in Ramadan
Why can't you feel khushu' in taraweeh despite profound recitation?
Student answers
Do you understand it? Your emotions are connected with the pendulum.
Taraweeh explanation
The Imam's voice is beautiful but you are not accustomed to emotion that is not about you.
Work hard and it comes
Those who keep coming get a moment of it.
Allow beauty to affect you
Hear Allah's name and be moved. You cannot appreciate beauty if you only swing.
Question: what if you know you derive value
These are your boundaries and triggers. Self-coach, write down why you care.
The source is usually one opinion
One person or an image before a group. Care about your image before Allah instead.
Removing is easier than recovering
Removing the source beats bringing it back each time.
Define khushu'
Emotional response to something you intellectually agree with, after reflection. Not a swing.
Student: sad at an ayah of punishment
Swing or genuine? Teacher: find out why you feel it.
Show-off crying
Some cry only while others watch. Once the image is gone they feel nothing.
Sahaba's khashya
Quran, Jannah and Nar moved them because they understood deeply.
Knowledge produces right sadness and joy
Fully accepting the reality of the Hereafter makes you sad at Jahannam and moved at Jannah.
Daily practice
Contemplate your daily emotions. Begin with simple ones you know are swings, then ones you thought were genuine.
Honesty gives khushu'
Be honest with yourself and Allah without the mask.
Keep the healthy part
Sadness over sin is fine. Distinguish and build on the healthy part so it is not once a year.
Real versus toxic emotions
Identify the real ones and experience them, stop the rest.
Student: can self-value drop with sin?
No. It never moves, not with sin and not with qiyam.
Worship and self-value
If you attach value to worship you become vain. Remove it at once.
Reframe happy after worship
Not 'I rock' but 'Allah saw me worthy of the opportunity'.
Example: memorizing Quran
Happy that Allah gifted me this word and hoping He is pleased.
Reframe sadness after sin
Not 'I am worthless' but 'I distanced myself from Allah and risked punishment'.
Learn it young
Waiting until 30s or 40s means more complexities.
Student: no aha moment yet
He needs more time and examples.
Journal
Keep notes on your phone as emotions hit. You feel only a few patterns repeatedly.
No aha moments
Tazkiyah is boring and slow. You see change only by checkpointing and revisiting after two years.
Majadhib
Allah pulls some people who arrive without the path. Rare.
Variation in nafs
Like some people immune to HIV or COVID. A bell curve.
Most is slow and consistent
For most people it is continuous drawing nearer.
Why not talk about loving Allah yet
You need to understand this first. He is not selling fake emotions.
Be patient
Compare yourself to two years ago.
Student: Prophet's teaching
Did the Prophet teach these concepts? Teacher: yes, he corrected detailed mistakes. To be revisited.
Close
Not everyone received the same level of attention from him.

L.title: Reflection, tawbah plan and the sunnah of Fajr
obj: Announce the schedule change: the halaqa moves to Saturday night after Maghrib prayer, since weekdays are fully booked.
Press the need for daily reflection and contemplation: keep a private 15-minute sit-down and write your thoughts.
Explain why he will not move on yet: without a solid self-value, pushing self-criticism leads to self-loathing.
Wrap up the salah increments (no third repeat) and add the sunnah of Fajr as the first weekly sunnah commitment.
Set the tawbah exercise: choose a sin you truly regret, then plan it.
Teach how to change convictions (knowledge, plus the triangle of thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and what goes into the heart) versus how to plan (a quick analysis of when, who, where).
Show that each failed tawbah adds a new factor to remove, and that one solid tawbah changes a whole cluster of habits.
Build belief that radical change is possible, and that this belief is the real obstacle.
topics: Schedule change
Mullah's return crowds his week. Weekdays 6:30 to 10 are booked.
New slot
Move to Saturday after the Maghrib prayer, 9 to 10, before Isha. Ladies' time to be sorted separately.
Fading option
If not changed, the halaqa shrinks to 40, 30, then 20 minutes and dies. Put a pin and he will message the group.
Two years review
He counted topics covered over two years.
What is missing: your own effort
Reflection, contemplation, mindfulness daily.
Quiet time
Sit in a quiet place facing the qiblah, with no distractions, and think.
Self-awareness and self-accountability
The aim at the start, later to become something different.
Risk of harm
If you do not reflect, you could be harmed by what you hear, since the topics build in a hierarchy.
Proposal: 15 minutes
Even if you do your wird on the go, sit 15 minutes and write for yourself. He will not read it.
Why
Later you tie your first thoughts to the concepts as they crystallize.
Why self-value comes first
After a year he is still unsure the majority understand. Anything else could harm you.
Self-loathing
Pushing self-criticism without solid self-value leads to hating yourself, which is the opposite of the goal.
Without self-value you cannot apologize
You cannot feel true regret, or hold yourself accountable.
Ritual: increments covered twice
Pause, Fatiha point, tasbih, gratitude, du'a in sujud, a sin at the jalsa, tashahhud and salawat.
Individual time
He wants to sit with each person but has no slot. Plans a campaign in November, daily wisdom talks.
Praying alone is harder
With an imam it is easier. Alone or at work you rush.
Jogging through prayer
It becomes mechanical and kills the potential of the relationship with Allah.
Aim of tazkiyah
Less focus on self needs and whims, more on love of Allah.
Add a sunnah each week or two
Start with the sunnah of Fajr.
Sunnah of Fajr
The Prophet said the two rak'ahs are better than the world. Short, with Kafirun and Ikhlas.
Caution
If you recite them in the sunnah you cannot repeat the same in fard when praying alone.
Slow increments
Adding all sunnahs at once will crumble. Add two, hold two weeks, add more.
Secure the Fajr two
Whether you are woken by your parents or alone.
Exercise: tawbah
He had planned something else but had not covered regret and planning.
Choose one thing
Pick a sin or shortcoming you can realistically stop.
Regret requires the black box
Rip off the lid. Choose something you know is wrong, not one you rationalize.
Why
Changing convictions takes months and would make the exercise nearly impossible.
Planning is practical
More pragmatic and easier than convictions.
Changing convictions
Knowledge plus the triangle of thoughts, emotions and behaviors.
Behavior changes thought
Staying away from the sin starts to change the way you think. Example: lowering the gaze in the street.
Emotions and the heart
The qalb is a pot. What you see, hear, think and who you are with goes in.
Mixed input, mixed emotions
Homogeneous input pushes emotion one way. Mixed gives confusion.
What are you subjecting yourself to?
Company, conversation, what you watch and read.
Planning as analysis
A plan needs an analysis, like in quality improvement in the hospital.
Flowchart and bottleneck
What leads to the problem, what leads to that, where is the bottleneck?
Creatures of habit
Most people have their own algorithm of how they plan their day.
Fishbone analysis
Look at social, environmental, management (you), financial.
When
A time of day or a situation: after waking, before bed.
Who
Who encourages the sin? Example: gossip.
Where
Is it attached to a place?
Skip 'why'
Why is belief, which is a different job. Here we want technicalities.
Adjust and iterate
Each tawbah makes an adjustment, it works, fails, you analyze again and add another factor.
Up to ten factors
Each fix removes negative forces from your life.
Tawbah nasuh
Nasuh is influence not just advice. A tawbah that fixes other problems as well.
One solid tawbah is enough for life
Bad things come in clumps and so do good ones.
Vicious and virtuous cycles
Example: a smoker finds his friends also keep him up at night and cause him to miss Fajr.
Learning by failing
Two to three tries, removing four to six external factors.
Recap of tawbah
Counting sins, insensitivity, beliefs that block regret. Choose a sin with a solid belief.
Result
Environment, companionship and lifestyle changes remove 85% of the problem.
Believe change is possible
Many believe 'who I am today is who I will be forever'. Tazkiyah offers radical change.
Addiction recovery
Rehab shows they can change, and recovery involves a big lifestyle change and cutting off old circles.
This is the essence of tawbah
Cut off what reminds you of the sin.
Converts to Islam
Changing where they spend their time: 0 to 14 hours a week in the masjid is a radical lifestyle change.
Two questions
Do you believe you should? Do you believe you can? The second is the biggest problem.
Share the process
Next time some will share the process, not the sin.
Student: a sin I do not regret
Do not choose one where it is not a big deal. You can plan but it is likely to fail.
Choose something you fully regret
Be honest. Close with prayer.

L.title: Genuine emotion and masculinity
obj: Recap that every emotion from a pendulum swing is toxic, and that you spot a swing only through emotion.
Teach that genuine emotions, including anger, are healthy when they are not attached to self-value, with the Prophet as the model.
Explain why modern youth carry more stress, and how constant comparison and proving yourself end in depression after reaching the top.
Show that people who cannot cry at funerals are unfamiliar with genuine emotion, and that men hide emotion because of a distorted definition of masculinity.
Teach that shame about emotion usually means shame that the pendulum swung, so test it by asking why you are ashamed.
Insist that definitions of masculinity, value and right come from Allah, not society, and that living by them will cost you relationships.
Show that the Prophet, the Companions and the Salaf felt and expressed emotion openly, and that feeling is what separates the living from the dead.
topics: Today: connection
Connection piece has not been covered for a while. Back to self-value and humbleness wrapping.
What humbleness requires
Self-value, assumptions, expectations, ujb (vanity) and kibr (arrogance).
Recap: swing emotion is always toxic
You know the pendulum swung only through emotions. Your job is to tease out toxic from healthy.
Genuine emotion is healthy, even anger
The anger forbidden is the one attached to self-value.
Example: teacher or father
Angry because they defy me is about me. Healthy anger is for their benefit.
Prophet never angry for himself
He had no buttons. Anger at oppression stayed until justice was served.
Healthy anger motivates
Seeing Gaza or injustice and angering to educate yourself and do good. Wrong anger leads to harm.
Sadness must be felt
Healthy sadness is therapeutic. The Prophet felt sad often.
Abu Bakr cried with joy
Genuine tears can be happy or sad.
Two types of happiness
Quran: Allah does not love the exultant. Bad: pendulum toward vanity. Good: bathing in Allah's mercy.
The Prophet's emotion
Quick to tears, always smiling, felt grief, anger and frustration genuinely.
Point of tazkiyah
See Allah in everything, not detach from the world.
Today's generation more stressed
Expected to perform earlier, compared globally, beauty standards everywhere.
Not a fair playing field
You compare yourself to people given different hands.
Psychiatrists agree
Adolescent psychiatry notes rising stress from technology.
Trying to prove value all the time
When you stop you see no purpose and may become depressed.
Depressed at the top
Having proved the most, the swing reverses violently to the low side.
Why you cannot cry at a funeral
Grief is not attached to self-value so you do not know it.
You block genuine feeling
Genuine feelings are intense and scary to those used to superficial ones.
The Prophet's grief
He sobbed at the loss of Ibrahim and Hamza.
Children feel openly
A three-year-old still feels. Social norms push us into the game.
Stop proving yourself
You are a human being and no one can take it away. Hold the pendulum in the middle.
Beauty needs genuine emotion
Those who see beauty only for self-image cannot be moved.
Q: trauma can numb
Rare, needs professional help. Otherwise it is the nafs.
The nafs ignores emotion
It sees emotion as useful only to bring the pendulum back.
Men hide emotion
Masculinity is defined as a pendulum attachment.
Society's definitions
Fear of the worst insult, a distorted definition.
His grandmother in Syria
Two men holding hands: normal friendship in Syria in 1996, he did so until mid-20s.
Redefine value
Do not attach value to masculinity. Prophet's masculinity was service and carrying burdens, and even then do not attach.
Why are emotions annoying?
Prolonged, not a quick fix, and they make you vulnerable.
Vulnerability
Emotions show love and failure. We push it down so no one sees.
Student: they will use it against me
Are you ashamed of crying? If so the problem is yours.
Shame test
You are not ashamed that you cried, you are ashamed that it swung.
Strength at the funeral
Be the pillar for your family, then cry later in your room.
Hide for others' sake
In front of fragile elders or the overloaded. That is respect, not shame.
Definitions come from Allah
Muslims take the definition of masculinity, value and right from Allah.
Do not let society dictate
A distorted society changes your understanding of the world.
Crying test
Ask: is this because I feel weak, or is it genuine?
People who judge
A friend who tells others you cried is not a friend.
Shut off dead weight
Living by true definitions loses you some people and brings others.
Not advice to express emotions everywhere
Hide only toxic emotion. Genuine emotion needs no shame.
His father
Traditional Syrian farming man, father died when he was nine. He asked his mom at ten if his dad loved him.
Understand those who hide emotion
Different experience and definitions. His father only showed emotion after 60.
The Prophet was not like that
Bravest, closest to the enemy, ascetic life, and still quick to emotion. The Companions always knew his mood.
Fudayl ibn Iyad story
Serious, never smiling. Said he smiled out of fear Allah would think he was irritated.
Lessons from Fudayl
Hard past dented his ability. If you have no such past you can learn.
Assignment: identify your tears
Defeat versus real sadness. Shame about a toxic emotion is normal and good, it means you see it.
Student: perceiving correctly
How do you perceive things correctly whether others agree or not?
His example of cost
Played the note people want or tell the truth? Removed from every masjid, still pays at work.
Define what is right and live by it
People who should not be in your life will leave. 85% will go.
Friends and the masjid
Gatherings like this are your best chance of people sticking around.
Not combative
You can get along at work with those who do not share your views.
Opinions after death
How quickly people forget you after funeral.
Be truthful, honest, genuine
Live the way life should be lived by Allah's guidance.
Work story
Asked for Fridays off for Jumu'ah, was sabotaged, and still pays.
Nothing to hold over you
Only if you give up self-value for it.
Essentials
Genuine emotions are beautiful. Distinguish them from toxic. Do not be ashamed of them.
The Companions wept at Quran
The Prophet disliked loud crying so they held it down. Umar had tear scars down his cheeks.
Walls
We know emotions are annoying so we build walls. You lose life.
A mosaic of emotions
Angry, happy, sad, excited for the right reasons.
Alive versus dead
What is the difference? Feeling. The sternal rub test.
Love of Allah needs feeling
Before talking about love of Allah you must first feel.
Dhikr
The one who remembers Allah is alive, the other dead.
His oncology work
Breaking bad news twice a day, tearing up with patients. Let them feel, and never hold it against them.
Betraying someone's emotion
A friend who uses your tears against you is not a friend.
When to hold back
With someone struggling who cannot bear it. Otherwise no walls.
Close
Went beyond planned. Will continue.

L.title: Imagining your death
obj: Set the death simulation (tawahhum al-mawt): lie in a dark, cramped place and coach yourself that you have died.
Show that the whole equation of Islam and tazkiyah collapses if death is not accepted as real.
Teach through a thought experiment (what if you never died?) that urgency, drive and beauty come from limited time.
Argue that accepting mortality improves life, using his sarcoma patients and a mock-diagnosis study as examples.
Link death to the Prophet's life (18 direct bereavements), where it is the bridge to Allah and a reason to draw close now.
Tie procrastination to ignoring death, and set a harder optional version: live a week as if it is your last, which should change nothing you should not already be doing.
Collect each person's wish-list at the moment of simulated death.
topics: The exercise: imagine your death
Only one student brought him anything on it before, so he moved on.
Source: an early scholar
A teacher of Imam Malik would lie between his bed and the wall in the dark and tell himself he had died.
Tawahhum
He runs a similar simulation on every 27th night of Ramadan.
Death is part of the equation
Without death the equations of Islam and tazkiyah crumble.
If you ignore death it will not resonate
He does not know exactly why. Allah created us this way.
Step one: imagine not dying
You live forever, aging slowly without becoming dependent.
Why would you do anything?
School, marriage, any goal. A student laughs at the thought of staying with one person forever.
Why this exercise
He did it at around 17. If faint-hearted or very young, skip it.
Near-death clarity
This simulates the focus of a near-death experience without going through one.
We all know subconsciously it ends
Religious and non-religious alike. We avoid facing it.
Ignoring does not work
Like an exam or a presentation: preparing beats avoiding.
Accepting mortality improves life
Everything tastes sweeter even if you are not religious.
The mock cancer diagnosis experiment
A reported unethical study told healthy people they had a few weeks left. After revealing the truth, most lived better, quit addictions, mended relationships.
Prophet: death is a sufficient reminder
'Kafa bil-mawti waa'izan'.
The Prophet lived with death
18 direct losses: wives, parents, children, cousins, friends, adopted son.
Our different attitude
Their acceptance explains why they adhered to the law and felt close to Allah.
Death is the bridge
The closer it feels, the closer to Allah you draw.
How to do the exercise: set the time
A time with no early morning, and not right after a meal, or you will fall asleep.
Darkness, no communication
No light, no phone, a small uncomfortable space. Like building a fort.
Coach yourself for 10 to 15 minutes
I am dead. No tomorrow, no second chance.
Student recalls his attempt
He used pillows rather than the wall.
Do not play outside audio
Coach yourself. You will not see loved ones or greet parents again.
Feel the fear then document
What do you wish you had done or secured? Each person feels differently.
Then Allah and the book
Imagine meeting Allah and accountability.
Repeat for acceptance
Not so often that it becomes habitual. When accepted, life gets better, and you skip the depression.
His sarcoma patients
Bone tumors in people under 30. Best case a year to a year and a half.
The best six months
They accept it, then do things of meaning: loved ones, travel, appreciating creation.
Come back and tell him
He wants your feelings, not a lecture. A student brought two points earlier.
His dream
Driving with good people, a bridge over water, a nuclear submarine, an explosion. He died in the dream.
Waking up
Paralyzed for 15 minutes, overwhelmed by the purest sadness he has felt.
Sadness not fear
Sad that it ended, sad that he did not do more and was too slow.
After self-value and humbleness comes mortality
Self-value talked about for two years. Next piece is accepting mortality.
It makes you happier
Every moment is valuable because it ends.
Legoland example
Tell kids 20 minutes: they use every ride. Tell them all the time they want: they waste it.
We are made that way
Only limited time reveals value. The Hereafter is different.
Ignoring death removes urgency
It also removes drive and beauty.
Beauty needs genuine emotion and death
Allah is beauty. To love Him you must see it, so you need genuine emotion, a still pendulum, and limited time.
Harder version: one week left
What would you do if you knew you die next week? Not required.
However you live that week is how you should live
If you would stop studying, you did not understand why you study.
Start with the simple simulation
Then tell him how you feel.
Student: procrastination
Chronic procrastination describes everyone.
Procrastination is ignoring death
You tell yourself there is time. Same for exams, deadlines and life.
Fix the big one
Get death in line and the small stuff follows.
Assignment
Do the simulation this week, report feelings and hopes. Talk next week, not in two.
Student: spend all your money, quit a job?
Teacher: that means you did not understand what Islam commands.
Other people are involved
You live for the dunya and the rest of your life too.
Doomsday novels
Writers imagine people abandoning every law. It reveals who you really are.
Exposure of the black box
The one-week exercise shows what is in the black box.
If you understood Islam correctly
You would not change a thing.
Close
Start with the simple simulation.

L.title: Death, time and fulfilment
obj: Debrief the death simulation: what people felt, and note the common thread that everyone mentions time.
Teach that the point is to feel how precious limited and unknown-length time is, and that emotions will vary with how you view yourself.
Distinguish healthy regret and sadness from anger, which signals living someone else's life.
Explain why the exercise is repeated every two to three months as a baseline to compare against.
Teach why Allah hides the time of death (mercy), and the hadith of living for the dunya as if immortal and for the akhirah as if dying tomorrow.
Show that if you are living for Allah, regret about death is about quality, not quantity, and that regret about cars, yachts or trips means a distorted view of life.
Teach that death lets you see beauty, and that the Companions died young yet fulfilled.
Re-set the exercise for another week with advice on how to do it.
topics: Debrief
Who tried it? He does not expect everyone to have.
Student: disappointment in himself
Looked at blessings, compared with others, realized how close to nothing he had done.
Keep it short
The simulated state need not last long. Share the emotion and thoughts.
Student: scared, regret
Regret for what he could have done. Feeling not ready and guilty.
Student: postponed it
Kept postponing it.
Common thread: granular attention to time
People start seeing details of their lives. What do you run out of at death? Time.
Everyone says time
'I wish I spent my time better.'
Point: feel the value of time
Limited and of unknown length, so even more precious.
Near-death or a simulation
The only way it dawns on many people.
Emotions vary
Sadness, fear, regret, disappointment, anger. Depends on accountability and self-analysis.
Took him three to four tries
He did not get it right the first time.
No need to keep doing forever
Once or twice gives clarity, and later reflection on death becomes less abstract.
Baseline
Remember how it felt. Do something differently now to feel differently later.
Repeating shows progress
If you change your life you will feel different each time.
What should you want to feel?
Calm, some sadness (losing time for good deeds), no heavy regret, no anger.
Anger at death
Common in people with a poor understanding of life.
Living on hold
Muslims who feel they are not living, waiting until they have money or time.
Lived someone else's life
Culture of parents or a sheikh, not deep belief. Died angry.
The 78-year-old patient
Many diseases, oxygen, said 'I haven't lived yet'.
Reflection
Some live others' lives and are unfulfilled at the end.
Sadness is normal, anger is not
Some regret, some sadness at losing opportunities for good deeds and tawbah.
Check your black box
Make sure you actually believe, to be fulfilled.
Repeat every two to three months
Three minutes is enough. Compare feelings. Am I using time better?
If nothing changed, ask why
What have I not changed about myself?
Why stay unchanged for years?
We are good at denial and bargain that we are special.
Student: knowing death date would help?
Teacher: it would make it harder. Procrastination: I have time.
Student: prioritize one thing
Start with one thing, the domino effect follows.
Ideal versus real
Listening is not change. It takes small steps and self-analysis.
Why Allah hides the time
Mercy. Knowing far ahead harms. Closeness helps.
Sudden death
The Prophet sought refuge from mawt al-faj'ah, sudden death with no chance for tawbah.
Student: knowing from birth
Teacher: you would not invest in relationships and goals.
Ibn Umar's saying
Work for the dunya as if you will live forever and for the akhirah as if you die tomorrow.
Work backwards
What do I not want to feel at death? Anger, frustration, wasted time.
Two things to change
Behavior and your understanding of role and importance.
Student's idea: throw away money
Teacher: why? Is feeding your family not the best use?
Wealth stays behind
But do not stop investing in long-term goals.
The seed
A tree is a 15-year investment. You still plant it even if the world ends.
Role: abd and khalifa
Once you understand it, dying tomorrow or in 15 years changes little.
His day
Fajr, dhikr, visiting the sick, halaqah, friend. Nothing to change.
If you live for Allah, you have nothing to change
Your regret will be quality.
Regret is quality not quantity
Wish my prayer was more focused, my intention clearer.
Less ujb, kibr, hasad, riya, ghaflah
Remembrance of death removes these.
Death in the equation
Humbleness and an acceptance of death must both be in place.
Quality means appreciating beauty
Is an hour in the halaqah well spent? It depends on feeling the beauty.
Last thing you see
Your last view of anything would look beautiful.
Death lets you see beauty
Beauty in what you have always overlooked.
Sahaba died young yet fulfilled
They lived with beauty, with the Prophet.
Middle-aged before you know it
Deep down he is still 16. Look at the elderly: they did not plan it.
Fulfilled people do not retire
He saw scholars die reciting Quran or listening to a student.
Shaykh who died listening to a 25-year-old
It was his mission, so 17 or 97 was the same.
Feel and ask if it is healthy
How would I feel now? Is that right? Make changes.
Dying scholar and talqin
A grandchild would say la ilaha illallah. Imam: go learn it so you are ready.
Sahaba feared death rightly
They feared they had not done enough, not depression.
Smiling on the deathbed
Tomorrow I meet my beloved ones.
Reflect young
Make peace early so death motivates.
Advice for this week
Intensity not duration. A few minutes, calm, quiet, dark.
Coach yourself and write
I am gone. What would I have wanted? What not?
Check your regrets
Regret not owning a car, yacht or visiting places means a distorted view of life.
Normal feelings
Some sadness, some regret, and hope of returning to the One who loves you.
Severe regret, fear or anger
Signals something distorted.
Student: why did the Prophet choose death?
He lived perfect quantity and quality and was ready. Readiness is the difference.
Ready to die: like chains gone
You do not throw away money or stop studying, you live them with appreciation.
Close
No right or wrong answer. Feel, reflect, check if it is healthy.

L.title: Accepting mortality
obj: Distinguish accepting mortality from fixating on the moment or manner of death, and make acceptance a requirement of the path.
Explain that Muslims should fear the outcome (punishment, lack of deeds) rather than nothingness, and that people drop out of tazkiyah at this topic.
Link weak iman to unexamined belief in the resurrection and the black box, showing how ignoring death lowers the quality of worship.
Use the hadith of nations calling each other to the Muslims as to a platter (wahn: love of the dunya and hating death) to show the difference between loving life and refusing death.
Contrast the Companions (living near death in battles) with our distance from it, and name the benefits of making peace with mortality.
Teach that you are not owed a warning before death, and warn against tul al-amal (long hopes).
Teach that you walk the path and are not held to the outcome, with the Prophet and Umar's words as examples.
Present acceptance of mortality as the strongest weapon against the nafs, to be renewed regularly.
Reiterate that daily reflection and an active struggle (mujahadah) against the nafs are required of members.
topics: Mortality, not the moment
Do not get stuck on when or how. Come to terms with the fact that you will not be here.
Acceptance defined
It should not give anxiety or depression and should not be actively ignored.
A Muslim who does not accept mortality
He does not know what category that is.
A durability test of tazkiyah
This is where people drop off. They find excuses.
Without it, nothing works
Everything else is meaningless without mortality.
West fears death as the end
Fear of nothingness. A Muslim should fear the outcome and lack of deeds instead.
Shaitan, not death, is the enemy
Death is a fact of life, but not something to wish for.
Why we want a longer life
The hadith of two men: the one who lived longer is higher. For more good deeds and closeness.
Transform your mentality
Fear and ignoring to acceptance, then avoiding death because you want more time.
Expose your fears
Nothingness? Why were you anxious or angry? Find the true source.
The black box again
'I believe in the Akhirah' but the scroll says otherwise.
The reason people go in and out
A lack of certainty in resurrection leads to ignoring death and poor quality.
Fluctuation is internal
Not external problems.
Why death should intensify life
It makes experiences more intense, so ignoring it lowers quality.
You are not getting anything from prayer
He cannot explain in a minute why. It takes months of attending.
Hadith of the platter
Nations will call each other to devour the Muslims as to a dish. Numerous but like foam. The cause is wahn.
Wahn: love of dunya and hatred of death
Loving the dunya is not the problem.
What is hayat al-dunya
A life of lower instincts, eating, drinking, reproducing.
Love is how you find sweetness of iman
Loving family, community, Allah and His Prophet all happen in the dunya.
The real problem
Loving dunya so much that you refuse death and compromise values to live.
Example: a fighter in Gaza
The image of a leader fighting to the end shows how some see their mortality.
Easier where death is near
Where people are dying all the time it is easier to accept.
The Prophet's era
Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Mu'tah, Khaybar. They did not need a simulation.
Battle is terrifying
Even paintball scares us. They constantly had near-death experiences.
Benefits of peace with mortality
Brave, mentally stable, stronger appreciation of beauty.
You are not owed a warning
Not everyone gets time for tawbah. The Prophet sought refuge from sudden death.
Tul al-amal
A sin of the heart: convincing yourself you have long to live, which kills urgency.
Debrief: simulation
Keep it to a minute or less. An hour will kill you.
Student: fear then salah
He realized everything rides on his prayer.
Student: not enough time
Feeling 'I have so many things I have not done' is a bad feeling. How to deal with it?
Student answers
Constant remembrance, plan the day around prayers.
Ihsan
Everything has a level of ihsan. You are not held to the outcome.
Are you doing it for Allah?
If so, 'so much left to do' does not exist.
The Prophet did not see the outcome
He did not see Islam spread across three continents and ask for time.
Tazkiyah is not about outcomes
It puts your feet on the path.
Midlife crisis
If you walk the path properly, what is the crisis?
Two requirements
Ongoing mujahadah against your nafs, and daily reflection. At least 15 minutes.
Do not just bring your nafs's words
You push back first, then come when you cannot.
Hadith of Abu Musa and Umar's sons
Umar said he hoped only to break even after the Prophet. Abu Musa's son said Umar's father was better.
Living longer cuts both ways
More chance of good deeds, more chance of deviating.
Looking back
Sometimes the heart was clearer 10 years ago. Fix your intention.
Student: feeling it was better
You can state how you felt without declaring acceptance.
Mortality becomes a source of peace
If iman is strong and intention clear, you keep doing what you do.
Memorizing Quran example
If you die before finishing, you get the reward of the full Quran if you put in the effort.
You walk the path
He holds you to effort, not outcome.
I cannot kill you and bring you back
He wishes to internalize it for you.
Strongest weapon against the nafs
We have little time. The nafs's excuses do not hold.
Scene on the Day of Judgment
People will be naked and the nafs will be overrun by what they witness. It is a stronger weapon.
The sword
Remembrance of mortality, which you must renew.
Renew it weekly
A near-death experience fades. Remind yourself regularly.
His own near-death experience
After release from detention in 2013 he felt reborn and thankful, and 6,000 residency rejections did not bother him. It wore off.
Appreciation
Breathing, the sun, loving his wife and child more.
The detention prayer
In a room of 26 blindfolded people, two taken and killed that day. When called for interrogation he prayed the easiest prayer of his life.
Prophet internalized mortality
He could not be pressed. The Companions had it too.
Without this piece it will not work
The halaqah would harm you.
Assignment: reflect for a minute
Not necessarily lying in a bed. What are you afraid of?
Certainty in resurrection?
Fear of punishment or of nothing?
Next: a harder exercise
The simulation is the easy one. Make peace with it.
Someone who accepts death
Under interrogation they cannot be manipulated.
Not for combat but for quality
Live with intensity, clarity, better motivation.
Sword at the neck of the nafs
The nafs gets power when you neglect this.
Logistics
Aim to finish by 9 once Isha is 7:45. Usher everyone out after the post-Isha talk.

L.title: Mortality: ruh, nafs and the one-week exercise
obj: Announce that mortality continues over several sessions to leave room for discussion, questions and shared experience until most members have made peace with it.
Explain why acceptance of mortality is the most powerful weapon against the nafs, and why the two years of earlier exercises were left without it so members would feel how hard changing the nafs is.
Distinguish the ruh (not afraid of death, since it returns to Allah every night in sleep) from the nafs (terrified of death), and note that pain frightens both.
Show that ignoring death is programmed by the nafs and that tul al-amal is a major sin of the heart (Qushayri ranks it above the four already discussed).
Set the exercise: live one week as if the next Isha is your last, revise choices and raise the intensity of worship and relationships, without rash decisions.
Teach with the bequest rule (a third), the value of Fard prayers, and the parents calculation that this is not about reckless spending or dropping out of school.
Separate healthy fear (shortcomings, not having done enough, missing family) from toxic fear (nothingness, family cannot cope without me), and link regret to tawbah and hope.
Clarify that short-term knowledge of death is a weapon, while long-term knowledge is weak, and that the nafs convinces us our mortality is far away.
topics: Mortality continues as a topic
It will continue until most or all of the group feel they have made progress and come to terms with it.
Why several sessions
To allow discussion, questions and shared experiences so members can make peace with it.
What being at peace means
Not terrified, not letting it ruin your thinking, and using it as motivation.
The most powerful weapon in the toolkit
Without acceptance of mortality you are very weak against the nafs.
Why the earlier exercises were done without it
He let the group feel how hard it is to go against the nafs, so that this topic is taken seriously.
If it was easy, listen less
If changing habits was hard, listen carefully because this is by far the most powerful tool.
The nafs is terrified of death
Only death paralyses and silences the nafs. Pain is second.
Double layering of the human
The nafs gives potential (Adam's ability to learn, think, metacognition) but also pulls you down.
Ruh versus nafs
Ruh: high-level thinking, compassion, selfless action. Nafs: survival and different values.
Link to the black box
Your real values in the black box were set by the nafs. You must replace them and it resists.
Do not kill the nafs
If you kill it, you kill yourself. You tame it.
Mortality is the tool for taming it
The nafs is terrified of it and the ruh is not.
Death is not scary to the ruh
Death is leaving the body and returning to Allah, which the ruh does every night in sleep.
Pain scares both
So talking about Akhirah and azab works on both ruh and nafs.
Euthanasia (MAID) example
People fight back at the last moment because the nafs is not okay with mortality.
Kryptonite
Mortality is the nafs's kryptonite. It becomes a negotiating chip in your hands.
New chapter on pain
Pain is different. The spirit fears it too. To be discussed later.
Advantage over the nafs
Anticipate that you can die at any moment and the nafs falls in line.
Death is the only constant
Every living thing dies. You do not know when or control your heart, liver or kidneys.
Why is it weird that we do not care?
The nafs has programmed us to neglect it and keep it in a blind spot.
Remove the blind spot
You could easily not walk out of the building tonight. The percentage is not zero.
Tul al-amal
A disease of the heart: being convinced you will be fine for a long time.
Qushayri on tul al-amal
In the first centuries, he saw it as the biggest sin of the heart, above arrogance, envy and showing off.
Changing the nafs's attitude
It changes when it sees death at its doorstep.
An unfair advantage
The nafs loses its ability if you are at peace with dying soon.
The one-week experiment
Hard. Only for those mentally stable and mature. Imagine you have a week left, ending after next Isha.
Adam and his progeny
Adam (as) was shown his offspring and a light between the eyes. Dawud's lifespan.
Adam's two problems
He disliked being a servant and being mortal. Khuld, the hope of immortality, was the trap.
Adam nearly asked for his years back
He gave 40 years of his life to Dawud and later wanted them back. Mortality was his ongoing issue.
A 19-year-old with sarcoma
A patient with perhaps 18 months. Do not become a hypochondriac. Accept the uncertainty and make good choices.
Pediatric oncology ward in Damascus
Visiting dying children as a volunteer. The point is peace with this topic.
Everyone died and will die
A Muslim focuses on what comes next and looks forward to meeting Allah, the Prophet (saw) and loved ones.
The exercise stated
If you had one more week after next Isha, what would you do differently? Live the week like that.
Avoid harsh decisions
Talk to him before any big decision. Do not drop out of school.
Result one: quantity
Revise your choices. Stop what is worthless regardless of death date.
Money and the one-third rule
Once you know you are dying, only a third may be given away. The rest goes to heirs.
School is not a waste
Seeking knowledge is the best thing right now. If not, he would say so.
Do not scrap leisure
Time with friends is part of silat al-rahim. Remove the pointless.
Result two: intensity
35 Fard prayers left would be treated differently. A million sunnah do not equal a fard.
Time with parents
A sociologist's calculation: 3 visits a year, 10 years, 30 visits left. And who said you will live that long?
Probabilities and dice
Betting on odds is a mental problem. 'Maybe we live, maybe we do not.'
The sword
Accept it, and the nafs sits in the corner at any moment it opposes your interest.
Tazkiyah impossible without it
In his opinion tazkiyah is impossible without being at peace with mortality.
His childhood in Medina
Learned in a masjid near Masjid Nabawi. As a 7 or 8 year old he told his mother to be ready.
Every moment is a gift
Live as if sustainable, accept it can end any moment, and be okay going back to Allah.
The nafs will fight the last time
A hesitation at the last breath is normal, like a drop that takes a second to leave the spout.
Hadith of the believer leaving the dunya
A long hadith to be narrated word by word next week in an imaginary reflection.
Exercise logistics
Try it for a week, journal, share findings or struggles.
Whatever you feel is normal
There is no doing it wrong. Common threads will appear.
Knowing the time: short vs long
Knowing it is a week or month helps. Knowing it is 20 years is a weapon for the nafs.
The nafs convinces us it is far away
We live on the premise that mortality is decades away. You do not know that.
Student: fear of nothingness
Break it down. What exactly are you afraid of leaving?
Healthy versus toxic fears
Healthy: not enough deeds, missing family. Toxic: family cannot cope without me, nothingness.
Tool needs skill
Accepting mortality will not fix problems by itself.
Student: shortcomings overwhelmed me
Healthy regret. Use it to motivate change, make tawbah.
Case of the one who died with stolen goods
The imam does not lead his funeral prayer. Sin is a problem only if not repented.
Student: regret over past sins
It is fine to regret. The Prophet's companion who wept over his sin until death.
Do not despair
Hope in Allah's promise to those who repent and try.
Renew your tawbah
Tajdid al-tawbah keeps the sin fresh in understanding.
Fear of mortality is healthy
Fear of nothingness is what cripples and depresses.
Debilitating regret
As long as you are trying, you have not given up and hope remains.
Shahadah and martyrdom
Not a guarantee. Do not hope to die in war. Hope to die serving Allah.
Dying while teaching
A sheikh who died mid-lesson. A better death than any.
Husn al-khatimah later
Deferred. Now just accept mortality.
The one-week exercise from his days
He did it once with his teachers. Very hard, then lived that way.
Closing
Think this way at any moment. Life improves without self-help books.

L.title: Walking the path, not owning the outcome
obj: Debrief the one-week exercise (imagine dying after next Isha) as an interactive session, with students sharing what happened.
