Show that a conviction you do not truly believe fades, so the nafs cannot be talked into a lie, though even reflecting on death more often helps.
Show how mortality de-stresses, puts things in perspective, removes the fog around choices (deleting Instagram) and improves both quality and quantity.
Teach that if you are living correctly, almost nothing should change when you imagine a last week. Fix the intention, do not scrap the path (school, work, family, exercise, leisure).
Counter the idea of giving away all your money or dropping out of school. A person who is dying should keep walking the path, as shown by Abdul Rahman Ayyub's story.
Reframe responsibility: you are responsible for walking the path (sirat), not for the outcome, with Mus'ab ibn Umair as the example.
Show the contradiction of longing for the Akhirah while ignoring the death that leads to it.
Replace the nafs's lie ('you will live to 70 or 80') with the true statement ('God willing I will live long, but I may pass away at any moment') and repeat it daily for the week.
topics: Today is more interactive
Students report back on the previous exercise. Some brothers are at the MSA event.
The exercise restated
Treat the coming week as your last. Reflect on emotions, thoughts, struggles and share them.
Not everyone can do it
Depends on imagination and ability to convince yourself. Do it at least once in your life.
The point: familiarity with mortality
By the end of this part of tazkiyah the group should be more comfortable with it.
Student: it faded
The conviction faded afterwards and it was business as usual.
Conviction fades without real belief
Anything you merely talk your nafs into is short-lived. It applies to far more than mortality.
Student: a better week
More thinking, almost acted on it, but not enough to change the past.
Reflecting on death helps even without full belief
It is a lesser weapon than true conviction, but you can settle for it for a while.
Student: stress before a presentation
Death is the biggest de-stressor. It puts everything in perspective.
Some stress is needed
Without any stress you will fail an exam. Death shrinks the excess. Do not use it as an excuse to slack.
Student: deleted Instagram
Mortality removes the fog and shows what is clearly a waste of time.
Boredom afterwards
Fill the gap with beneficial things. Seeking knowledge helps.
Quality and quantity
Death improves quality (khushu, sincerity) and quantity (not only removing, but adding).
The salaf would not change anything
The Companions and the righteous said they would not change their lifestyle if they knew they would die tomorrow or in 40 years.
Do the exercise together
Write down what you would change in your last week.
Student: quality yes, not quantity
Slow some things down, speed others up.
Healthy conclusion
If you live right, nothing should change. If not, a lot should.
Priorities check
What are your top four? Am I doing them? Bring back what you are missing.
Quality of salah, Quran, dhikr and parents
Death helps you improve how you do things, not just what.
Changing an action versus doing it better
Time with parents may be right already. Improve the quality of the meeting.
Student: setting affairs in order
With forewarning you would put affairs in order.
Grief fades into acceptance
Sadness about mortality works like grief. It softens into du'a and action.
Student: obsession with 'more'
Doing more, then checking each action against 'would I do this in my last week?'
A window into your soul
The exercise surfaces emotions and thoughts about your nafs that you can journal.
Death row example
Those told their execution date are heavily medicated. Companions in captivity were calm and close to Allah.
Prophet's verse
'O Allah, there is no life except the life of the Hereafter.' You cannot think of the Akhirah and ignore death.
Ignoring the vehicle
You look forward to Jannah, the shade of Allah, the Prophet and the Hawd, but ignore death that takes you there.
Graduation analogy
Thinking about graduation while ignoring the tests.
Student: would give up school and spend more on Islam
Teacher: that is not your priority. Keep seeking knowledge and fix your intention.
Seeking knowledge includes boring parts
Labour pains of learning. There is more reward in staying than quitting.
You are responsible for the path, not the outcome
You were never responsible for the fruit.
Giving all your money away
The best use of wealth is feeding and clothing yourself and family, then sadaqah. Where is the most ajr?
Danger of rationalizing
Saying 'I would not change anything' can be denial. Most would change one or two things.
Check the boxes
Fajr, work as service, school, family, jama'ah, Quran. If you do these, why change them?
Check for postponed things
Bring a postponed priority closer.
Story of Abdul Rahman Ayyub
A residency friend who died at 45 of stage 4 colorectal cancer. He finished boards, a fellowship and started practice, living 45 months on chemo. He kept going for Allah's sake.
Lesson from his story
Know your priorities. Live so that whenever he takes you, you are ready.
Small additions are fine
Hajj, visiting a distant relative. But do not ditch school, money use, or time use. Do them better.
The nafs's weapon is 'you have a long time'
Your conviction of mortality is a weapon the nafs cannot fight.
Is the nafs telling the truth?
'You will live until 70 or 80' is not truthful. It is a lie of convenience.
The true statement
There is a high likelihood you live long, but a real possibility you pass away at any moment.
His own exercise at 19
Very intense because he convinced himself. Most cannot.
The belief in the lie is the struggle
Planning decades ahead is fine, but you are responsible for the journey, not the outcome.
Goals and the path
Your long-term goal (spreading the deen, strengthening Islam) and what leads to it.
Mus'ab ibn Umair
He gets the reward of all that followed because he was on the path.
You get the reward for what you worked toward
Not just what you completed.
Student: how do I find the path?
The exercise should provoke reflection on what you specifically must offer.
A path is a trajectory
If you lived forever, where is your graph heading in each area?
Sirat
We ask for the straight path because that is what we are responsible for staying on.
Intensity of the relationship with Allah
Joy in dhikr and Quran needs mortality in the middle. No other way.
The lie you could not live
You could not live the lie of dying next week, yet you live the lie of a guaranteed long life.
A lie of convenience
There is a possibility you do not make it home tonight.
Student: same as self-reflection
Yes, everything taught here is repetition of reflection from different angles.
Do not run away from the topic
We get excited about Akhirah but forget we must die to get there.
Experience of death helps
Near-death or the death of someone close. The Companions saw death more often.
Ask the right questions
What should I prioritize? Where does my long-term journey lead? What is best use of my time?
Why not do the better thing now?
If something is better than school, do it. If not, you are being cheated by the wrong intention.
Athleticism and leisure
Keeping fit is an amanah. Leisure supports the end goal.
Be careful of self-deception
Convincing yourself you are doing all the right things when you are not.
The week's goal
Replace the lie of guarantee with the true statement.
Tul al-amal is the lie
One of the worst sins per the salaf. It makes it far enough away to ignore.
Productive worry
It should not be depressing. It should motivate.
His morning practice
The morning du'a reminds him that he has been granted today. This helps him manage stress, failures and calamities.
If not okay with ending tonight
Find out why. Bad choices? Poor quality? Both.
Repeat the sentence for a week
'God willing I will live long, but I may pass at any given moment and this could be the last one.'
Closing
Halaqah continues after Isha. Saturdays at 7:45, Seerah before.

L.title: Commitment, pain and living in extra time
obj: Explain why tazkiyah demands commitment and accountability: someone who half-engages and still feels nothing loses hope, so he does not run the halaqah as an open lecture.
Contrast Islam with cults that keep the goal out of reach, and show that the Sahaba and tabi'in stayed because they found real clarity.
Insist on self-effort: reflection, journaling and mujahadah, since you only retain a fraction of what you are told and everything you work out yourself.
Warn that without a firm grasp of self-value (servitude and humility) and mortality, nothing after it is worth continuing.
Show that the nafs fears only death and pain, wants immortality and comfort, and that acceptance of mortality (and pain) breaks its grip.
Present the stages of grief that accompany accepting mortality and say they are a good sign.
Use 'extra time' (the football analogy), Hanzala's hadith and the Salman and Abu Darda story to show balanced spiritual intensity.
Close with the cure for fear: turn to Allah, as there is no one else to seek refuge in, and handle feeling 'far behind' without giving up.
topics: Why this halaqah exists
Reflections after talking with a student about who attends and what the goal is.
Tazkiyah as the missing link
Those who do nothing can blame the missing step. Those who do it and still fail have nothing left to blame.
The danger of half-engagement
You lose hope and he may harm you. That is why he does not run it open.
Cult comparison
Cults always dangle one impossible step. Islam is clear truth and attainable.
Why not public
Without continuity, accountability and discussion it does not help and causes cognitive dissonance.
Strict teachers he attended
He was kicked out of one. Now he understands why they were strict.
The Sahaba stayed
They found clarity, serenity and joy. Islam grew stronger after the Prophet (saw) and the tabi'in are giants.
No magician
Presence of the Prophet (saw) was half the effect but they still had to put in the work.
Better not to attend than to fail with hope lost
If you try seriously and fail, you cannot blame the audience, which strengthens the nafs against you.
Make a decision about commitment
Do the tasks and think. He can tell if you did not.
You retain what you work out
You get maybe half from him. Reflection and journaling are required.
Blame me, not Islam
His fear is that you conclude it does not work.
Tazkiyah is going against desires
Few do this without a reason. The nafs cannot take you where you will be happy.
Modern psychology validates every feeling
Human instinct is not always good. Feelings are not blame but should not be validated blindly.
Constant muhasabah
Rest and you lose ground. Climbing a mountain needs ongoing struggle.
Mortality is the most uncomfortable thing
But without it, why are we doing this?
Sahaba's lifestyle seems insane
They would look at us and ask how we know about death and the Akhirah and live like this.
Your jihad is self-control
Harder than carrying a rifle.
Two prerequisites
Self-value and mortality. If these are not clear, do not continue.
The lie of convenience
You rejected the lie of dying next week but accepted the lie of 70 or 80 years.
The truth
You likely live long but there is a real possibility of dying at any moment. Outside religion too.
Behavior reflects belief
Procrastination comes from believing you have 70 years. Impossible to change that way.
Weapon of tazkiyah
The nafs will not submit without acceptance of mortality.
The nafs's two fears
Death and pain. Pain tolerance rises, so it is less reliable.
What the nafs wants
Immortality: wealth, power, comfort. Love your nafs but explain we will die anyway.
Life is reaction to pain
Sternal rub as a test for responsiveness. Pain is part of life and must be accepted.
Before the adhkar and the du'as
Without these basic realizations, any spiritual high is temporary.
What the Prophet (saw) said
'We are all going to die soon and the Akhirah is scary.' The Sahaba dedicated the rest of their lives.
Your whole life is following the Book
School, gym, friends and parents are all worship.
A hundred years from now
Everyone present will be dead. 100 years is nothing against the universe.
What matters is what you do
Old people were once like you.
Acceptance brings sadness then liberation
You will feel sad, depressed and anxious, then free.
Someone who accepts death cannot be threatened
Movie characters who hold their ground. Non-Muslims who accept mortality at the oncology ward.
What did Islam offer?
If akhirah is not something you look forward to, what was the shahadah for?
Living in extra time
His teacher's football analogy: stoppage time with the referee holding the whistle.
You will feel depressed
If not, you have not done it. Grief stages: denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance.
Time management is not the issue
Acceptance lets you do what you are doing fully, present.
Student: do I remind myself every time?
Once you accept it, it is a quick fix that brings you back.
Hadith of Hanzala
Hanzala felt a hypocrite after the Prophet's gatherings. 'If you were as you are with me, the angels would shake your hands.'
The spiritual high is a gift to enjoy
But duties like family and work come first.
Salman and Abu Darda
Abu Darda neglected his wife. The Prophet said, 'Your wife has a right over you.'
The dynamic is the opposite
The Prophet had to say 'go take care of your family'. Today we must beg people. Two hurdles: self-value and mortality.
Never achieving perfection
Work toward functional: academics, career, relationships working and enjoyed.
Student coaching on self-value
Months of repeating before it sank in. The nafs pushes back.
Turn to Allah
With mortality there is no one else to seek refuge in. This makes the relationship real.
Next week: the hadith of death
The Prophet's description, narrated in Arabic with a guided reflection.
Why a group
Sahaba went through emotions together.
Student: feel far behind
A healthy feeling if it motivates. Shaytan's oldest trick is to convince you there is no hope.
Next step approach
Where am I, where am I going, what is the next step. Do not paralyze yourself with everything.
Mortality shrinks other fears
Life is managing stress. Value things appropriately.
Closing
Mus'ab and Umar walked the path sincerely, died early, and got the reward.

L.title: Death as a transition, not lights out
obj: Review the weeks of mortality teaching and explain that abstract realities need long repetition, so do not expect quick results.
Argue from the opposite side: immortality does not work for humans (excitement, then aimlessness), so mortality is a necessary stage before the immortal life of the Hereafter.
State that an atheist who sees death as lights out should ignore it, while a Muslim cannot, because death is a transition (barzakh) into a different reality.
Redirect the fear: a Muslim fears lost opportunity for deeds and tawbah and the account, not lights out or missing the Super Bowl or weddings.
Teach that the real fear is meeting Allah on the wrong terms, so husn al-khatimah is the focus, with examples from Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali and Bilal.
Explain what happens on the Day of Judgment: the nafs is gone as the voice of resistance, you are left with the consequences, and the best du'a and salah is offered too late.
Connect disbelief in the resurrection (ba'th) to the Arabs of the Quran who believed in God but treated death as the end.
Admit the earlier exercises were set to fail, so the group could see they cannot accept 'lights out', and set up the guided barzakh and resurrection reflections that follow.
topics: Eight weeks of mortality
He covered it from many angles. Abstract concepts need repetition.
Repetition takes time
Humbleness and self-value took about 15 months. Do not expect mortality in record time.
The nafs distracts you from death
Getting over this hurdle lets you appreciate life and function as a liberated servant.
The opposite: immortality
Why did Adam want it? Try the mirror image.
Novels about immortality
Authors almost always reintroduce death. We cannot fathom immortality.
Immortality brings aimlessness
Excitement at first, then purposelessness. Fountain of youth myths.
Sunday blues analogy
The excitement of the first day of a week off, the dread of the day before returning.
Immortality is for the next life
Khalidin fiha, but you need to change first. This life is a necessary stage.
Opposite hurdles
Immortality: excited then empty. Mortality: heavy first, then better.
Living the truth is reward enough
If nothing else, you are not living a lie.
An atheist should ignore death
Do not think about it, limit grieving. Funnily, most believers behave this way.
A Muslim cannot do the same
Death for the believer is a transition, like birth is painful for an infant.
Barzakh
A space between spaces, a transition to a different reality.
What is lost at death
Freedom of choice, ability to repent and do good, and being held to account.
What you should fear
Not missing life, the Super Bowl or weddings. The worry is whether we meet again on good terms.
Who will surround you?
Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab versus the righteous. Final goodbye versus 'see you later'.
Visiting the graves
'Peace upon you, abode of believers. We are following you.'
You still see death as the end
Impossible to accept. If so, stop attending and ignore it.
Death as the end of a chapter
A critical chapter that defines what follows.
Husn al-khatimah
The Prophet's frequent du'a for a good ending. The plot ending on the wrong side.
Sheikh Muhammad al-Ghazali
Died of a heart attack mid-lesson. Better to work on dying doing the right thing.
Why simulations failed
If you see it as lights out you can only imagine life.
The opposite of life is spiritual non-existence
Not a body decaying but loss of awareness and control.
You lose control
Right now you hold the driver's seat. After death you do not.
Nafs's fear of leaving the body
The nafs was born when the spirit met the body and fears detaching.
Student discussion: does the nafs exist on Judgment Day?
Qarin, the aspects of resistance and the spiritual high.
On the Day of Judgment
No one is bored of worship or tempted. Everyone is at the highest iman, but it is too late.
Nafs defends itself from punishment
It fears pain and death. You are left with the consequences of kibr and shirk.
Why the nafs fears dying
A part of its existence leaves. People push back before death.
Calm beats fear
Preparation for husn al-khatimah brings calm.
Abu Bakr and Aisha
'Do not say that. Make du'a for mercy and forgiveness.'
Umar
Asked that his face be placed on the soil to be humble before Allah.
Uthman
Read Quran as he was killed, because the Prophet told him that his death would quiet a fitnah.
Ali and Bilal
Ali was killed at fajr. Bilal woke smiling: 'Tomorrow I meet the beloved ones, Muhammad and his companions.'
Their fear was due diligence
Did I do enough? Am I going to make it?
The Day of Judgment's regret
Your spirit needs cleansing and does not understand why it did these things without the nafs's voice.
Like looking at yourself 10 years ago
You cannot explain why you did it. 'Aflaha man zakkaha.'
Blaming others
People will ask 'how could you let me do this' and say 'you did not stop me'.
The best salah on Judgment Day is too late
Du'a in the billions is meaningless then. Now is the time to strive against the nagging voice.
You are stronger than your nafs
But you live in a web of lies. Death is one of the biggest.
The Quran's number one issue
Idolatry and denial of ba'th and nushur. The Arabs believed in God but no resurrection.
The Arabs' compromise
Believing in God, treating death as the end. 'Who will revive bones?'
The exercises were fraudulent
Intentionally. He wanted you to find that you cannot accept 'lights out'.
Nobody said it worked
You can only accept mortality as moving on.
The nafs will fight at death
You will still be calm because you know better.
The fear shifts
From lights out to losing the ability to do deeds and tawbah.
His work experience
Seen people die in many ways. The best is a peaceful passing.
End of chapter one
Chapter two is written by chapter one. Your fear becomes healthy.
Loved ones will die
You will bury some, some will bury you. See you later, not goodbye.
Redo the earlier exercises
Simulate and give yourself a deadline, with this new lens.
Plan: walk through the stages weekly
Barzakh and the Day of Judgment, from the Quran only. Eyes closed or lights dimmed.
The Prophet looked to the Akhirah
In dunya, eyesight on Yawm al-Qiyamah. This does not make you less productive.
The sheep hadith
He gave all the meat away and said what remains is what is gone (given). The rest is waiting for us.
Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik and Abu Hazim
'Why do we love the dunya and hate death?' 'You built the dunya and ruined the Akhirah, so you hate moving from a built place to a ruin.'
Sulayman's final act
He died within the month and named Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as successor.
Closing
If it is lights out, do not waste time. If Muslim, prepare. Make sure absentees listen to this one.

L.title: Tafakkur: learning to contemplate
obj: Pause the barzakh and resurrection reflections to teach tafakkur (contemplation), since many members have no experience with real reflection.
Show that the Prophet (saw) practiced contemplation in Hira, and that i'tikaf is the continuing sunnah form of a spiritual retreat.
Set the exercise: 15 minutes every day for a week, undistracted, on one topic of your choice that you have been avoiding.
Teach how to contemplate: stay with the thought, let feelings pass, argue for and against it, and then research the open facts and ask questions.
Distinguish contemplation from obsession and from venting to others, and show how it builds convictions (honesty, the shahadah) rather than imported opinions.
Explain why this is needed before the guided narration of death, since Quran, salah and dhikr need the same skill.
Contrast real spirituality with cheap highs, noting that long qiyam and Dawud's weekly worship were joyful because of calm reflection.
topics: Plan for the next sessions
Slow narration from hadith and Quran in Arabic and English. He wants high reflection, not high emotion.
Little experience with reflection
Discovered through talking to students, including the sisters' side.
He grew up with less distraction
Less TV and devices meant you learned to entertain yourself, which is a kind of reflection.
The brain is chaotic and that is fine
Like a washing machine. You cannot have chaos outside and chaos inside.
Calm is required
Running at 100 mph, you cannot dive into a concept.
Hira
What sparked the Prophet's (saw) prophecy was contemplation. He stayed there months, sometimes days at a time.
What he did in the cave
Scholars call it tafakkur. There was nothing else to do.
Why he is putting the cart before the horse
If you cannot reflect, you cannot benefit from salah, du'a, adhkar and Quran.
Contemplate what is distracting you
If it is already thought through, reflection removes the nagging thought.
The Prophet's isolation
No phone, no communication, no drugs or alcohol, no people.
Messaging is not contemplation
Checking messages keeps you in conversation.
Tafakkur, ta'ammul, tadabbur
Established Islamic practices of the Prophet and Sahaba.
Learning to mute the surroundings
He memorized in noisy huffaz circles and learned to focus.
What will happen if you cannot
You will be bored in the first minute or two when the narration starts.
The exercise: 15 minutes a day
Schedule it. Tie it to a prayer, such as after Fajr or late at night.
It will feel awkward
You may laugh at yourself at first. The brain is a powerful tool to tame.
Choose your own topic
Something unresolved in your life. It need not be religious.
Most thinking lasts 50 seconds
Contemplation means staying with the thought and not running away.
Avoidance examples
The failed exam report, the unopened file, the box you do not want to sort.
Feelings pass
You will be upset or ashamed, then fine. Then you can learn what to fix.
Why the Prophet contemplated
He knew his grandfather Ibrahim was a prophet and that idols were baseless, but lacked answers.
We have the answers
Allah answered them, so we do not repeat that. We contemplate how to walk the path.
Closest sunnah: i'tikaf
A spiritual retreat in the masjid. Recommended to do it outside Ramadan too.
The Prophet's i'tikaf
He made a covered spot in the masjid. He had already contemplated a lot but we need it more.
Write it down
Notes let you build on thoughts later. A retreat of a couple of days helps.
Values come from deep thought
You will not become honest by deciding. You must contemplate honesty and dishonesty in depth.
Like attending 30 debates
Contemplation is an internal debate with the devil's advocate.
Do it alone, not only in the halaqah
Otherwise he cannot build on what you have thought.
His childhood and his son
Staring at clouds for hours. Today's kids are overscheduled and have no downtime.
Brain works even when you do nothing
Sit with the thought and let it process.
Example: a confrontation
Why did they do that? Did I start it? What should I have said? Rehearse the endings.
Close the case
Pick the best response for next time so you need not feel ashamed or discuss it with many people.
Venting is cheap contemplation
Talking to others complicates it and starts rumours. Think first.
Argue against your own view
Play devil's advocate. That strengthens the argument or exposes a weak one.
Why you are Muslim
If you inherited it and did not argue against la ilaha illa Allah, that is a problem.
Link to mortality
Maybe death is hard to accept because you have not argued it to conviction.
Choose a lane
Contemplate deeply or import someone else's beliefs.
Depth matters
Specialists get annoyed by superficial thoughts. Step number two of a million.
Contemplation then research
After 15 minutes you will have questions that need facts. Look them up and contemplate again.
Then ask questions
Good questions show a person is thinking.
Tafakkur needs knowledge
But they are different activities.
Reflect on every topic here
Think about each lesson for 10 to 15 minutes a day. Conversation becomes more profound.
Do it undistracted
Not while driving, jogging or eating. Learn to be calm. Slow is fine.
Why prepare for narration
So you can imagine the story and let it sink into the subconscious.
Cheap spiritual highs
Concerts and jumping crowds versus real, profound spirituality.
Long qiyam
They prayed four to six hours in his own training. Those who could not reflect wanted out within half an hour.
Dawud (as)
Set aside time each week for worship alone.
Reflection on Quran
Have you taken one verse and kept reading until it spoke to you?
Student: regret about the first two years
Teacher: it is fine and we can revisit any topic.
Method of the halaqah
He gives challenging ideas. You think for a week, then come to argue or ask.
The nafs is sneaky
You will not know what is you and what is it unless you reflect.
Assignment
Schedule 15 minutes, sit facing the qiblah, choose a topic you avoid.
Not doing the exercise until comfortable
He will not start the guided narration until the group is comfortable with reflection.
Not meditation
Tafakkur has been part of Islam for 1400 years. You are commanded to do it.
Obsession versus contemplation
Obsession repeats. Contemplation analyses from angles.
Choose what you avoid
So you feel its benefit. 15 minutes a day achieves a lot.

L.title: Contemplation in practice: the ball of yarn
obj: Debrief the first week of daily contemplation, since most had never learned how to reflect and failed by choosing topics that were too big or too simple.
Teach how to contemplate: isolate one thread at a time (ball of yarn), build over multiple sessions, document thoughts, and zoom out when overwhelmed.
Show that the qalb and fu'ad keep processing after the 15 minutes, so write down thoughts as they come.
Teach the method: ask why repeatedly to find the root cause, then toy with solutions (even silly ones), try one in life and revise.
Explain that contemplation is the only way to grasp abstract concepts (Allah, mortality, humility), and that intellectual stimulation is a higher joy than the senses.
Challenge the 'I can't' of procrastination as a sign that you are not in control, and warn that people leave the masjid after about two years because they never find fulfilment.
Remind the group of the first four daily contemplations (ubudiyyah, ihsan, tashih al-niyyah, qubul al-a'mal) and the thoughts, emotions, actions triangle.
Set next week: another 15 minutes a day on a harder topic, documented, with a joke fine for missed days.
topics: His mistake
He assumed contemplation was common. Now he will revisit earlier concepts so the group can connect with them.
Who tried 15 minutes a day
Feedback requested. First student: first day went well, later days garbage, felt like standing in a ring with 20 thoughts.
Student: failure was not isolating one thought
Superficial and distracted by other thoughts.
Brain always works
He reviews the structure: nafs, ruh, 'aql, fu'ad (conscious) and qalb (subconscious).
Contemplation is laying track
Your 15 minutes sends the train on its way. Thoughts come all day.
Always document
He often loses thoughts during patients. Write it down.
Common mistake: topic too narrow
Tafakkur and tadabbur need several sittings.
Boxing ring versus a string
A topic too big overwhelms you. Pull one string from a ball of yarn slowly.
Yarn analogy
Pulling fast tangles everything. Who has the patience to pull one at a time?
Do not rush
If you are rushed, stop the session. Build the habit first with 15 minutes.
Zoom out when overwhelmed
Take one thing and set the others aside. He keeps lots of notes on his phone.
Make the sessions joyful
Thinking about yourself should be easy to enjoy, unlike dhikr, which needs a relationship.
Student: asking why and implementing
How to turn insight into life changes.
Find the root source
Keep asking why until you find a childhood problem, habit or conviction. Then contemplate the change.
Nothing is an algorithm
You cannot put it in AI. He teaches skill sets.
Stone wall
Same question, same answer means zoom out and ask for specific guidance, after walking 80% yourself.
Toy with ideas
Creativity comes from toying. Think silly solutions. You learn more from wrong paths.
Try something in your life
Change one thing and see. If it fails, try the next hypothesis.
Practical approach beyond 'read more Quran'
You still need practical ways to handle reactions and plan the future.
Contemplation makes abstract concepts usable
Mortality and humility need it, as do Allah and the ghayb.
Ghayb is not without evidence
It is accessed by the mind, not the senses.
Senses versus mind
Human beings love sense stimulation (food, sex). Becoming an intellectual means shifting toward the mind.
Contemplation elevates you
More dopamine from figuring things out than from food. The scientist's eureka moment.
Student: two strings are tangled
Find your first string. It is usually self-value or mortality.
Observe the competing ideas
Each interrupting idea is information. Shredded paper analogy.
Why seek knowledge
How do you know what to seek unless you reflect on what you do not know?
Islam is simple
Pray, avoid haram, do good, be honest. Hard things are surgery or roofing in July.
Why can't you?
'I can't' is a sign you are not in control. Why not do the right?
Different value systems exist
Some are taught to get ahead at any cost. You chose better values, so be them.
Procrastination is a made-up word
It means you are not in control, because you have not reflected on what is inside.
Why people leave
He sees people attend for about two years, leave, come back. They look for fulfillment and do not find it.
What happens if you contemplate honesty daily for a month?
It sinks from superficial to solid.
The first four daily contemplations
Ubudiyyah, ihsan, tashih al-niyyah and qubul al-a'mal.
Do not get sick of it
If you hit the same wall, zoom out, add knowledge, ask. Conclusions become solid.
Plan for the next weeks
Questions about contemplation sessions until everyone feels comfortable.
Student: after seeking knowledge, will the habit end?
You go back and contemplate with the new material.
What the finish line looks like
Contemplating the negativity reduces the habit. Find the source. Change it or ask a specific question.
Thoughts, emotions, actions
The triangle. Stimulating thoughts and actions together brings the emotions along.
Hawa becomes aligned
You will fall in love with Allah and His Prophet, but it takes time.
Student: it is just contemplation
He agrees. Stare at the ugliness until you are no longer scared or embarrassed.
No one is perfect
There are things he still does not touch. The list should shrink to two or three.
Knowing what you avoid
Contemplation shows what you are not contemplating.
Student: lanes of a highway
It is normal. Isolate one lane.
Build a ritual
Same time, same place, deep breaths, a short reminder. Lower your heart rate.
Regulating reactions
If it excites or upsets you, calm down again and continue.
Student: overarching concepts
Hard to stop. Choose situational topics. Learn to put a pin in it.
The Prophet's six months
Once you learn to contemplate you could do it for long. He had no Quran.
Allah answered those questions for him
We start ahead of the Sahaba, but maybe we never contemplated existence for ourselves.
Your wife may complain
Constant thinking affects marriage. Find time at work for 30 minutes.
Quran halaqah noise
White-noise the background. A prophetic skill.
The Prophet's i'tikaf
Four or five times a year. Read Quran as a guide for contemplation.
Be comfortable with yourself
From books to radio to TV to phones, we escape ourselves, then feel depressed at night.
The nafs hates being figured out
It wants you in the dark thinking you are in control.
Mortality as a topic
Mortality becomes less terrifying once seen as a transition.
Next week
He will check on contemplation. Send messages if useful. The topic is open but must be meaningful.
Tongue-in-cheek fine
$10 for each missed day.
Choose a harder topic
Not too simple (finished on day one) and not too big. Do cause analysis and then solutions.
Closing
Move to next steps: do not just collect pieces of information.

L.title: Catching ideas and the four daily contemplations
obj: Announce the last session before a few weeks off and set the homework for the break.
Recap the halaqah's history: started September 2022, split into two groups, then merged back, and explain that the problem is not numbers but whether people reflect between sessions.
Argue that proficiency in any field (and in tazkiyah) needs time spent thinking outside required hours, unlike certificates that only prove attendance.
Teach being present in the moment, and why superficial ideas are worthless without depth gained through reflection.
Use the bird-in-a-cage and fishing-line images to show that reflection captures free-floating ideas so they become part of you, and compare to nightly daydreams that become goals.
Show that the nafs runs from the hated task to a less hated one (even contemplation), so focus is a form of control.
Assign the four daily contemplations from the start of the halaqah (ubudiyyah, ihsan, tashih al-niyyah, qubul al-a'mal) for 15 minutes a day.
Warn that video-game addiction destroys contemplation and urge counting the hours spent.
topics: Last session before the break
A few weeks off. He usually gives homework.
History of the halaqah
Began September 2022, split into groups a year later, merged back after burnout.
The method
He gives a thought, you reflect, he adds the next week.
Discovered gap in progress
Reflection was not as clear as he thought. People waited a week and relied on his hour.
Proficiency requires time outside class
Hours of thinking beyond study make you good in a field.
Certification versus competency
A degree shows attendance. In Islamic fields it was not always like this.
Cramming is not a life skill
Four years of exams does not teach creating or innovating.
Beyond tazkiyah
How to do anything well: relationships, jobs, books, engaging in the moment.
Life is the moment
Do not live in the past or future. Plan and contemplate intentionally.
Superficial ideas are worthless
90 percent are wrong and everyone has the same ones. Reflection finds hidden angles.
Prioritize reflection in the break
If exams are done, use the time. The Quran commands thinking and the Prophet began with six months in Hira.
Kites and birds in your mind
Ideas are in a closed space flying around. Reflection cages and examines them.
Describing what you caught
Measure the beak, eye colour. Decide whether to keep or release the bird.
Why people struggle
A highway of ideas with none of depth. Reflection catches one and reels it in like a fish.
Patience
Too tight breaks the line. Too loose and it escapes. An art that becomes enjoyable.
You already contemplate things you like
You play movies in your head before sleep.
Nightly dreaming becomes a goal
Imagining medical school every night turns the dream into a goal. The power of the subconscious.
Tazkiyah means practicing it well
Do you pray all five prayers with serenity, or just to get it out of the way?
Daydreaming is contemplation
Kids stopped daydreaming after TV and phones.
Powerful tool shaping who you are
Humility and mortality are wasted if not contemplated.
Lectures are wasted without contemplation
Old hajis have heard everything. He cannot reinforce for you daily.
Why you replay certain clips
Your qalb is thirsty for depth. You know there is more but are too lazy to write and think.
Thinking is chaotic but a process
Newton's apple was step 150,000 after stacks of work.
Contemplate what matters
Who am I, why am I here, where am I going, am I in control or a slave?
Put in the hours
You become more efficient.
How many hours to study a course?
Not time but quality of focus.
The nafs's priorities
It prefers the phone, then the second best thing like thinking about something unrelated, over what it hates.
Contemplation lets you control it
Focus is control.
Homework for the break
Return to the four daily contemplations from the start.
1. Ubudiyyah
What does it mean to be Allah's servant and the best servant?
2. Ihsan
Everything has an outward and spiritual side. Islam, Iman, Ihsan from the hadith of Jibril.
3. Tashih al-niyyah
Check your intention before each action.
4. Qubul al-a'mal
You have no evidence any deed is accepted. All your deeds are pending.
15 minutes with a journal
Choose one a day, journal, review and build. Two months of daily thought transforms understanding.
His own habit for 23 years
Daily reflection on at least one. Niyyah and qubul never end because you do new things.
Pulling out of things for niyyah
He stopped actions when he could not identify his intention.
Ihsan and ubudiyyah are saturating
You reach a feeling of fullness.
Quran practice
Take two or three verses a week and think. Ask what the Prophet's state of mind was and how the Sahaba received it.
Iblis has deprived your generation
Joy of contemplation lost, and socialization too.
Video games
Heavily encouraged to cut down. His friend's Ultimate Team and brother's Counter-Strike.
Addiction similar to substances
Neuroscience compares it to cocaine. It is a modern form of slavery.
You cannot reflect with an itch
Hunger, tiredness or addiction blocks contemplation.
Count your hours
Add up weekly and monthly. It harms Quran, health, sleep and studies.

L.title: Three goals of tazkiyah: clarity, closeness, control
obj: Teach a breathing-based way to start contemplation: exhale with the name of Allah, acknowledge racing thoughts, set them aside, then pick one thought.
Explain that tazkiyah is a slow process without 'aha moments' and that people avoid it because they want quick results.
State the three end goals of tazkiyah: clarity and presence in the moment, closeness to Allah, and self-control with consistent ethics.
Explain the origin of practices like the whirling dervishes and Quran-swaying as tools for clarity, not entertainment.
Teach that the nafs camouflages selfish motives with good reasons, so self-control means seeing through it.
Show that closeness to Allah is infinite, so the path has no finish line and growing closeness reveals how far you are.
Debrief the break's contemplation attempts: wandering thoughts, prioritization, playing scenarios like a movie, and the nagging thought as the first thread.
Teach contemplating the past (tawbah) and the future (planning), the benefit of doing it after Fajr or before sleep, and slowing the heart rate.
topics: Breathing technique
Breathe, say Allah's name on each exhale, and acknowledge racing thoughts before settling.
One thought at a time is a skill
We are used to chaos. It takes time to hold a single thought.
No aha moments
Tazkiyah is slow, like exercise. People want quick results like protein shakes.
Small increments
Over 100 or 200 weeks you will move a few centimeters in the right direction.
What is the end game?
Three goals to keep in mind.
Goal 1: clarity
Presence in the moment, which supports khushu and joy in worship.
Practices come from clarity
Scholars of tazkiyah all aimed at it. Whirling in Konya was meant to clear racing thoughts.
Repetitive movement helps
Students swaying while reading Quran release excess energy.
Practices without meaning
People copy the activity without understanding the goal.
A quiet space
Drop a thought in like a fish in a fishbowl and watch.
Clarity in worship
Focus on a word of dhikr, the Quran in salah, ruku.
Living in different tenses
In salah you may be in the past or future. Choose times to plan and reflect.
Joy makes time fly
You lose time only when you enjoy something. Otherwise time drags.
Goal 2: closeness to Allah
Piggybacks on clarity. Some stoics and yogis get clarity without God.
Goal 3: self-control
Not guided by impulse or the camouflaging nafs.
The nafs camouflages motives
It dresses selfish, bitter or petty choices as good reasons.
Consistency of ethics
If you are kind you are always kind. You disable the buttons.
Hands on the steering wheel
You are no longer in the passenger seat.
Three goals in a nutshell
Even if you leave this group, this is what you aim for.
Remove diseases of the heart
Vanity, arrogance, ostentation, envy, laziness, lust.
The closer you get, the farther you realize you are
Like knowledge: the bubble pops and you see how big the sphere is.
There is no finish line
Allah is infinite, so closeness is infinite, including in Jannah.
Debrief after the break
A student found it easier to think about bad things.
Acknowledge intruding thoughts
Like someone opening the door during a conversation. Wait, then continue.
The brain runs on two levels
The subconscious has been working on the thought that jumped in.
Only a minute or two of real contemplation
The rest is setting the scene and calming down.
Heart rate and breathing
Slow breathing, calm heart. Falling asleep is fine. Hibernation analogy.
Contemplation becomes enjoyable
Adhkar, Quran and du'a in that state are more enjoyable.
Everyone is different
No cookie-cutter system.
Student: prioritization
Set a priority list. Racing thoughts decrease when your subconscious trusts the system.
Start with the right thread
Self-value and humility come first.
Why mortality is hard to prioritize
Maybe it is not yet important to you.
Biggest challenge
Focusing on one thought.
Playing scenarios
A student plays it out like a movie. He uses the same trick: keep outcomes you like, scrap the rest.
Student: same thought keeps returning
It means something is missing. A settled thought goes into your value system.
The one you avoid is the one to do first
Fears, trauma or embarrassing memories. Allah will ask about it.
Hypochondriacs
They avoid thoughts of death. Contemplating it solves half of the problem.
Student: what to do with the past
Either what could be better or what not to repeat.
Tawbah as contemplation
Contemplate the past (do I regret it?) and the future (how not to repeat it).
Student: when to do it
After Fajr or before bed.
Imams and the qiblah after Fajr
Classical imams stayed seated facing the qiblah until sunrise.
Student: gym walking
Works. Fajr is a good time with barakah in the early hours.
Plan: a few more weeks
Notes, sharing, making it habitual.
Benefits beyond
Calm in exams and anxiety. He has used it in hard moments.

L.title: Contemplating the concepts of salah
obj: Admit that contemplation is harder for most members than expected, so training continues, and announce i'tikaf nights in Ramadan with real reflection time.
Teach that contemplation is the portal for any abstract idea to sink in and become a reflex, with the Prophet (saw) keeping the habit of Hira after revelation through i'tikaf.
Assign a concrete topic: the six core concepts of salah (takbir, Quran, tasbih in ruku, hamd, du'a, istighfar) and how to give each an immediate personal meaning.
Show how contemplating, hitting a roadblock, seeking knowledge and returning builds meaning, so each movement of prayer becomes enjoyable.
Teach the preparation principle: most of the time goes to calming down, and three or four solid minutes of thought is a great outcome.
Debrief the week: breathing helps even when agitated, and success builds on success.
Explain through creative-process examples (Jarir and al-Farazdaq's rival) that tafakkur is centralizing a thought and letting the brain marinate it.
topics: Contemplation is harder than thought
He will do training so members can learn to take a thought and sit with it.
Contemplation is the portal
No abstract idea sinks in without it.
Ramadan plan
A few nights of proper i'tikaf, where the majority of time is spent thinking.
The Prophet and Hira
Hira stayed with him after Jibril came. i'tikaf for 10 days in Ramadan and from the first year in Medina.
What people do in i'tikaf
Mostly Quran and prayer, zero thinking. The Prophet's was 24/7 in the masjid.
Not playing cards in the masjid
For children something fun is fine. Adults set the example.
Why contemplate
To make an idea part of who you are, a reflex, instead of something to remind yourself of.
Ten minutes is not enough
Mastery takes long hours. You have already done many hours commuting or at a bus stop.
Starter topic: concepts in salah
Think about the movements and what each stands for.
Takbir
Allah as the most important thing, prioritized above all.
Quran in qiyam
What does the word of Allah mean to you? He is speaking to you.
Words must become a reality
Ask where in your life it is not the case.
Ruku and tasbih
The most complex concept. What does exalting God mean? A relationship no other faith has.
Every tasbih should land
Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim should evoke a feeling and understanding.
Roadblocks
You hit what you know. Seek knowledge, add material, return and think again.
Du'a
Why do you make du'a? Quran is Allah speaking to you, du'a is you speaking to Him.
Istighfar and hamd
Istighfar should connect to regret and shortcomings. Hamd is gratitude.
Immediate meaning for each
So each transition in salah brings a familiar, enjoyable concept.
Which is more pleasurable?
The person praying does not know which state is sweeter, which explains the Prophet's salah.
This is a method, not the method
The key is clarity.
Set aside thoughts that force themselves
Postpone them. You control the thought process.
Student: contemplate what I know now?
Yes, then seek knowledge to add material.
Salah will improve soon
Movements become easy and beloved when you know what to think.
Calm the heart rate
Breathing, exhale through the name of Allah, repeat when distracted.
Preparation takes more than the act
A procedure takes 15 minutes after 45 minutes of preparation. His workshop took a lifetime of work.
Three or four solid minutes is great
Do not despair. You are not expected to contemplate for long yet.
Assignment
Take one salah concept and contemplate it a lot, then see how it affects your prayer.
Student: imagining holding things back
The things you imagine you are holding back need attention.
Success builds
Early successes feel nice and build on each other.
Be at peace with the chaos
Mind is not an algorithm.
Creativity needs intuition
Creative people spend time not thinking about it to let a spark come.
Jarir and al-Farazdaq
The poet who was humiliated by Jarir's verse and disappeared. Jarir's creative process was wrestling in the sand.
Tafakkur is centralizing
Remove distractions, let it marinate in the subconscious, allow room.
Islamic behavior
Allah commands reflection often. Ramadan i'tikaf will be a real attempt.
Longer than three or four minutes
Not just a short time.
Logistics
Workshop at 10, food after.

L.title: Impact of each salah concept, and an intro to envy
obj: Extend the salah-concepts contemplation by teaching the method: for each concept, ask what feeds into it (why do you conclude it) and what impact it has on you.
Illustrate impacts: tasbih gives trust, istighfar gives hope and fresh starts, hamd gives optimism and love.
Explain that contemplation is lecturing your nafs and that showing it the benefit (the carrot) wins its cooperation.
Promise that when each movement of prayer is clear and beloved, salah becomes a sequence of ease and joy (Ibn al-Qayyim).
Introduce the next topic: envy (hasad), the third of the four cardinal diseases of the heart after vanity and arrogance.
Define envy as not wanting the other person to have it, regardless of wanting it yourself, and distinguish it from jealousy and from wanting the same.
Teach that envy of dunya things is disqualifying, while envy about akhirah things (like hifz) is the real concern, and that envy is an alarm showing where you still derive self-value.
topics: Six themes of salah restated
Takbir, Quran, tasbih, hamd, du'a, istighfar.
Contemplating tasbih
Allah is flawless, and no fault lies with Him. How does this affect you?
Two prompts for every concept
What feeds into it, and what branches out. What do you base the conclusion on, and what does it do for you?
Impact of tasbih: trust
You trust Allah's wisdom more and do not question what happens to you.
Impact of istighfar: hope
Fresh starts and moving on from the past.
Impact of hamd: optimism and love
Gratitude turns into love and a desire to give back.
Contemplation is looking from angles
Like walking around an object. Do not just stare at the concept.
Give your nafs a carrot
Show it the benefit so it supports the habit.
Contemplation as lecturing the nafs
Like lecturing a student who is not listening. It may take a hundred tries.
Each movement clicks
When the concept is clear, that movement becomes the most enjoyable part.
Ibn al-Qayyim
Moving from one moment of ease and beauty to another.
Upset if the imam is too quick
Because you did not get to enjoy the moment.
Instruction for the next weeks
Slow your heart, find an empty spot on the road, place the thought. One or two minutes is fine at first.
Seek knowledge when stuck
Learn more so there is material to contemplate.
New topic: envy
To freshen up the halaqah. The four heart diseases: vanity, arrogance, envy and one more.
Vanity and arrogance were covered
Vanity is removed by hamd and arrogance by istighfar.
Hasad (envy) vs jealousy
Jealousy can be positive. Envy is one of the most detrimental diseases.
All four are interconnected
Vanity is how you see yourself, arrogance compares you to others.
Class defines envy
Wanting it for yourself, wishing the person worse, etc.
Teacher's definition
Envy is not wanting them to have it. It has nothing to do with wanting it yourself.
Children and envy
A child proud of a toy becomes upset when a friend has it too.
Envy in children is funny
Give a child two chocolates and see him calculate. Not funny in an adult.
Envy is a pain at someone else's good
Not a classy wanting.
Dunya versus akhirah envy
Scholars do not even discuss dunya envy. It is not worth it.
Envy of akhirah things
Someone who memorized the Quran and you feel closed. This is what concerns scholars.
Inqibad
A tightening in the heart when someone achieves something.
Class: why does it happen?
Not liking someone. Held grudge. 'He should not deserve it.'
Comparison
It makes you feel bad about yourself. Threatened that someone is better.
Envy is an alarm
It shows that you still derive self-value from that thing.
Few core concepts
Self-value is one of three or four that make details easy.
Envy for hifz versus wealth
Envy of a hafiz shows value derived from deeds. Envy of wealth shows value from money, probably worse.
Envy is fueled by vanity and arrogance
When these disappear, most envy goes.
Imams and income
Imams should have a career. If you earn from being an imam, a new imam in town feels like a threat.
Next week
Think about any aspect of envy. Six or seven points to cover.

L.title: Hasad: Qabil and Habil, and the cure of jama'a
obj: Announce the upcoming Tazkiyah Pearls series, a reference summary of two years of material for newcomers
Restate the core definition of hasad: not wanting someone else to have something, separate from what you want for yourself
Show that value tags drive envy, using Abu Lahab as the example
Study Qabil and Habil as hasad over acceptance (qabool), not over dunya
Give the solution: the concept of jama'a, seeing everyone as one team
Show hasad as the reflection of vanity and arrogance, and set up contemplation for next week
topics: Tazkiyah Pearls series announced

A weekday series after Fajr in Ramadan summarising everything covered over two years. Meant as a reference point for newcomers who feel they are parachuting in. This halaqa stays slower, with time for questions and contemplation.
Recap: the definition of hasad
Hasad has nothing to do with what you want for yourself. It is only not wanting something for someone else. What you want depends on your value system and how much illusion you allowed in.
Hasad over dunya is low
Scholars see hasad over dunya as extremely low. Nothing in dunya is worth envying.
Audience example: physique
A student offers an example: someone who values working out can be bothered by a more built person. Envy comes from where you derive value.
Value tags
Everything has a weight you assigned subconsciously. The more value, the harder it is to see it in someone else's hands. Dunya should carry very low value.
Abu Lahab
He had every reason to believe, but wealth was his heaviest weight. Anything placed on the other scale lost, even the truth. Ask what value you assign to things and why.
Value only through Akhira
Something should be high value only if tied to Akhira. Hasad over dunya is petty and fixable even without religion. Hasad over Akhira is the real problem.
Quranic example: two sons of Adam
Qabil and Habil. The offering was accepted from one and rejected from the other. In their time acceptance was visible. The Quran frames it as acceptance, not a woman as older sources say.
Why Qabil wanted to kill
He could not take away Allah's acceptance of his brother, so the only act left was removing him. Habil replied that Allah accepts only from the mindful.
Why this story is dangerous
Today no one can know whose deed was accepted, so there is no analogy. The closest is seeing someone doing more deeds than you. In that position you would likely feel as Qabil did.
Audience: can we ever know?
Students think about whether any situation compares. Deeds are visible but acceptance is not.
Qabil's real problem
Not that he was rejected but that his brother was accepted. He did not care about getting it later, he did not want his brother to have it.
Solution: jama'a

Seeing the people beside you wearing the same jersey. Others' gains are a collective win. Maturity widens the team from sibling to friends, community, ummah and humanity, and the idea of an enemy dissolves.
Team player vs selfish player
The selfish player wants everyone else to be worse so he shines. A team player wants the best players on his team. Someone else achieving more is an advantage.
Hasad reflects vanity and arrogance
It is the outcome of deriving value from wrong sources. If it shows up, there is unfinished work on vanity and arrogance. The fix is a change of mentality.
How to contemplate it
Ask where the concept comes from and how it impacts you. For the solution, contemplate togetherness. Team sports teach it: a teammate's mistake gets encouragement, not cursing.
Audience pushback and the spark
A student says he does not feel envy without another reason to dislike the person. The teacher says for a moment a chest tightening is felt and good nature overrides it. Shaytan only needs the spark.
Less hasad is possible but not zero
Focusing on yourself, contentment and good values help. Learning the concept prepares you for when circumstances provoke it.
Priority: them or the team
You can dislike a teammate and still want the team to win. Start with family, since sibling envy is the worst, then widen the circle.
Audience: the two gardens story
A student raises the Quranic story of the two friends and the garden, where one said may Allah take it away. The teacher says it is a reminder, not envy.
Jama'a is vast
Our goal is that others join our side, not that they be enemies. Five or six more angles are promised for next week.
Hasad among the learned
If you do postdoc research you meet people with large heads and small chests. Hasad makes adults behave like toddlers going for the jugular.
Hasad is a force of nature
Recited every time at the end in the seeking of refuge from the envier when he envies. Understanding it and removing it is essential. Next week continues the topic.

L.title: Envy vs ghibta, Yusuf's brothers and the opposite of hasad
obj: Separate envy from healthy jealousy (ghira) and from ghibta, being inspired by what someone has
Study the second Quranic story of hasad, Yusuf and his brothers, and see that both stories are about attention and acceptance, not possessions
Break hasad into three types: dunya for dunya, dunya dressed as akhira, and akhira for akhira
Give two tools: keep asking why, and put the opposite of envy in front of it
Announce Ramadan planning for the coming weeks and two more sessions on hasad
topics: Envy vs jealousy
Healthy jealousy (ghira) protects spouse, integrity and loved ones and is not about not wanting someone to have something. It is not seen as a problem.
Ghibta: being inspired
Seeing what someone has and being inspired to work for it, with no joy in them losing it. The Prophet allowed it in two cases only.
The two categories worth being inspired by

Someone given wealth who spends it for Allah, and someone given knowledge or the Quran who teaches it and acts on it. The teacher reads this as two categories, not two items: dunya used for Allah, and akhira used for Allah.
Tazkiyah Pearls in Ramadan
A weekday series after Fajr. Attend whether you are old or new, use it as a reference, and go back to unclear lessons. About half recap and half new.
Second Quranic story: Yusuf and his brothers
Both stories of hasad are between siblings, one ending in murder and one in an attempt. The brothers wanted their father's attention.
Your attention is your most valuable asset
Not wealth. Be stingy about whom you give it to and in what dose. Too little breeds resentment, too much cheapens it.
Why the stories exist
They show the epitome of a problem. Iblis shows arrogance can refuse a direct command. Hasad starts as a small discomfort at someone's good fortune and can make a brother kill.
Neither killed over possessions
Qabil lost over Allah's acceptance of his brother. Yusuf's brothers lost over a father's attention. The thing envied was moral, not physical.
Three types of hasad
Dunya for dunya (petty, easy to drop). Dunya envy dressed in an akhira reason (most common). Akhira for akhira (the most subtle and hardest to clean).
The middle type
Someone does good for akhira but you envy the dunya gain: fame, popularity, status. This is the majority of hasad and how the heart is ruined.
Tool one: lecture your nefs
Sit your nefs in a corner and lecture it with what you know. A contemplation trick when you cannot think of angles.
Tool two: keep asking why
Why did it bother me, why does that matter, is there not enough of it? The answers are upsetting but they reach the root problem, not the symptom.
Tool three: the opposite of envy
Clarity comes from putting the opposite in front of a thing. A group discussion lands on being happy for them, and wanting them to increase.
Being happy even if you dislike them
You can be happy someone gets more dunya, since the pie is not small. If they are close to Allah you benefit, if you love them they do more khayr.
Compete with yourself
Do not compare to someone dealt different cards. Allah did not choose you for their role. In your 40s you will see peers ahead of you.
Why the opposite works in friendship
Being truly happy for friends, you sleep better and avoid eggshells. People will seek you out with their good news because genuine happiness is rare.
Hasad is deadly but easiest to fix
Qarun and Iblis killed no one, hasad led to murder. Yet it only needs a change of mentality: stop seeing what others have as something that affects you.
Two forms: envying and inducing envy
Enjoying making others envious is a separate illness, tied to arrogance. Notice how you feel about others and how they feel about you.
Stable self-value
Why the course began with self-value. Love for them what you love for yourself, and the why-question reveals what you crave: fame, wealth, status.
Ramadan planning
The next two weeks are on Ramadan as the prime season for tazkiyah. He has booked March 2026 off already. Two more sessions on hasad follow Eid.
Admit you have felt it
If you will not admit past envy you are Qabil and Iblis together. Envy is a normal human feeling and tazkiyah accepts normalcy, then learns to be genuinely happy.

L.title: Pre-Ramadan prep: sleep, schedule and i'tikaf
obj: Start pre-Ramadan prep: plan the month in advance and raise the bar each year
Set the bare minimum of Isha and Fajr in congregation for all 30 days, which means changing sleep habits
Work backwards from the schedule: sleep earlier, remove late-night slots, write down where your 24 hours go
Plan sleep, food and tarawih together, and use Ramadan's rigid schedule to drop bad habits
Add daily contemplation time modelled on the Prophet's i'tikaf, and choose two topics: sincerity and mortality
Assignment: write a schedule and a list of what you want out of the month
topics: Pre-Ramadan prep
Next week gets planning. Ramadan is the high season for anyone doing tazkiyah, where real changes are made and then held onto.
Plan the month ahead
Everyone gets something from Ramadan, but those who put the most in take the most out. Raise the bar every year, starting small and adding on.
Bare minimum: Isha and Fajr in jama'a
All 30 days and nights, unless physically on call. Even the Companions, working far away, made sure of Fajr and Isha. Pray at the nearest masjid if it is not this one.
Work backwards from sleep
To wake earlier you must sleep earlier, which means removing evening activities and moving them earlier. Write down where your 24 hours go.
Zone in, Eid will wait
Give up late gatherings for the month. Friends and fun will be there after Eid. Doing it once changes the taste of the month.
Residents and call
On-call days are exceptions. He used to leave the hospital to give the talk and return. He missed only one Fajr in three years, because of a patient's family death.
Sunnah, Quran, wird and full tarawih
Pray the sunnah, listen to the imam, do your wird. Stay for the full tarawih until the end, not a shortened version.
Suhoor and two rak'at of witr
Wake 5 to 6 minutes earlier. The myth that you cannot pray after witr is wrong. Witr is best last, with the imam if possible.
Sleep is biology
You cannot sleep at midnight and wake at 5 for weeks. If you have no midday nap, you need night sleep. Expect to be wrecked at the end, and sleep it off after Eid.
Take time off for worship
Take leave in Ramadan, not only for Eid vacations. The aim is ta'abbud.
Contemplation and the Prophet's i'tikaf
He did i'tikaf all year. A curtain in the masjid gave him solitude to think. Spend 3 or 4 hours in the masjid in the last nights, praying and reading, and a gap appears for reflection.
Tazkiyah Pearls in Ramadan
Weekday talks after Fajr, a reference for anyone joining later.
Why sleep is the key piece
Sleep management is the most important piece. Even on tahajjud nights, take what you can.
One extra hour matters
Without enough sleep you crash in days and lose Fajr and Isha for a full day. This year's earlier schedule helps. Book time off for the last ten nights.
Big changes remove bad habits
Large changes are good for getting rid of bad habits, not for building small good ones. Ramadan's rigid schedule can remove gaming, screens and late nights.
Eat less, sleep less
A light iftar, tarawih, then mostly one meal. Less food means less sleep needed, so five to six hours is possible versus eight and a half if you overeat.
Daily i'tikaf time
Our masjid cannot host 24-hour i'tikaf. Make an intention for the time you are there, focused on ibadah and not chatting.
Contemplation topics: sincerity and mortality
Ikhlas and its opposite riya, plus mortality, which they failed to reflect on this year. Ramadan is the time to try.
Reasonable plan, remove one habit
Turn off the console or similar for 30 days. Keep the plan realistic or it will crash in the first days.
Assignment
1. Schedule and sleep plan. 2. What you want to walk away with from the month. Write both down.

L.title: Ramadan domains: sleep, Quran, contemplation and the fast
obj: Review the schedules the group drafted and stress the sleep piece, where most people fail
Make the case for sleeping early: biphasic sleep before electricity, and early night sleep being worth more
Lay out the domains for Ramadan: Quran, salah, du'a, wird, contemplation, an act of khayr daily, and planning
Set objectives so you do not fade by the end of week one or around the middle of the month
Put siyam first: fast from distractions and from the dunya, so that you can focus on the heart
Answer practical questions on volunteering and praying jama'a at home
topics: Low attendance and plan for next term
Most skipped because they think they do not need Ramadan prep. A new time slot for next semester is under consideration.
Fajr daily in jama'a from next Saturday
30 days straight, at the nearest masjid if far away. Sit for the talk after Fajr, or have a daily source of knowledge. After Fajr is a prime hour for contemplation.
Check-in on schedules
Group members share their drafted plans. A key point: if you sleep at 12:30 the day is already ruined.
Sleeping early has baraka
His story from Syria: sleeping by 10 without electricity, waking at 5 with no alarm. Not always possible for a physician, but worth building a phase of life around.
Biphasic sleep before electricity
People slept at 9 or 9:30, woke around 1 to eat and work, then slept again. Qiyam al-layl fits this pattern.
Early sleep is worth more
He says sleeping the first four hours of the night equals about six and a half hours in the day. You do not need nine hours.
Benefits of sleeping early in Ramadan
Easier suhoor, a little tahajjud, and an hour and a half between Isha/tarawih and sleep is used to sleep right away.
Naps and group discussion
Steal a half hour or hour: a desk nap at lunch, a nap after school at 3 or 3:30. Group members share their end-of-day times.
Why most people fail
The first week looks full, then attendance disappears for 10 days. They did something unsustainable, did not sleep, crashed and could not return.
Domain 1: Quran
The whole month exists because the Quran was revealed in it, which is why Laylat al-Qadr has status. The Salaf set other knowledge aside. Plan daily recitation and contemplation.
Domain 2: Salah
Fajr and Isha in jama'a nightly. If forced to choose between tarawih and Fajr, always choose Fajr. Stay with the imam until the end for the full night's reward. Keep the other fara'id well too.
Domain 3: Du'a
Learn the etiquette of du'a. Beginners are forgiven for their lack of it, with time you should learn how to speak to Allah. The Prophet's du'as in the Quran are the model.
Domain 4: Wird
Keep a Hizb of Quran daily, such as one after Fajr and one after Asr. Use Ramadan to get ahead and add on.
Domain 5: Daily contemplation
10 to 15 minutes. After Asr in Ramadan is perfect since the body slows down. Keep a list of topics, and cross each off when done. You may doze off once or twice.
Domain 6: An act of khayr daily
Silat al-rahim, birr, sadaqah, calling a great aunt, volunteering. One every day.
Domain 7: Planning
Use Ramadan to plan where your life is going. Muslims are not good planners. The act of planning is itself worship, even if the plan will change.
Set objectives
Without goals Shaytan wins within seven days. Attendance dips toward the middle of the month then climbs again on the odd nights.
Siyam is the most important act
Fast from food and drink, and from haram, doubtful things and distractions. Delete from your phone and choose your company so the fast is pure. Losing your temper or road rage ruins it.
Fasting from the dunya
Allah takes away the basics of dunya, food and intimacy, so you stop being distracted and focus on the qalb.
Volunteering
You get the reward of both worship and service. Keep a rotation, not volunteering every night and skipping worship.
Praying maghrib and jama'a at home
Home jama'a with family is fine. In Canada the masjid is far, so there is no need to fill it at Maghrib. Priority is Fajr and Isha at the masjid.

EX.title: The daily wird for 15 straight days
EX.instr: Twice a day, planned around weekends and travel. Alone, count it. In session follow the leader and do not worry about your own count.

uses.instr: Keep the wird twice a day, once in session, without a break. Tell him once you reach 15 days. Then more is added.
usual: Skipping days and postponing it, which is why it is restarted from today.
should: Treat it as proof of discipline and character: it only takes about 15 minutes.
Do it in dead time such as commuting or standing in line.
Do not rush to feel transformed. The point is to establish the habit first.

uses.instr: Twice a day, early and late. Miss one, make it up. Miss two in a row, reset.
usual: Weekends and travel break the routine, which is why you reset instead of quitting.
should: Keep it small and consistent, the most beloved acts are the consistent ones.
See it as a show of love, since it is not mandatory.

uses.instr: Do it in a focused setting every 2 or 3 days and keep the streak rules: miss one, make up, miss two, reset.
feel: In session you feel urgent: I want this over, this is a waste of time, I hate being made to do this.
usual: Weekdays are chaos and weekends differ, so one of them breaks.
should: Drop the urgency and let it settle, absorb it.
Treat it as a daily dose of invocation, Quran and dua that holds even on a chaotic day.

uses.instr: Twice a day, planned around weekends and travel. Alone, count it. In session follow the leader and do not worry about your own count.
feel: Fidgety after a few minutes.
An itch to leave and get on to the next thing, the nafs wants out of its cage.
Weekends are harder than weekdays.
usual: Doing both sets at once late at night.
Trying to rush through it.
should: Find your attention span and extend it slowly.
Calm your heart rate first, then start.
Treat it as a daily dose of calm and honest dua.

uses.instr: Sit and do it once or twice a week in a quiet setting. The rest can be done on the run.
feel: Feeling like you are wasting time.
Wanting to rush because it is not dead time anymore.
should: Keep the tongue going even if the heart is not there.
Notice why it feels different sitting versus on the run.

EX.title: Contemplation: am I a servant of Allah?
EX.instr: Through the week, ask yourself how often you evaluate your service to Allah and whether your life actually shows it. Do not research it, just reflect.

uses.instr: Through the week, ask yourself how often you evaluate your service to Allah and whether your life actually shows it. Do not research it, just reflect.
feel: The nafs pushes back: servant of what, servant of me.
usual: Saying it as an abstract line the sheikh repeats while not feeling or living it.
should: Over time you notice you follow your whims and desires.
Clarity about who you are brings serenity and tranquility.

EX.title: Pause before salah
EX.instr: Before each salah, stop for about 15 seconds. Cut off your train of thought, breathe, centralize, and think about the salah itself. If your mind is full, write a note on your phone to put the thoughts away first.

uses.instr: Before each salah, stop for about 15 seconds. Cut off your train of thought, breathe, centralize, and think about the salah itself. If your mind is full, write a note on your phone to put the thoughts away first.
feel: Preoccupied or stressed, thinking about four things at once.
Unsure what to think about during the pause.
usual: Rushing through it like a world record, especially when praying alone.
should: Enter the salah more focused, in the zone.
Find your own thing that works, there is no single answer. He deliberately gives no example.

uses.instr: Keep pausing before salah to cut off your train of thought. No new weekly addition this week.
should: Stick with it. He will not give something new every week.

uses.instr: Keep pausing before salah.
feel: It worked for the first two times, then old habits returned.
should: Noticing is the beginning. It is not meant to make you feel bad.
The pause breaks the thought chain and later makes salah a break you look forward to.

uses.instr: Before salah stop the thought process and centralize. While reciting al-Fatiha reflect on one theme. In ruku' think of exalting Allah.
feel: Mind still running with the day.
Boredom in ruku' if you only say words.
Possible joy once the theme is meaningful.
should: A small silence before takbir.
Feeling Allah is above comparison and you are not entitled to question Him.
Contentment with His decrees.

uses.instr: Give three to ten seconds before takbir to centralize, then think about one theme or dua in Al-Fatiha while reciting.
feel: Awkward and hard to stop a thought.
Mind racing at 100 miles an hour.
Calmer once you breathe.
usual: Walking into prayer with the same thought running.
Reciting Fatiha with nothing in the mind.
Lowered heart rate after a pause.
should: Feel like salah is a time out from dunya.
Feel closer to Allah in a few moments of serenity.
Eventually pause less as it becomes natural.
answers: A student asked about contemplating while the imam recites. He said contemplation is not recitation, you can hold one thought and rejoin.

uses.instr: Pause before takbir, contemplate one Fatiha point, and in ruku' think about Allah as the Exalted.
feel: Overwhelmed in the second rak'ah.
Forgetting to pause.
Brain running away after takbir.
usual: Closing eyes helps some.
Running a verse in the mind before the pause.
Pausing after takbir instead of before.
should: Feel you are entering a different realm like ihram.
Feel like you are facing the Lord of all.
In ruku' feel that Allah is exalted and unquestioned while you are the servant.
answers: A student closes his eyes and was told that is acceptable if it helps focus.
A student primes with a verse before pausing.
A student does the pause after takbir and was corrected to do it before.

EX.title: Fix the intention before you act
EX.instr: Before an act, especially a group act, take a second and ask why you are doing it. Practice saying it to Allah in your own words.

uses.instr: Before an act, especially a group act, take a second and ask why you are doing it. Practice saying it to Allah in your own words.
feel: Scared that you have never perfected an intention.
Tempted to ask for a ruling so you do not have to do the work: the nafs wants less work and a different answer.
It is hard, like opening a door on a trashed room.
usual: You stand because everyone stands.
The honest reason is to be seen, to please a friend, or just habit, a mix of reasons.
should: Aim to improve it, not perfect it.
Acknowledge it honestly: acknowledging a bad intention is half the work.
Ask Allah to purify it, since He is the one who grants it.
Over time the right reason becomes second nature, if you keep regenerating it.
answers: Group answer: say Ya Rabbi, forgive me, this is for You, and be thankful for friends who reminded you.
Student answer: stack several intentions for money such as providing for family and not begging.
Student answer: sport as using the body as an amanah, and leisure for energy.

EX.title: Turn the four ideas into values
EX.instr: Name what feeds your sense of value (wealth, utility, status, health, reputation, friends, accomplishment). Ask whether it should, and where the constant source is.

uses.instr: Contemplate ubudiyyah, qabul, niyyah and ihsan every day until they are second nature. Notice your own values from your habits, and where they came from.
feel: Overwhelmed. He says do not be, it is step by step.
Confusion about how to have a relationship with an unseen Allah: this is the expected first feeling.
usual: Knowing something as a fact, like death, without it being real to you.
Wanting the thought to be a value while it just sits in line.
should: Ask yourself the four questions at the right frequencies, until you respond to them without reminding yourself.
Let it bring humility and focus, and stop you drifting.

uses.instr: Open the cellar and find what you derive your value from (grades, others' approval, purpose, wealth). Ask if it is stable.
feel: Surprise at what you actually derive value from.
Sinking feelings on bad days when a tube drains you.
Possible relief that your value is fixed.
usual: Value from grades, pleasing others, achievements or brands.
A fragile sense of self that swings with each day.
Seeing yourself as more or less valuable than others.
should: Feel secure that your value is constant and given by Allah.
Keep accountability for behavior without linking it to your worth.
Feel confident and humble together.
answers: Students said value comes from purpose, from satisfying others or from grades.
One said identity as a Muslim.
One said it must be constant or things shift.
One pointed to faith and accepting the test.

uses.instr: Name what feeds your sense of value (wealth, utility, status, health, reputation, friends, accomplishment). Ask whether it should, and where the constant source is.
feel: Strange and unsettled as sources are pulled away. 'I don't know how to feel anymore'.
Pain when untangling relative value from innate value.
Defensiveness when told value is not earned.
usual: Feeling good with money and bad when it drops.
Sizing up strangers within five seconds.
Rage and self-attack after losing at a game or sport.
Hurt by feedback at work or in training.
should: Calm: value is divine and no praise or insult changes it.
Equal to others, neither arrogant nor lowly.
Take feedback as room to grow without it touching who you are.
Motivated by pleasing Allah, not by proving worth.
answers: Class listed wealth, utility, social status, health, accomplishments, reputation and friends.
Example from the teacher: his value to an NBA team is minus a million but his innate value is the same.

uses.instr: Look at how you see yourself in success. Move the spotlight from 'I did it' to Allah, and see your effort as a tiny share.
feel: Pride and entitlement when you succeed.
